sec10-card-sec10-F011.front: Which three elevated or tunnel-like highway structures prohibit unattended parking?
sec10-card-sec10-F011.expected_back: A bridge, elevated roadway structure or highway underpass is not an allowed location for unattended parking.

sec10-card-sec10-F012.front: Is parking alongside another vehicle already stopped or parked at the curb allowed?
sec10-card-sec10-F012.expected_back: Do not double-park beside a vehicle stopped or parked at the curb or roadway edge.

sec10-card-sec10-F013.front: When must you avoid parking near a street work crew or roadway obstruction?
sec10-card-sec10-F013.expected_back: Do not park alongside an obstruction when doing so would worsen congestion.

sec10-card-sec10-F014.front: May you leave your vehicle parked along a curb posted with signs prohibiting stopping?
sec10-card-sec10-F014.expected_back: Do not leave a vehicle parked where traffic signs prohibit stopping.

sec10-card-sec10-F015.front: Outside business and residential districts, where must you position your vehicle to park?
sec10-card-sec10-F015.expected_back: Outside residential and business districts, park entirely off the roadway.

sec10-card-sec10-F016.front: When parking beside a highway, how many feet of clear roadway width should remain for passing traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-F016.expected_back: When parking along a highway, leave at least twenty feet for traffic to pass if possible.

sec10-card-sec10-F017.front: From at least what distance in both directions should a highway-parked vehicle be clearly visible?
sec10-card-sec10-F017.expected_back: A vehicle parked along a highway should be visible from at least two hundred feet in either direction.

sec10-card-sec10-F018.front: Which lights must stay on if your vehicle is parked beside a highway after dark?
sec10-card-sec10-F018.expected_back: At night, leave the highway-parked vehicle’s parking lights or emergency flashers illuminated.

sec10-card-sec10-F019.front: How close to the curb must your right-side tires finish when parallel parked?
sec10-card-sec10-F019.expected_back: When parallel parked, position the tires no farther than twelve inches from the curb.

sec10-card-sec10-F020.front: How should you handle opening street-side doors versus unloading passengers or cargo?
sec10-card-sec10-F020.expected_back: Take special care when leaving a vehicle on its street side, and unload from the curb side.

sec10-card-sec10-F021.front: What three setup actions begin a clean parallel-parking maneuver?
sec10-card-sec10-F021.expected_back: Begin parallel parking by choosing a space large enough, signaling and stopping beside the vehicle ahead of the space.

sec10-card-sec10-F022.front: Once traffic clears, how do you steer while backing in—and what alignment landmark cues your wheel flip?
sec10-card-sec10-F022.expected_back: After checking for conflicting traffic, steer sharply right and reverse slowly toward the curb until the front tire aligns with the forward vehicle’s rear bumper.

sec10-card-sec10-F023.front: After your front tire aligns with the forward car's rear bumper, how do you steer while backing?
sec10-card-sec10-F023.expected_back: Then steer sharply left and continue reversing without hitting the vehicle behind.

sec10-card-sec10-F024.front: How do you straighten and position your vehicle to finish parallel parking?
sec10-card-sec10-F024.expected_back: Finish parallel parking by moving forward into the space’s center, leaving room at both ends and aligning close to the curb.

sec10-card-sec10-F025.front: Who holds right-of-way when a parked driver pulls out into traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-F025.expected_back: A driver leaving a parking space has no priority over traffic or pedestrians and must wait for a clear path.

sec10-card-sec10-F026.front: Which two safety steps come right before pulling out of a parallel-parking space?
sec10-card-sec10-F026.expected_back: Before leaving parallel parking, look over the shoulder and signal before entering the travel lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F027.front: How should you reverse out of an angled or perpendicular parking stall?
sec10-card-sec10-F027.expected_back: When backing from an angled or straight-in space, wait for a clear area behind and keep looking backward.

sec10-card-sec10-F028.front: Why must you look over your shoulder while reversing instead of relying on mirrors alone?
sec10-card-sec10-F028.expected_back: While reversing, look over the shoulder rather than depending solely on the rearview mirror.

sec10-card-sec10-F029.front: Which way do you turn your front wheels when parking downhill—with or without a curb?
sec10-card-sec10-F029.expected_back: For downhill parking, turn the wheels sharply right whether or not a curb is present.

sec10-card-sec10-F030.front: Which direction do you turn your front wheels when parking uphill with no curb?
sec10-card-sec10-F030.expected_back: When parking uphill without a curb, turn the wheels sharply right.

sec10-card-sec10-F031.front: Which hill-parking scenario is the lone case where you turn your front wheels sharply left?
sec10-card-sec10-F031.expected_back: When parking uphill beside a curb, turn the wheels sharply left.

sec10-card-sec10-F032.front: How must your driving adjust once darkness cuts forward visibility?
sec10-card-sec10-F032.expected_back: Reduced nighttime visibility calls for a lower speed and greater caution.

sec10-card-sec10-F033.front: What rule links your nighttime speed directly to your headlight beam reach?
sec10-card-sec10-F033.expected_back: Do not drive faster at night than a speed allowing a stop within the distance illuminated ahead.

sec10-card-sec10-F034.front: What two actions protect your eyes and lane position when dazzling headlights approach?
sec10-card-sec10-F034.expected_back: When approaching dazzling headlights, dim your own lights and direct your gaze toward the roadway’s right side.

sec10-card-sec10-F035.front: Where in your lane should you position when an oncoming vehicle shows only one working headlight?
sec10-card-sec10-F035.expected_back: If an approaching vehicle has only one working headlight, remain toward the far-right side of your lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F036.front: Why should you never wear sunglasses or dark lenses against glare at night or on gloomy days?
sec10-card-sec10-F036.expected_back: Dark glasses do not solve glare at night or on dark days, because they further reduce vision.

sec10-card-sec10-F037.front: Within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle must you switch from high beams to low beams?
sec10-card-sec10-F037.expected_back: Use low beams within five hundred feet of an oncoming vehicle.

sec10-card-sec10-F038.front: Within how many feet behind a lead vehicle must you switch to low beams?
sec10-card-sec10-F038.expected_back: Use low beams when following another vehicle within five hundred feet.

sec10-card-sec10-F039.front: During what clock period and visibility threshold must your headlights be on?
sec10-card-sec10-F039.expected_back: Use lights from sunset to sunrise and whenever visibility ahead is less than five hundred feet.

sec10-card-sec10-F040.front: May you drive using parking lights instead of full headlights at dusk or in poor visibility?
sec10-card-sec10-F040.expected_back: Use headlights when lighting is needed rather than driving with parking lights alone.

sec10-card-sec10-F041.front: Where do high beams belong, and how should your night speed still compare to daytime?
sec10-card-sec10-F041.expected_back: Reserve high beams for open-country driving without nearby vehicles, and still drive slower than in daylight.

sec10-card-sec10-F042.front: Which three driving environments call for low beams rather than high beams?
sec10-card-sec10-F042.expected_back: Use low beams on lit streets, when following another vehicle and in fog during daylight or darkness.

sec10-card-sec10-F043.front: What happens to your forward visibility if you flick on high beams in fog?
sec10-card-sec10-F043.expected_back: High beams reduce the driver’s visibility in fog.

sec11-card-sec11-F001.front: Which seating rows must wear properly fastened safety belts under Mississippi's handbook?
sec11-card-sec11-F001.expected_back: The handbook requires drivers and passengers in both front and rear seats to use properly fastened safety belts.

sec11-card-sec11-F002.front: When and where does Mississippi's passenger-vehicle seat-belt requirement apply?
sec11-card-sec11-F002.expected_back: The seat-belt rule applies when a passenger vehicle moves forward on a public street, road or highway in Mississippi.

sec11-card-sec11-F003.front: How must a child younger than age four ride in a vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F003.expected_back: A child younger than four must be properly secured in a child-restraint seat meeting the applicable safety standard.

sec11-card-sec11-F004.front: When does a child age four through six legally require an approved belt-positioning booster seat?
sec11-card-sec11-F004.expected_back: A child aged four through six needs an approved belt-positioning booster when shorter than four feet nine inches or lighter than sixty-five pounds.

sec11-card-sec11-F005.front: What legal penalty can hit violations of Mississippi's seat-belt or child-restraint laws?
sec11-card-sec11-F005.expected_back: Violations of Mississippi’s seat-belt or child-restraint requirements can result in a fine.

sec11-card-sec11-F006.front: Below what age does Mississippi's handbook recommend keeping children in a rear seat?
sec11-card-sec11-F006.expected_back: The handbook recommends that children younger than thirteen ride in a rear seat.

sec11-card-sec11-F007.front: How long does the American Academy of Pediatrics guidance in the handbook keep a child rear-facing?
sec11-card-sec11-F007.expected_back: The handbook attributes to the American Academy of Pediatrics a recommendation to keep a child rear-facing until reaching the convertible seat’s maximum permitted height or weight.

sec11-card-sec11-F008.front: Apart from the legal age rule, across what weight range does the handbook recommend using a booster seat?
sec11-card-sec11-F008.expected_back: Separately from its legal age-based rule, the handbook recommends a motor-vehicle booster for children weighing forty to sixty-five pounds.

sec11-card-sec11-F009.front: Why must you drop speed right when rain starts falling?
sec11-card-sec11-F009.expected_back: Reduce speed as rain begins because water mixes with accumulated dirt and grease to create a slippery road film.

sec11-card-sec11-F010.front: Why must you slow down whenever standing water covers the road?
sec11-card-sec11-F010.expected_back: Slow down whenever water covers the road, because speed can cause loss of traction and hydroplaning.

sec11-card-sec11-F011.front: What actually happens beneath your steering tires during hydroplaning?
sec11-card-sec11-F011.expected_back: Hydroplaning occurs when the steering tires ride on pooled water instead of maintaining road contact.

sec11-card-sec11-F012.front: How do you prevent hydroplaning during rainstorms and near puddles?
sec11-card-sec11-F012.expected_back: Avoid hydroplaning by reducing speed in rain and around standing water or puddles.

sec11-card-sec11-F013.front: What must you do when facing a flooded roadway or deep pool of standing water?
sec11-card-sec11-F013.expected_back: Do not cross a flooded road or a large pool of standing water; choose another route.

sec11-card-sec11-F014.front: Why avoid sudden braking in a skid, and what manual-transmission pedal must you leave alone?
sec11-card-sec11-F014.expected_back: Sudden braking can worsen a skid, and the handbook says not to use the clutch while trying to control the skid.

sec11-card-sec11-F015.front: What are your first two pedal rules the instant a tire goes flat or blows out?
sec11-card-sec11-F015.expected_back: For a flat tire or blowout, release the accelerator and avoid abruptly applying the brakes.

sec11-card-sec11-F016.front: Once steady after a blowout, how should you brake—or stop when plenty of clear road lies ahead?
sec11-card-sec11-F016.expected_back: After a blowout, brake gradually and carefully; if there is ample distance, allow the vehicle to stop without braking.

sec11-card-sec11-F017.front: How should you use your brakes if your wheels drop off the paved roadway edge?
sec11-card-sec11-F017.expected_back: If the vehicle leaves the pavement, use the brakes gently before returning to the roadway.

sec11-card-sec11-F018.front: Where should you move a disabled vehicle whenever possible?
sec11-card-sec11-F018.expected_back: Move a disabled vehicle onto the far-right shoulder.

sec11-card-sec11-F019.front: If forced to walk for help, which side of a regular highway do you use, and what interstate rule applies?
sec11-card-sec11-F019.expected_back: If walking for help becomes necessary, walk on the highway’s left side facing traffic, cross highways with great care and never cross an interstate.

sec11-card-sec11-F020.front: What three immediate steps follow involvement in a crash with injuries?
sec11-card-sec11-F020.expected_back: After a crash, stop promptly and assist injured people, calling nine-one-one when injuries require reporting.

sec11-card-sec11-F021.front: What human harm in a traffic crash triggers a prompt report to law enforcement?
sec11-card-sec11-F021.expected_back: Report a crash promptly to law enforcement when it involves injury or death.

sec11-card-sec11-F022.front: Above what apparent dollar amount of property damage does Mississippi's handbook require reporting a crash?
sec11-card-sec11-F022.expected_back: The handbook expressly requires reporting apparent crash damage exceeding five hundred dollars.

sec11-card-sec11-F023.front: Which four pieces of information must crash participants exchange with one another?
sec11-card-sec11-F023.expected_back: Exchange your name, address, plate number and insurance information with the other crash participants and obtain the same details from them.

sec11-card-sec11-F024.front: What coverage details must you show the investigating officer at a crash scene?
sec11-card-sec11-F024.expected_back: At a crash scene, show the responding officer insurance evidence and the policy number.

sec11-card-sec11-F025.front: Can an uninsured driver still get ticketed after a crash caused entirely by someone else?
sec11-card-sec11-F025.expected_back: A driver without proof of insurance may be cited even when that driver did not cause the crash.

sec11-card-sec11-F026.front: Who may file the immediate crash report if injuries keep the driver from doing so?
sec11-card-sec11-F026.expected_back: If injuries prevent the driver from making an immediate crash report, a passenger may report it.

sec11-card-sec11-F027.front: How does Mississippi's handbook classify the privacy status of crash reports?
sec11-card-sec11-F027.expected_back: The handbook says crash reports are confidential.

sec11-card-sec11-F028.front: What toll-free mobile keypad code connects directly to Mississippi Highway Patrol dispatch in a real highway emergency?
sec11-card-sec11-F028.expected_back: For a genuine highway emergency in Mississippi, dialing star four seven on a mobile phone connects toll-free to Highway Patrol dispatch.

sec11-card-sec11-F029.front: What location info do you give Highway Patrol dispatch, and when is that hotkey allowed?
sec11-card-sec11-F029.expected_back: Give the Highway Patrol dispatcher the emergency details and the highway location or mile marker; use that emergency number only for actual emergencies.

sec11-card-sec11-F030.front: Which emergency vehicles and active warning signals claim immediate right-of-way?
sec11-card-sec11-F030.expected_back: An ambulance, fire engine or police vehicle using red or blue emergency lights, a bell or a siren has right of way.

sec11-card-sec11-F031.front: Where should you move and wait when an active emergency vehicle approaches?
sec11-card-sec11-F031.expected_back: When possible, move to the far-right shoulder and wait for an approaching emergency vehicle to pass.

sec11-card-sec11-F032.front: What should you do if you are already inside an intersection when an emergency siren approaches?
sec11-card-sec11-F032.expected_back: If already in an intersection when yielding to an emergency vehicle, clear the intersection before pulling right.

sec11-card-sec11-F033.front: On a four-lane highway, how must you respond to a roadside emergency vehicle flashing lights or sounding a siren?
sec11-card-sec11-F033.expected_back: On a four-lane highway, move away from a roadside emergency vehicle displaying lights or a siren by merging into the adjacent lane when safe.

sec11-card-sec11-F034.front: What is your backup duty if heavy traffic makes merging away from a roadside emergency vehicle unsafe?
sec11-card-sec11-F034.expected_back: If moving over for a roadside emergency vehicle is unsafe, reduce speed and be ready to stop.

sec11-card-sec11-F035.front: How should you pull over when a law-enforcement officer signals a traffic stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F035.expected_back: When an officer signals a traffic stop, stay calm, signal and pull off or beside the road as soon as it is safe.

sec11-card-sec11-F036.front: Once stopped for an officer, what should you turn off—and should you step out?
sec11-card-sec11-F036.expected_back: During a traffic stop, turn off the engine and audio equipment and remain in the vehicle unless told to exit.

sec11-card-sec11-F037.front: What interior switch should you turn on during a nighttime traffic stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F037.expected_back: At a nighttime traffic stop, turn on the cabin light to improve visibility.

sec11-card-sec11-F038.front: Where should your hands rest while speaking with an officer during a traffic stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F038.expected_back: Keep your hands visible on the wheel or another clearly observable location and follow the officer’s instructions.

sec11-card-sec11-F039.front: Why might you lower the passenger window instead of the driver window at a traffic stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F039.expected_back: An officer may approach either side of the stopped vehicle, so lower the window on that side for communication.

sec11-card-sec11-F040.front: What must you tell the officer right away if a weapon is inside the vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F040.expected_back: Tell the officer immediately if a weapon is in the vehicle.

sec11-card-sec11-F041.front: When should you reach into a pocket, console, or glovebox for your license and papers?
sec11-card-sec11-F041.expected_back: Wait for instructions before reaching for your license or vehicle papers.

sec11-card-sec11-F042.front: Which three documents do officers typically ask to inspect at a traffic stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F042.expected_back: The officer typically asks for the driver’s license, insurance evidence and vehicle registration.

sec11-card-sec11-F043.front: What should you do if requested papers sit out of reach in a backpack or trunk?
sec11-card-sec11-F043.expected_back: If requested documents are out of reach, explain their location and wait for acknowledgment before retrieving them.

sec11-card-sec11-F044.front: What identification should an officer out of uniform display, and what if they don't?
sec11-card-sec11-F044.expected_back: An officer not in uniform should show law-enforcement credentials, and you may request them if they are not shown.

sec11-card-sec11-F045.front: If an officer instructs you to step out of your vehicle, how should you exit and stand?
sec11-card-sec11-F045.expected_back: If told to leave the vehicle, keep your hands visible and stand where the officer directs.

sec11-card-sec11-F046.front: Which three enforcement outcomes can end a traffic stop, and what question may you ask?
sec11-card-sec11-F046.expected_back: A traffic stop may end in a warning, a ticket or an arrest, and you may ask the officer to explain the action taken.

sec11-card-sec11-F047.front: Where should you contest a ticket instead of arguing on the roadside?
sec11-card-sec11-F047.expected_back: Ask for clarification respectfully and use established court procedures to challenge a decision rather than prolonging the stop through argument.

sec11-card-sec11-F048.front: Does signing and accepting a traffic citation mean you are pleading guilty?
sec11-card-sec11-F048.expected_back: Signing and accepting a traffic ticket does not admit guilt.

sec11-card-sec11-F049.front: How should you follow up if you have concerns about an officer's conduct during a stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F049.expected_back: If concerned about an officer’s conduct, contact the agency and ask for a supervisor as soon as practical after the stop.

sec12-card-sec12-F001.front: What speed rule governs your approach along an interstate entrance ramp?
sec12-card-sec12-F001.expected_back: Obey the entry ramp’s posted speed while approaching an interstate.

sec12-card-sec12-F002.front: What is the exact purpose of an interstate acceleration lane before merging?
sec12-card-sec12-F002.expected_back: Use the acceleration lane to bring the vehicle’s speed into line with interstate traffic before merging.

sec12-card-sec12-F003.front: Why avoid merging onto an interstate far faster or slower than surrounding traffic?
sec12-card-sec12-F003.expected_back: Merging much faster or slower than the traffic stream is dangerous.

sec12-card-sec12-F004.front: Who holds right-of-way at an interstate on-ramp, and how should you blend into traffic?
sec12-card-sec12-F004.expected_back: Yield to approaching interstate vehicles, signal and merge gradually rather than swerving into the traffic flow.

sec12-card-sec12-F005.front: What small step finishes every interstate merge?
sec12-card-sec12-F005.expected_back: Cancel the turn signal once the merge is complete.

sec12-card-sec12-F006.front: At least how far ahead of your interstate exit should you already sit in the exit lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F006.expected_back: Be in the appropriate exit lane at least one-quarter mile before the exit.

sec12-card-sec12-F007.front: Why must you read overhead exit signs carefully even though most ramps leave on the right?
sec12-card-sec12-F007.expected_back: Most interstate exits leave from the right lane, but some leave from the left, so read the exit signs.

sec12-card-sec12-F008.front: Which three steps take you cleanly off the main freeway into the deceleration lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F008.expected_back: Before exiting, check beside and behind the vehicle, signal and enter the deceleration lane.

sec12-card-sec12-F009.front: When should you begin slowing down for an interstate exit, and what follows inside the ramp lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F009.expected_back: Wait until inside the deceleration lane before slowing, then reduce speed to its posted limit and cancel the signal.

sec12-card-sec12-F010.front: What must you do if you accidentally peel onto the wrong interstate exit ramp?
sec12-card-sec12-F010.expected_back: If you use the wrong exit, continue down the ramp rather than stopping or reversing.

sec12-card-sec12-F011.front: What is the only safe and legal response if you drive past your intended interstate exit?
sec12-card-sec12-F011.expected_back: If you miss an exit, continue to the next one instead of stopping and backing up.

sec12-card-sec12-F012.front: Which three maneuvers are strictly forbidden on any interstate exit ramp?
sec12-card-sec12-F012.expected_back: Never stop, reverse or turn around on an exit ramp.

sec12-card-sec12-F013.front: How do the right lane and left lane divide duties on a standard interstate?
sec12-card-sec12-F013.expected_back: The interstate’s right lane is intended for through travel and its left lane for overtaking.

sec12-card-sec12-F014.front: On a multilane interstate, on which sides is overtaking permitted?
sec12-card-sec12-F014.expected_back: Passing on either side is allowed on the interstate.

sec12-card-sec12-F015.front: Which lane belongs to drivers traveling slower than surrounding interstate traffic?
sec12-card-sec12-F015.expected_back: Keep right when traveling slower than surrounding traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F016.front: How must you manage speed while another interstate driver is overtaking you?
sec12-card-sec12-F016.expected_back: Do not increase speed when another driver is passing you.

sec12-card-sec12-F017.front: Why avoid lingering side-by-side next to a vehicle you are overtaking on the interstate?
sec12-card-sec12-F017.expected_back: When overtaking, avoid remaining alongside the other vehicle longer than needed to pass.

sec12-card-sec12-F018.front: How does the handbook rate cruising inside another vehicle's blind spot?
sec12-card-sec12-F018.expected_back: Driving in another vehicle’s blind spot is dangerous.

sec12-card-sec12-F019.front: When cruising in the right interstate lane near an on-ramp, how can you help entering traffic?
sec12-card-sec12-F019.expected_back: From the right lane, watch for entering vehicles and move left to provide room when it is safe.

sec12-card-sec12-F020.front: Which two checks must precede every interstate lane change?
sec12-card-sec12-F020.expected_back: Before changing lanes, inspect both mirrors and the blind spot for traffic beside and behind you.

sec12-card-sec12-F021.front: Once mirrors and blind spots check clear, what three steps complete a lane change?
sec12-card-sec12-F021.expected_back: Signal the lane change, move only when safe and cancel the signal afterward.

sec12-card-sec12-F022.front: What checking and signaling routine applies when moving back into your original lane after passing?
sec12-card-sec12-F022.expected_back: Use the same checking and signaling procedure when returning to the previous lane.

sec12-card-sec12-F023.front: What interstate maximum speed does the handbook give for both daylight and darkness—and what qualifies it?
sec12-card-sec12-F023.expected_back: The handbook gives seventy miles per hour as the interstate limit in daylight and darkness, subject to conditions and posted restrictions.

sec12-card-sec12-F024.front: What two speed boundaries govern interstate driving alongside the maximum limit?
sec12-card-sec12-F024.expected_back: Adjust interstate speed to road and weather conditions and observe the posted minimum.

sec12-card-sec12-F025.front: At least how many car lengths of following space does the handbook specify at seventy versus fifty miles per hour?
sec12-card-sec12-F025.expected_back: The handbook’s following guidance specifies at least seven car lengths at seventy miles per hour and five at fifty miles per hour.

sec12-card-sec12-F026.front: Where must you move your vehicle after an interstate crash or mechanical breakdown?
sec12-card-sec12-F026.expected_back: After an interstate crash or breakdown, move entirely off the pavement toward the far-right shoulder, or as far right as practical.

sec12-card-sec12-F027.front: Which lights must stay illuminated after a nighttime crash or breakdown on an interstate?
sec12-card-sec12-F027.expected_back: At night after an interstate crash or breakdown, leave lights on and use emergency flashers.

sec12-card-sec12-F028.front: How do you signal passing patrols and motorists that your broken-down interstate car needs help?
sec12-card-sec12-F028.expected_back: Turn on emergency flashers to show that a broken-down vehicle needs assistance.

sec12-card-sec12-F029.front: Which four outside-the-car actions must a stranded interstate driver never take?
sec12-card-sec12-F029.expected_back: When stranded on an interstate, do not step into traffic, stand beside the vehicle, walk along or across the highway, or hitchhike.

sec12-card-sec12-F030.front: Where and how does Mississippi's handbook advise a stranded interstate driver to wait for help?
sec12-card-sec12-F030.expected_back: The handbook advises a stranded interstate driver to stay in the vehicle with doors locked while waiting for trustworthy help.

sec12-card-sec12-F031.front: What visibility gap sits directly behind a large tractor-trailer?
sec12-card-sec12-F031.expected_back: A large tractor-trailer has a blind area directly behind it.

sec12-card-sec12-F032.front: How can you tell instantly whether a large truck's driver can see your car?
sec12-card-sec12-F032.expected_back: If you cannot see a large truck’s side mirrors, its driver cannot see you in that position.

sec12-card-sec12-F033.front: What should you do if you aren't sure which interchange ramp enters the interstate properly?
sec12-card-sec12-F033.expected_back: If unsure which ramp enters the interstate correctly, pull off the road and stop to check the route.

sec12-card-sec12-F034.front: When is it safe to drive onto a complex interstate interchange ramp?
sec12-card-sec12-F034.expected_back: Do not proceed onto an interchange ramp until you understand how to use it.

sec13-card-sec13-F001.front: Why is lingering closely around a semi-truck or bus risky for smaller cars?
sec13-card-sec13-F001.expected_back: Large vehicles have blind areas in which their drivers cannot readily see or respond to nearby traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F002.front: How should you position your car when trailing behind a large truck?
sec13-card-sec13-F002.expected_back: Leave space behind a large truck and position your vehicle where the driver can see it in the side mirrors.

sec13-card-sec13-F003.front: What does it mean if you cannot see a large truck's front-mounted side mirrors from your driver's seat?
sec13-card-sec13-F003.expected_back: If the truck’s front-mounted side mirrors are not visible to you, the truck driver cannot see you in that position.

sec13-card-sec13-F004.front: Why must you switch to low beams when following a large truck at night?
sec13-card-sec13-F004.expected_back: Dim your headlights when following a large vehicle at night because bright reflections in its side mirrors may dazzle the driver.

sec13-card-sec13-F005.front: Why should you leave extra room when stopped behind a heavy truck facing uphill?
sec13-card-sec13-F005.expected_back: Leave extra room when stopped behind a large vehicle facing uphill, since it may roll backward slightly as it starts.

sec13-card-sec13-F006.front: Where inside your own lane should you stop behind a large truck on an uphill grade?
sec13-card-sec13-F006.expected_back: While stopped behind an uphill truck, stay toward the left within your own lane so its driver can see you.

sec13-card-sec13-F007.front: How does a large truck's stopping distance compare with a passenger car's, and how should you follow?
sec13-card-sec13-F007.expected_back: Large vehicles need more stopping distance, so avoid following closely.

sec13-card-sec13-F008.front: What checks and conditions are required before pulling into the passing lane around a large vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-F008.expected_back: Before passing a large vehicle, check ahead and behind and enter the passing lane only when clear and within a legal passing area.

sec13-card-sec13-F009.front: On a flat road, how much longer does overtaking a large vehicle take compared to passing a car?
sec13-card-sec13-F009.expected_back: The handbook estimates that passing a large vehicle on a level road takes three to five seconds longer than passing a car.

sec13-card-sec13-F010.front: How does an uphill grade typically affect passing a heavy truck?
sec13-card-sec13-F010.expected_back: An uphill grade may slow a large vehicle and make it easier to pass.

sec13-card-sec13-F011.front: What happens to a heavy truck's speed on a downhill grade, and what smart choice remains?
sec13-card-sec13-F011.expected_back: A large vehicle may gain speed on a downhill grade; waiting for a safer passing opportunity remains an option.

sec13-card-sec13-F012.front: After overtaking a large truck, what must appear in your rearview mirror before you merge back?
sec13-card-sec13-F012.expected_back: After passing a truck, wait to return until the rearview mirror shows its front wheels touching the road.

sec13-card-sec13-F013.front: What should you do with your speed right after pulling back in front of a large vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-F013.expected_back: Maintain speed after completing a pass of a large vehicle.

sec13-card-sec13-F014.front: How should you steer and manage speed when a large truck is overtaking your car?
sec13-card-sec13-F014.expected_back: When a large vehicle overtakes you, remain toward the far side of your lane and do not accelerate.

sec13-card-sec13-F015.front: Where should you position your car when meeting an oncoming semi-truck, and why?
sec13-card-sec13-F015.expected_back: When meeting a large oncoming vehicle, stay as far right as practical to reduce sideswipe and turbulence exposure.

sec13-card-sec13-F016.front: Why might a large truck swing toward the left just before making a right turn?
sec13-card-sec13-F016.expected_back: A large truck may swing left before a right turn because it needs additional turning room.

sec13-card-sec13-F017.front: What pass must you never attempt when a truck ahead could be setting up a right turn?
sec13-card-sec13-F017.expected_back: Do not pass a truck on its right when it may be preparing to turn right.

sec13-card-sec13-F018.front: How does Mississippi law classify a bicycle riding on a public road?
sec13-card-sec13-F018.expected_back: Mississippi treats a bicycle traveling on a public road as a vehicle, with the rider sharing motorists’ rights and responsibilities.

sec13-card-sec13-F019.front: How should you treat an approaching cyclist when yielding right-of-way at an intersection?
sec13-card-sec13-F019.expected_back: Yield to an approaching cyclist in the same way you would yield to an approaching motor vehicle.

sec13-card-sec13-F020.front: What is the minimum side clearance Mississippi requires when overtaking a bicycle?
sec13-card-sec13-F020.expected_back: Leave a minimum of three feet between your vehicle and a bicycle when overtaking it.

sec13-card-sec13-F021.front: When does Mississippi's bicycle-sharing guidance allow overtaking a same-direction cyclist inside a no-passing zone?
sec13-card-sec13-F021.expected_back: The bicycle-sharing section allows passing a same-direction bicycle in a no-passing zone only when it is safe.

sec13-card-sec13-F022.front: After overtaking a cyclist traveling your direction, when may you turn right?
sec13-card-sec13-F022.expected_back: After overtaking a same-direction cyclist, make a right turn only when it can be completed with reasonable safety.

sec13-card-sec13-F023.front: What turning shortcut in front of a bicyclist is strictly off-limits?
sec13-card-sec13-F023.expected_back: Never cut in front of a cyclist to make a turn.

sec13-card-sec13-F024.front: How should you use lanes when overtaking a bicycle instead of squeezing beside the rider?
sec13-card-sec13-F024.expected_back: When passing a bicycle, slow down and move into the next lane rather than attempting to squeeze alongside within the same lane.

sec13-card-sec13-F025.front: What must you do if oncoming cars prevent passing a bicyclist with safe clearance?
sec13-card-sec13-F025.expected_back: If approaching traffic prevents safe bicycle passing, wait behind the cyclist until that traffic clears.

sec13-card-sec13-F026.front: Even without physical contact, how can passing too closely destabilize a bicyclist?
sec13-card-sec13-F026.expected_back: Passing too close can disturb a bicycle with the passing vehicle’s airflow.

sec13-card-sec13-F027.front: What intersection controls and turn-signaling duties apply to bicyclists on Mississippi roads?
sec13-card-sec13-F027.expected_back: Cyclists must obey traffic controls, stop signs and stoplights, and use hand or arm turn signals.

sec13-card-sec13-F028.front: Where in the roadway should a cyclist normally ride, and how far from the pavement edge?
sec13-card-sec13-F028.expected_back: A cyclist should ride as far right as safely possible, generally two to four feet from the road edge.

sec13-card-sec13-F029.front: Which two situations allow a cyclist to move away from the right edge toward the left?
sec13-card-sec13-F029.expected_back: A cyclist may move left to overtake another same-direction vehicle or avoid hazards on the right.

sec13-card-sec13-F030.front: For which two intersection paths may a cyclist move farther into the travel lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F030.expected_back: A cyclist may move farther into the lane to continue straight past a right-turn-only lane or to prepare for a left turn.

sec13-card-sec13-F031.front: How fast can an experienced cyclist travel, and what misjudgment does that create for drivers?
sec13-card-sec13-F031.expected_back: An experienced cyclist may travel twenty to twenty-five miles per hour and be closer than a driver expects.

sec13-card-sec13-F032.front: Why should cyclists wear a bicycle helmet, and where might wearing one be mandatory?
sec13-card-sec13-F032.expected_back: A bicycle helmet helps reduce the risk of serious injury, and local rules may require one.

sec13-card-sec13-F033.front: Should a bicyclist ride with the flow of traffic or facing oncoming cars?
sec13-card-sec13-F033.expected_back: Ride a bicycle with the direction of traffic rather than toward approaching vehicles.

sec13-card-sec13-F034.front: What riding pattern helps motorists anticipate a cyclist's path safely?
sec13-card-sec13-F034.expected_back: Cycle predictably without weaving through traffic or back and forth across the road.

sec13-card-sec13-F035.front: What must a cyclist do before rolling into a street from a driveway, alley, or behind parked cars?
sec13-card-sec13-F035.expected_back: Before cycling into a road from an alley, driveway or behind parked vehicles, check for a clear path and yield to approaching traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F036.front: What gear helps motorists spot a cyclist during the day and after dark?
sec13-card-sec13-F036.expected_back: Bright clothing makes a cyclist easier to see; at night use bright front and rear lights and reflective clothing.

sec13-card-sec13-F037.front: Which three carriers should cyclists use to haul packages or gear safely?
sec13-card-sec13-F037.expected_back: Carry bicycle cargo in a basket, rack or panniers.

sec13-card-sec13-F038.front: When is carrying a passenger on a bicycle prohibited?
sec13-card-sec13-F038.expected_back: Do not carry a second rider on a bicycle designed for only one person.

sec13-card-sec13-F039.front: What rule governs holding onto or attaching a bicycle to another moving vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-F039.expected_back: Never attach a bicycle to another vehicle to be towed.

sec13-card-sec13-F040.front: What should a cyclist do on a narrow stretch when trailing cars cannot pass and a line builds?
sec13-card-sec13-F040.expected_back: When motorists have difficulty passing, a cyclist should periodically pull aside rather than allowing a long queue to build.

sec13-card-sec13-F041.front: Does Mississippi law allow cyclists to ride two abreast, and what limit applies?
sec13-card-sec13-F041.expected_back: Cyclists may ride side by side under state law, but two-abreast riding should not hinder normal reasonable traffic movement.

sec13-card-sec13-F042.front: How should cyclists position themselves on a roadway with multiple lanes?
sec13-card-sec13-F042.expected_back: On a road with several lanes, a cyclist should remain within one lane.

sec14-card-sec14-F001.front: Which three items must every Mississippi resident's vehicle carry or maintain legally?
sec14-card-sec14-F001.expected_back: Mississippi residents’ vehicles need a state license plate, a certificate of title and adequate insurance.

sec14-card-sec14-F002.front: When must a motorist carry a valid driver's license?
sec14-card-sec14-F002.expected_back: Carry a valid driver’s license whenever driving.

sec14-card-sec14-F003.front: In which county must you buy your vehicle tag, and which local official handles tag information?
sec14-card-sec14-F003.expected_back: Buy the vehicle’s plate or tag in the county of residence and contact the local Tax Collector for purchase information.

sec14-card-sec14-F004.front: How many days do you have to get a Mississippi license plate after moving a vehicle into the state?
sec14-card-sec14-F004.expected_back: A person moving a vehicle into Mississippi must obtain the state’s plate within thirty days.

sec14-card-sec14-F005.front: Where on the vehicle must a Mississippi license plate be mounted?
sec14-card-sec14-F005.expected_back: Mount a Mississippi plate on the rear of the vehicle.

sec14-card-sec14-F006.front: What rule applies to trailer hitches, frames, emblems, or decorations around your license plate?
sec14-card-sec14-F006.expected_back: A hitch, emblem or decoration must not hide any letter or number on the plate.

sec14-card-sec14-F007.front: From how far away must your license-plate light make tag characters readable at night?
sec14-card-sec14-F007.expected_back: At night the plate light must make its characters readable from sixty feet away.

sec14-card-sec14-F008.front: Which ownership document is required for every vehicle in Mississippi?
sec14-card-sec14-F008.expected_back: Every vehicle must have a certificate of title.

sec14-card-sec14-F009.front: Who supplies the title application when you buy from a new-car or used-car dealership?
sec14-card-sec14-F009.expected_back: New-car and used-car dealers supply title applications for vehicles they sell.

sec14-card-sec14-F010.front: Which two supporting records does the manual list when backing a title application?
sec14-card-sec14-F010.expected_back: The handbook requires a bill of sale and two years of tag receipts to support a title application.

sec14-card-sec14-F011.front: What document is needed to apply for a Mississippi title on a car brought from another state?
sec14-card-sec14-F011.expected_back: A vehicle brought from another state needs its out-of-state title for the Mississippi title application.

sec14-card-sec14-F012.front: Which two groups must qualify in order to accept Mississippi title applications?
sec14-card-sec14-F012.expected_back: Licensed vehicle dealers and county tax collectors must qualify to accept title applications.

sec14-card-sec14-F013.front: Which lending organizations can also qualify as designated title-application agents?
sec14-card-sec14-F013.expected_back: Banks and other financial institutions may qualify as designated title-application agents.

sec14-card-sec14-F014.front: What check is required if your Mississippi-registered car has aftermarket window tint film installed?
sec14-card-sec14-F014.expected_back: A Mississippi-registered vehicle with aftermarket window film needs inspection at an authorized window-tint station.

sec14-card-sec14-F015.front: Which two compliance items are required once aftermarket-tinted windows pass inspection?
sec14-card-sec14-F015.expected_back: Aftermarket-tinted windows require an inspection certificate and decal.

sec14-card-sec14-F016.front: What fee does the Mississippi manual list for the window-tint compliance certificate and decal?
sec14-card-sec14-F016.expected_back: The handbook lists a five-dollar charge for the window-tint compliance certificate and decal.

sec14-card-sec14-F017.front: On which corner of the windshield must the window-tint compliance decal be placed?
sec14-card-sec14-F017.expected_back: Place the window-tint decal at the windshield’s lower-left corner.

sec14-card-sec14-F018.front: Where inside the cabin must you keep your paper window-tint compliance certificate?
sec14-card-sec14-F018.expected_back: Keep the tint compliance certificate on the dashboard or in the dashboard compartment.

sec14-card-sec14-F019.front: Which vehicles operated in Mississippi are required to carry liability insurance?
sec14-card-sec14-F019.expected_back: Mississippi requires liability insurance for every motor vehicle operated in the state.

sec14-card-sec14-F020.front: What are Mississippi's minimum liability coverage amounts for injury to one person and for two or more people?
sec14-card-sec14-F020.expected_back: The handbook lists minimum accident coverage of twenty-five thousand dollars for one person and fifty thousand dollars for two or more people.

sec14-card-sec14-F021.front: What is Mississippi's minimum liability coverage for damaging another person's property in one crash?
sec14-card-sec14-F021.expected_back: The listed minimum coverage for another person’s property damaged in a single accident is twenty-five thousand dollars.

sec14-card-sec14-F022.front: What insurance proof must insured owners keep inside each covered vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F022.expected_back: The insured parties must keep a current valid insurance card in each vehicle.

sec14-card-sec14-F023.front: What immediate consequences can follow failing to show insurance proof at a traffic stop or crash?
sec14-card-sec14-F023.expected_back: Failure to show insurance evidence at a crash or traffic stop may lead to a citation and fine.

sec14-card-sec14-F024.front: Must your Mississippi insurance card be printed on paper, or is digital display allowed?
sec14-card-sec14-F024.expected_back: An insurance card may be presented electronically on a phone or another electronic device.

sec14-card-sec14-F025.front: What license penalty can strike a driver who cannot show insurance after a crash?
sec14-card-sec14-F025.expected_back: A driver unable to show insurance after a crash may face suspension of driving privileges.

sec14-card-sec14-F026.front: What straightforward proof avoids a post-crash insurance suspension if you merely lacked the card on scene?
sec14-card-sec14-F026.expected_back: One way the handbook gives to avoid that suspension is proving adequate insurance was active when the crash occurred.

sec14-card-sec14-F027.front: What dollar value in a deposit certificate or securities does the manual list as post-crash financial responsibility?
sec14-card-sec14-F027.expected_back: The handbook also lists a deposit certificate or securities worth fifteen thousand dollars as an alternative demonstration of financial responsibility after a crash.

sec14-card-sec14-F028.front: What payment commitment must a Mississippi self-insurance certificate include?
sec14-card-sec14-F028.expected_back: A self-insurance certificate must include an agreement to pay judgments in amounts equivalent to an owner’s insurance policy.

sec14-card-sec14-F029.front: How many vehicles must an owner have to qualify as a self-insurer in Mississippi?
sec14-card-sec14-F029.expected_back: A self-insurer must own more than twenty-five vehicles.

sec14-card-sec14-F030.front: Which three financial guarantees sufficient to cover crash damages may the department accept after a collision?
sec14-card-sec14-F030.expected_back: The department may accept cash, negotiable securities or a corporate surety bond sufficient to cover damages as a post-crash responsibility measure.

sec14-card-sec14-F031.front: Which three fault or payment outcomes can also prevent a post-crash license suspension?
sec14-card-sec14-F031.expected_back: Other listed ways to avoid suspension include a liability release, a final finding of non-liability or proof the other party paid the damages.

sec14-card-sec14-F032.front: What insurance purchase and filing must an uninsured driver make after causing an injury or damage crash?
sec14-card-sec14-F032.expected_back: An uninsured driver at fault for a crash causing injury or property damage must buy liability insurance and file proof of it.

sec14-card-sec14-F033.front: What two standards must that mandatory post-crash liability policy satisfy?
sec14-card-sec14-F033.expected_back: The required post-crash policy must meet Mississippi’s minimum liability coverage and come from an insurer licensed in the state.

sec14-card-sec14-F034.front: For how long from the crash date must filed liability coverage stay active after an uninsured at-fault wreck?
sec14-card-sec14-F034.expected_back: The filed liability coverage required after the uninsured at-fault crash must remain effective for three years from the crash date.

sec15-card-sec15-F001.front: What is Mississippi's legal rule on driving while impaired by alcohol or drugs?
sec15-card-sec15-F001.expected_back: Driving while impaired by alcohol or drugs is unlawful in Mississippi.

sec15-card-sec15-F002.front: Which three mental traits can alcohol alter, and what physical response does it slow?
sec15-card-sec15-F002.expected_back: Alcohol can change a driver’s judgment, temperament and personality and can slow reactions.

sec15-card-sec15-F003.front: Besides staying out of the driver's seat yourself after drinking, what else must you refuse to allow?
sec15-card-sec15-F003.expected_back: After drinking alcohol, do not drive or allow another person who drank to drive.

sec15-card-sec15-F004.front: How can marijuana, street drugs, or even prescription medicines affect your driving skills?
sec15-card-sec15-F004.expected_back: Marijuana and other drugs, including prescription medicines, can slow reflexes and impair judgment.

sec15-card-sec15-F005.front: What legal consequence can follow smoking medical cannabis inside a vehicle or controlling a vehicle impaired?
sec15-card-sec15-F005.expected_back: Smoking medical cannabis in a vehicle or controlling a vehicle while impaired can violate Mississippi law and result in arrest.

sec15-card-sec15-F006.front: Does holding a valid doctor's prescription or medical-cannabis card make impaired driving legal?
sec15-card-sec15-F006.expected_back: A prescription or medical-cannabis status does not make impaired driving lawful.

sec15-card-sec15-F007.front: What testing agreement do you automatically accept simply by driving on Mississippi roads?
sec15-card-sec15-F007.expected_back: Operating a motor vehicle in Mississippi gives implied consent to testing for intoxicating substances.

sec15-card-sec15-F008.front: When may a Mississippi officer ask a driver to take a breath or chemical screening?
sec15-card-sec15-F008.expected_back: An officer with good reason to suspect impaired operation may request a breath or chemical test.

sec15-card-sec15-F009.front: What three-letter abbreviation stands for blood alcohol content in the manual?
sec15-card-sec15-F009.expected_back: Blood alcohol content is abbreviated BAC.

sec15-card-sec15-F010.front: What BAC threshold triggers regular DUI classification for drivers aged twenty-one or older?
sec15-card-sec15-F010.expected_back: For a driver aged twenty-one or older, the handbook’s alcohol threshold is a BAC of zero point zero eight percent or higher.

sec15-card-sec15-F011.front: What much lower BAC threshold applies to Mississippi drivers younger than twenty-one?
sec15-card-sec15-F011.expected_back: For a driver younger than twenty-one, the handbook’s alcohol threshold is a BAC of zero point zero two percent or higher.

sec15-card-sec15-F012.front: What happens to your physical driver's license on the spot if you refuse a breath or chemical check?
sec15-card-sec15-F012.expected_back: A driver may refuse the requested breath or chemical test but must immediately surrender the license to the officer.

sec15-card-sec15-F013.front: How many days does the temporary driving receipt last after a breath or chemical refusal?
sec15-card-sec15-F013.expected_back: After test refusal, the officer issues a license receipt functioning as a temporary driving permit for forty-five days.

sec15-card-sec15-F014.front: Where does the officer forward your seized license and sworn report after a chemical refusal?
sec15-card-sec15-F014.expected_back: After test refusal, the officer sends the license and sworn report to the Public Safety Commissioner for review.

sec15-card-sec15-F015.front: How long is the baseline administrative license suspension described for refusing a breath or chemical check?
sec15-card-sec15-F015.expected_back: The handbook describes a ninety-day administrative suspension for breath or chemical test refusal.

sec15-card-sec15-F016.front: How are suspensions affected if you refuse chemical screening again after a prior conviction or non-adjudication?
sec15-card-sec15-F016.expected_back: Later refusals resulting in conviction or non-adjudication carry longer suspensions.

sec15-card-sec15-F017.front: For how many days is the officer's temporary driving receipt valid when your BAC hits the legal limit?
sec15-card-sec15-F017.expected_back: When BAC reaches the driver’s applicable limit, the officer takes the license and provides a temporary driving receipt valid for thirty days.

sec15-card-sec15-F018.front: Which age group and minimum BAC reading anchor the manual's regular DUI penalty schedule?
sec15-card-sec15-F018.expected_back: The regular DUI penalty table applies to drivers aged twenty-one or older with BAC of at least zero point zero eight percent.

sec15-card-sec15-F019.front: How is a first regular DUI classified, and what fine range does the manual list?
sec15-card-sec15-F019.expected_back: The handbook lists a first DUI as a misdemeanor with a fine from two hundred fifty to one thousand dollars.

sec15-card-sec15-F020.front: What maximum jail stay and license suspension length apply to a first-offense regular DUI?
sec15-card-sec15-F020.expected_back: The first-offense DUI table lists up to forty-eight hours in jail and a one-hundred-twenty-day license suspension.

sec15-card-sec15-F021.front: Within what lookback window is a second DUI counted, how is it classed, and what is the fine range?
sec15-card-sec15-F021.expected_back: A second DUI within five years is listed as a misdemeanor with a fine from six hundred to fifteen hundred dollars.

sec15-card-sec15-F022.front: What jail range and license suspension apply to a second regular DUI within five years?
sec15-card-sec15-F022.memory_hook: Five days to six months, year
sec15-card-sec15-F022.expected_back: The second-offense DUI table gives jail time from five days to six months and a one-year suspension.

sec15-card-sec15-F023.front: How does charge severity shift on a third DUI within five years, and what fine range applies?
sec15-card-sec15-F023.expected_back: A third DUI within five years is listed as a felony with a fine from two thousand to five thousand dollars.

sec15-card-sec15-F024.front: What prison term and license loss follow a third-offense regular DUI within five years?
sec15-card-sec15-F024.expected_back: The third-offense table gives one to five years in Department of Corrections custody and license loss for the sentence’s full term.

sec15-card-sec15-F025.front: After finishing prison on a third-offense DUI, what driving restriction applies and for how long?
sec15-card-sec15-F025.expected_back: After incarceration for the third-offense DUI, the table permits only an interlock-restricted license for three years.

sec15-card-sec15-F026.front: Does the five-year lookback still limit a fourth DUI, and what fine range applies?
sec15-card-sec15-F026.expected_back: A fourth or later DUI applies regardless of elapsed time and carries a listed fine from three thousand to ten thousand dollars.

sec15-card-sec15-F027.front: What custody term and license penalty apply to a fourth or subsequent DUI?
sec15-card-sec15-F027.expected_back: The fourth-or-later DUI table gives two to ten years in custody and license loss throughout the sentence.

sec15-card-sec15-F028.front: After serving custody for a fourth or later DUI, what license limit applies and for how long?
sec15-card-sec15-F028.expected_back: After incarceration for a fourth or later DUI, only an interlock-restricted license is available for ten years under the table.

sec15-card-sec15-F029.front: Which age group and exact BAC band fall under Mississippi's Zero Tolerance penalty table?
sec15-card-sec15-F029.memory_hook: Under twenty-one, point two to eight
sec15-card-sec15-F029.expected_back: Zero-tolerance penalties apply to drivers younger than twenty-one with BAC at least zero point zero two percent but below zero point zero eight percent.

sec15-card-sec15-F030.front: How is a driver younger than twenty-one charged if their BAC reaches zero point zero eight percent or higher?
sec15-card-sec15-F030.expected_back: A driver younger than twenty-one with BAC at least zero point zero eight percent is classified under regular DUI rather than the zero-tolerance category.

sec15-card-sec15-F031.front: What fine and suspension length apply to a first Zero Tolerance DUI offense?
sec15-card-sec15-F031.expected_back: A first zero-tolerance DUI carries a listed two-hundred-fifty-dollar fine and a one-hundred-twenty-day suspension.

sec15-card-sec15-F032.front: What maximum fine and license suspension apply to a second Zero Tolerance DUI within five years?
sec15-card-sec15-F032.expected_back: A second zero-tolerance DUI within five years has a fine no higher than five hundred dollars and a one-year suspension.

sec15-card-sec15-F033.front: What is the maximum fine for a third Zero Tolerance DUI within five years?
sec15-card-sec15-F033.expected_back: A third zero-tolerance DUI within five years has a fine no higher than one thousand dollars.

sec15-card-sec15-F034.front: How long does the license suspension last on a third Zero Tolerance DUI?
sec15-card-sec15-F034.expected_back: The third zero-tolerance suspension lasts two years or until age twenty-one, whichever is longer.

sec15-card-sec15-F035.front: How much extra suspension time gets added when a first DUI or Zero Tolerance conviction includes chemical refusal?
sec15-card-sec15-F035.expected_back: A first regular or zero-tolerance DUI conviction combined with test refusal adds a ninety-day license suspension to the original penalty.

sec15-card-sec15-F036.front: Which two aggravating circumstances make DUI penalties harsher than the baseline tables?
sec15-card-sec15-F036.expected_back: DUI penalties become more severe for driving while suspended for an earlier DUI or for an impaired-driving crash causing injury.

sec15-card-sec15-F037.front: Which state official holds authority to remove driving privileges for unlawful or unsafe driving?
sec15-card-sec15-F037.expected_back: The Public Safety Commissioner can remove driving privileges for unlawful or unsafe driving.

sec15-card-sec15-F038.front: When can your license be suspended immediately without holding a preliminary hearing first?
sec15-card-sec15-F038.expected_back: A suspension may be imposed without a preliminary hearing when public records or sufficient evidence establish a listed basis.

sec15-card-sec15-F039.front: How does an offense that carries mandatory revocation also relate to suspension authority?
sec15-card-sec15-F039.expected_back: A conviction requiring mandatory revocation is also listed as a basis for suspension.

sec15-card-sec15-F040.front: Which three severe crash outcomes can trigger license suspension for an involved driver?
sec15-card-sec15-F040.expected_back: Involvement as a driver in a crash causing death, personal injury or serious property damage is a listed suspension basis.

sec15-card-sec15-F041.front: Which two patterns of dangerous behind-the-wheel behavior are grounds for suspending your license?
sec15-card-sec15-F041.expected_back: Habitually reckless or negligent driving and repeated serious traffic convictions are grounds for suspension.

sec15-card-sec15-F042.front: How do driving unfitness and letting someone misuse your license affect your driving privilege?
sec15-card-sec15-F042.expected_back: Physical or mental inability to drive and allowing fraudulent use of a license are listed suspension grounds.

sec15-card-sec15-F043.front: How can a DUI or serious violation convicted in another state affect your Mississippi license?
sec15-card-sec15-F043.expected_back: An out-of-state DUI conviction or another out-of-state offense that would trigger Mississippi suspension or revocation can affect Mississippi privileges.

sec15-card-sec15-F044.front: What happens if someone gets a Mississippi license while suspended in another state?
sec15-card-sec15-F044.expected_back: Obtaining a Mississippi license while another state’s license is suspended is a listed suspension basis.

sec15-card-sec15-F045.front: Which family-court financial obligation can get your Mississippi driver's license suspended if unpaid?
sec15-card-sec15-F045.expected_back: Failure to pay child support is a listed reason for suspension.

sec15-card-sec15-F046.front: What license penalty follows a driving-related manslaughter or negligent-homicide conviction?
sec15-card-sec15-F046.expected_back: A driving-related manslaughter or negligent-homicide conviction requires a one-year revocation in the handbook.

sec15-card-sec15-F047.front: What license penalty applies when a motor vehicle is used in committing any felony?
sec15-card-sec15-F047.expected_back: A felony involving use of a motor vehicle requires a one-year revocation in the handbook.

sec15-card-sec15-F048.front: What license consequence hits a driver convicted of failing to stop and render required aid at a crash?
sec15-card-sec15-F048.expected_back: Failure to stop and provide legally required crash assistance requires a one-year revocation in the handbook.

sec15-card-sec15-F049.front: What happens to your license for perjury or lying to the department about vehicle ownership or operation?
sec15-card-sec15-F049.expected_back: Perjury or a false department statement about vehicle ownership or operation requires a one-year revocation in the handbook.

sec15-card-sec15-F050.front: How many reckless-driving convictions within twelve months trigger a mandatory one-year revocation?
sec15-card-sec15-F050.expected_back: Three reckless-driving convictions in twelve months require a one-year revocation in the handbook.

sec15-card-sec15-F051.front: Does your license turn back on automatically when a suspension or revocation period ends?
sec15-card-sec15-F051.expected_back: Reinstatement eligibility after suspension or revocation requires following the applicable fee and procedure.

sec15-card-sec15-F052.front: What reinstatement fee applies after an Implied Consent, DUI, or controlled-substance conviction?
sec15-card-sec15-F052.expected_back: The handbook lists a one-hundred-seventy-five-dollar reinstatement fee for Implied Consent, DUI or controlled-substance-law convictions.

sec15-card-sec15-F053.front: What reinstatement fee does the manual list after a suspension for unpaid child support?
sec15-card-sec15-F053.expected_back: Reinstatement after suspension for unpaid child support has a listed fee of twenty-five dollars.

sec15-card-sec15-F054.front: What reinstatement fee applies to standard suspensions outside the DUI, drug, or child-support tiers?
sec15-card-sec15-F054.expected_back: The listed reinstatement charge for other suspensions is one hundred dollars.

sec15-card-sec15-F055.front: Which single payment instrument is accepted for mailed reinstatement fees, and which three are rejected?
sec15-card-sec15-F055.expected_back: For mailed reinstatement payment, use a cashier’s check payable to the Department of Public Safety rather than cash, a money order or a personal check.

sec15-card-sec15-F056.front: What court document is required before reinstating after failing to appear or leaving your license for bond?
sec15-card-sec15-F056.expected_back: A license deposited instead of bond or a failure to appear in court requires a judge’s corrected court abstract before reinstatement.

sec15-card-sec15-F057.front: To which bureau and Mississippi city are mailed DUI or unpaid-ticket reinstatement payments sent?
sec15-card-sec15-F057.expected_back: The handbook directs mailed DUI or unpaid-ticket reinstatement payments to the Driver Service Bureau in Canton.

sec15-card-sec15-F058.front: Where is discarding solid waste legal on public roads, rights-of-way, or public lands?
sec15-card-sec15-F058.expected_back: Do not discard solid waste on roads, public rights of way or other public land except in authorized containers or disposal areas.

sec15-card-sec15-F059.front: Who can be cited under Mississippi's littering law when trash is thrown from a motor vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F059.expected_back: When waste is discarded from a motor vehicle, its owner, operator or both may be treated as violating the littering law.

sec15-card-sec15-F060.front: What is Mississippi's rule on dumping solid waste into rivers, lakes, or state waters?
sec15-card-sec15-F060.expected_back: Disposing of solid waste in Mississippi waters is prohibited.

sec15-card-sec15-F061.front: What three conditions must be met before disposing of waste on private property?
sec15-card-sec15-F061.expected_back: Waste disposal on private property requires the owner’s prior written consent and must not create a public nuisance or violate other laws.

sec15-card-sec15-F062.front: What rule governs discharging raw human waste from a vehicle, camper, boat, train, or plane?
sec15-card-sec15-F062.expected_back: Raw human waste from a vehicle, train, aircraft or vessel may not be discharged onto state land or waters, whether public or private.

sec15-card-sec15-F063.front: Are you off the hook if you direct or cause someone else to dump or spill prohibited waste?
sec15-card-sec15-F063.expected_back: Causing another person to throw, scatter, spill or place prohibited waste is also unlawful.

sec16-card-sec16-F001.front: Which federal service and cabinet department administer the Natchez Trace Parkway?
sec16-card-sec16-F001.expected_back: The National Park Service, within the United States Department of the Interior, administers the Natchez Trace Parkway.

sec16-card-sec16-F002.front: What historic route does the Natchez Trace Parkway commemorate?
sec16-card-sec16-F002.expected_back: The Natchez Trace Parkway commemorates an early frontier route important to the Old Southwest’s development.

sec16-card-sec16-F003.front: Which vehicles are barred from the Natchez Trace Parkway, and how is road entry designed?
sec16-card-sec16-F003.expected_back: Commercial vehicles are excluded from the Natchez Trace Parkway and entry access is limited.

sec16-card-sec16-F004.front: Who patrols the Natchez Trace Parkway to protect resources and help motorists?
sec16-card-sec16-F004.expected_back: Park Rangers protect and patrol the Parkway and can assist travelers.

sec16-card-sec16-F005.front: To whom should you report a crash, wildfire, or emergency along the Natchez Trace Parkway?
sec16-card-sec16-F005.expected_back: Report a Parkway crash, fire or other emergency to the nearest Ranger.

sec16-card-sec16-F006.front: Which two key details should you give when calling for Park Ranger help on the Trace?
sec16-card-sec16-F006.expected_back: When requesting Ranger assistance, describe the situation and provide the approximate location.

sec16-card-sec16-F007.front: How do federal regulations and state traffic laws interact on the Natchez Trace Parkway?
sec16-card-sec16-F007.expected_back: Federal rules govern Parkway traffic and facility use, and state traffic laws also apply.

sec16-card-sec16-F008.front: What is the maximum speed limit on the Natchez Trace Parkway unless posted lower?
sec16-card-sec16-F008.expected_back: The Natchez Trace Parkway’s maximum travel speed is fifty miles per hour unless a lower speed is posted.

sec16-card-sec16-F009.front: What duty applies to posted traffic and park signs along the Natchez Trace Parkway?

sec16-card-sec16-F010.front: What rule governs hunting or discharging firearms on Natchez Trace Parkway lands?
sec16-card-sec16-F010.expected_back: The handbook prohibits hunting or using firearms on Parkway lands.

sec16-card-sec16-F011.front: How must you handle cigarettes, matches, and trash while driving the Parkway?
sec16-card-sec16-F011.expected_back: Fully extinguish smoking materials and matches and never throw them or other litter from a moving vehicle.

sec16-card-sec16-F012.front: Who should you ask whenever you are unsure about a Natchez Trace Parkway regulation?
sec16-card-sec16-F012.expected_back: Ask a Park Ranger when uncertain about a Parkway rule.

sec16-card-sec16-F013.front: In which court system are traffic or facility violations on the Natchez Trace Parkway tried?
sec16-card-sec16-F013.expected_back: The handbook states that violations on the Parkway roadway or facilities are tried in federal court.

sec16-card-sec16-F014.front: Which national industry organization operates the Share the Road highway-safety program?
sec16-card-sec16-F014.expected_back: Share the Road is a highway-safety program operated by the American Trucking Associations.

sec16-card-sec16-F015.front: Who leads instruction in the Share the Road program to help drivers avoid crashes?
sec16-card-sec16-F015.expected_back: The Share the Road program uses experienced professional truck drivers to teach the public ways to avoid road crashes.

sec16-card-sec16-F016.front: How do Share the Road demonstrations physically illustrate common highway crash traps?
sec16-card-sec16-F016.expected_back: Share the Road demonstrations arrange cars and trucks in simulated highway lanes to show common crash situations.

sec16-card-sec16-F017.front: Which two outreach channels does Share the Road use to promote safer highway habits?
sec16-card-sec16-F017.expected_back: The program uses media and community events to encourage safer driving behavior.

sec16-card-sec16-F018.front: Which three partner groups team up with the Share the Road safety campaign?
sec16-card-sec16-F018.expected_back: Share the Road works with state trucking groups, highway-safety partners and the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration.

sec04-card-sec04-F001.front: What two obligations does every driver have toward roadway traffic signs and signals?
sec04-card-sec04-F001.expected_back: Drivers must identify traffic signs and signals and follow their directions.

sec04-card-sec04-F002.front: How are U.S. road signs shifting away from text-only panels, and how are unfamiliar symbols introduced?
sec04-card-sec04-F002.expected_back: The handbook describes a gradual transition from word-based signs to international picture and symbol designs, with words accompanying unfamiliar designs.

sec04-card-sec04-F003.front: What core driver requirement does red communicate on a traffic-control device in the Mississippi manual?
sec04-card-sec04-F003.expected_back: Red on a traffic-control device indicates a stop requirement.

sec04-card-sec04-F004.front: Which two meanings does the color green convey on roadway controls and highway signs?
sec04-card-sec04-F004.expected_back: Green identifies route guidance or a movement that is permitted.

sec04-card-sec04-F005.front: Which standard roadway message category uses the color yellow?
sec04-card-sec04-F005.expected_back: Yellow is the standard color for a general warning.

sec04-card-sec04-F006.front: What do blue highway signs guide motorists toward?
sec04-card-sec04-F006.expected_back: Blue is used to guide motorists to services.

sec04-card-sec04-F007.front: Which sign category uses black lettering or symbols on a white background?
sec04-card-sec04-F007.expected_back: Black and white are used for regulatory messages.

sec04-card-sec04-F008.front: What roadside activity is announced by orange warning signs?
sec04-card-sec04-F008.expected_back: Orange warns of construction or maintenance activity.

sec04-card-sec04-F009.front: Which two kinds of public destinations are marked by brown guide signs?
sec04-card-sec04-F009.expected_back: Brown guides travelers to public recreation and scenic places.

sec04-card-sec04-F010.front: Which single traffic sign is reserved for the eight-sided octagon shape?
sec04-card-sec04-F010.expected_back: An eight-sided sign shape is reserved for stop signs.

sec04-card-sec04-F011.front: What type of highway sign commonly uses a wide horizontal rectangle?
sec04-card-sec04-F011.expected_back: A horizontal rectangular shape is commonly used for guidance signs.

sec04-card-sec04-F012.front: Which specific right-of-way sign owns the equilateral triangle shape?
sec04-card-sec04-F012.expected_back: An equilateral triangular sign shape is reserved for yield signs.

sec04-card-sec04-F013.front: What zone ahead is announced by a pennant-shaped warning sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F013.expected_back: A pennant-shaped sign warns that a no-passing zone is ahead.

sec04-card-sec04-F014.front: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign alert drivers about?
sec04-card-sec04-F014.expected_back: A diamond-shaped sign warns of a present or possible hazard on or near the road.

sec04-card-sec04-F015.front: What kind of rules appear on vertical rectangular signs, and what is a classic example?
sec04-card-sec04-F015.expected_back: Vertical rectangular signs usually carry regulations such as speed limits.

sec04-card-sec04-F016.front: Which two child-safety areas are marked by a five-sided pentagon sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F016.expected_back: A pentagon-shaped sign identifies a school crossing or warns of a school zone.

sec04-card-sec04-F017.front: What specific crossing ahead is announced by a round warning sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F017.expected_back: A round sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

sec04-card-sec04-F018.front: What two obligations apply at every stop sign before you pull into an intersection?
sec04-card-sec04-F018.expected_back: At a stop sign, halt completely before entering the intersection and yield to approaching traffic close enough to create danger.

sec04-card-sec04-F019.front: How can a Do Not Enter sign display its ban, and what does it forbid?
sec04-card-sec04-F019.expected_back: A Do Not Enter sign prohibits entering its lane, whether it uses words or a white bar across a red circle.

sec04-card-sec04-F020.front: What urgent danger does a Wrong Way sign warn you is happening right now?
sec04-card-sec04-F020.expected_back: A Wrong Way sign warns that your travel opposes the lane’s other traffic and creates a head-on crash risk.

sec04-card-sec04-F021.front: What must you do right away after spotting a Wrong Way sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F021.expected_back: After encountering a Wrong Way sign, leave the roadway and turn around as soon as possible.

sec04-card-sec04-F022.front: What intersection maneuver is outlawed by a No Left Turn sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F022.expected_back: A No Left Turn sign forbids a left turn at the intersection.

sec04-card-sec04-F023.front: What intersection maneuver is outlawed by a No Right Turn sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F023.expected_back: A No Right Turn sign forbids a right turn at the intersection.

sec04-card-sec04-F024.front: Which three roadway spots are covered by a no-turnaround or No U-Turn prohibition?
sec04-card-sec04-F024.expected_back: A no-turnaround prohibition applies to turning around in an intersection, a street’s center or a highway median.

sec04-card-sec04-F025.front: What vehicle restriction does a No Trucks regulatory sign enforce?
sec04-card-sec04-F025.expected_back: A No Trucks sign excludes trucks from the indicated street or highway.

sec04-card-sec04-F026.front: Under what three conditions is turning right on a red light allowed in Mississippi?
sec04-card-sec04-F026.expected_back: A right turn on red is generally allowed after a complete stop and checking that the route is clear, unless a sign prohibits it.

sec04-card-sec04-F027.front: When must you hold behind the line for a green light instead of turning right on red?
sec04-card-sec04-F027.expected_back: Where a sign prohibits right turns on red, wait for green before making the right turn.

sec04-card-sec04-F028.front: Who holds priority when you approach a yield sign at a merge or intersection?
sec04-card-sec04-F028.expected_back: A yield sign requires allowing vehicles already on the roadway to proceed first.

sec04-card-sec04-F029.front: What do Keep Left and Keep Right regulatory signs tell a driver approaching an obstacle or island?
sec04-card-sec04-F029.expected_back: Keep Left and Keep Right signs direct the side on which a driver must proceed.

sec04-card-sec04-F030.front: What choice does a driver have in a lane governed by a mandatory left-turn sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F030.expected_back: A mandatory left-turn sign requires turning left rather than choosing another movement.

sec04-card-sec04-F031.front: What movement is required when a mandatory right-turn sign controls your lane?
sec04-card-sec04-F031.expected_back: A mandatory right-turn sign requires turning right rather than choosing another movement.

sec04-card-sec04-F032.front: What travel rule does a one-direction arrow sign establish?
sec04-card-sec04-F032.expected_back: A one-direction arrow sign permits travel only in the arrow’s direction.

sec04-card-sec04-F033.front: Which vehicles are legally allowed to park in reserved accessible parking spaces?
sec04-card-sec04-F033.expected_back: Reserved accessible parking may be used only by a vehicle displaying an official indicator, such as an authorized plate or temporary hangtag.

sec04-card-sec04-F034.front: Which local Mississippi office provides information on getting an accessible-parking tag?
sec04-card-sec04-F034.expected_back: The County Tax Collector’s Office provides information about obtaining an accessible-parking tag.

sec04-card-sec04-F035.front: Under what road conditions does a posted speed-limit sign represent the top legal speed?
sec04-card-sec04-F035.expected_back: A posted speed-limit sign gives the highest allowed speed under ideal driving conditions.

sec04-card-sec04-F036.front: What is permitted inside a center turn-only lane, and which two uses are banned?
sec04-card-sec04-F036.expected_back: A center turn-only lane is available for turning, not for ordinary travel or passing.

sec04-card-sec04-F037.front: What driver maneuver does a regulatory no-passing sign forbid?
sec04-card-sec04-F037.expected_back: A no-passing sign prohibits entering another lane to overtake a vehicle.

sec04-card-sec04-F038.front: Which three upcoming intersection controls can yellow advance warning signs announce?
sec04-card-sec04-F038.expected_back: Warnings may announce an upcoming traffic signal, stop control or yield control.

sec04-card-sec04-F039.front: How does a crossroad warning diamond differ from a T-intersection warning diamond?
sec04-card-sec04-F039.expected_back: A crossroad warning indicates an intersection ahead, while a T-intersection warning identifies a joining road ending at the intersection.

sec04-card-sec04-F040.front: Which way should you prepare to merge when a warning announces that the right lane ends?
sec04-card-sec04-F040.expected_back: When a warning says the right lane ends, prepare to merge left.

sec04-card-sec04-F041.front: Which way should you prepare to merge when a warning announces that the left lane ends?
sec04-card-sec04-F041.expected_back: When a warning says the left lane ends, prepare to merge right.

sec04-card-sec04-F042.front: What roadway feature do side-road warning signs identify ahead?
sec04-card-sec04-F042.expected_back: Side-road warnings identify roads entering ahead, including an entry from an angle.

sec04-card-sec04-F043.front: What traffic movement does a merging-ramp warning sign alert mainline drivers to expect?
sec04-card-sec04-F043.expected_back: A merging-ramp warning announces traffic entering the roadway from an access lane.

sec04-card-sec04-F044.front: How does a new-lane or added-lane warning sign differ from a standard merge sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F044.expected_back: A new-lane warning means an additional lane joins the roadway without requiring a merge.

sec04-card-sec04-F045.front: What hazard ahead does a railroad-crossing warning alert a driver to?
sec04-card-sec04-F045.expected_back: A railroad-crossing warning alerts the driver to tracks ahead.

sec04-card-sec04-F046.front: What traffic pattern does a two-way-traffic warning sign tell you is operating?
sec04-card-sec04-F046.expected_back: A two-way-traffic warning indicates traffic moving in opposing directions.
