sec04-card-sec04-F047.front: What road change ahead is announced by a divided-highway warning sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F047.expected_back: A divided-highway warning indicates a separated roadway ahead.

sec04-card-sec04-F048.front: What change ahead does a divided-highway-ends warning sign announce?
sec04-card-sec04-F048.expected_back: A divided-highway-ends warning announces the return of two-way traffic ahead.

sec04-card-sec04-F049.front: What intersection layout ahead is announced by a traffic-circle warning sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F049.expected_back: A traffic-circle warning announces a roundabout ahead.

sec04-card-sec04-F050.front: Which three horizontal alignment changes can curve-family warning signs announce ahead?
sec04-card-sec04-F050.expected_back: Warnings can identify a sharp turn, a curve or a winding road ahead.

sec04-card-sec04-F051.front: What pavement risk does a Slippery When Wet warning sign highlight?
sec04-card-sec04-F051.expected_back: A Slippery When Wet warning alerts drivers to reduced traction when the roadway is wet.

sec04-card-sec04-F052.front: Why can a school-crossing warning sign appear several blocks away from the school building itself?
sec04-card-sec04-F052.expected_back: A school-crossing warning can be located several blocks from the school because it marks where children cross.

sec04-card-sec04-F053.front: What speed limit does the Mississippi manual set when passing a school during recess or arrival and dismissal?
sec04-card-sec04-F053.expected_back: When passing a school during recess or as children arrive or leave for opening or closing, the handbook gives a fifteen-mile-per-hour limit.

sec04-card-sec04-F054.front: How do painted stripes affect pedestrian right-of-way at Mississippi intersections?
sec04-card-sec04-F054.memory_hook: Pedestrians hold priority painted or not
sec04-card-sec04-F054.expected_back: Pedestrians have right of way at intersections whether or not a crosswalk is painted.

sec04-card-sec04-F055.front: What must drivers do if they remain in a lane marked by a mandatory-exit sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F055.expected_back: A mandatory-exit lane sign requires vehicles in that lane to continue onto the exit.

sec04-card-sec04-F056.front: What dangerous intersection setup is flagged by a plaque warning that cross traffic does not stop?
sec04-card-sec04-F056.expected_back: A stop-sign warning about cross traffic not stopping means the intersection is not an all-way stop and other lanes retain right of way.

sec04-card-sec04-F057.front: Which three highway networks are distinguished by numbered route marker shapes?
sec04-card-sec04-F057.expected_back: Route markers distinguish interstate highways, United States highways and state highways.

sec04-card-sec04-F058.front: What two navigation facts do destination, direction, and distance signs give highway drivers?
sec04-card-sec04-F058.expected_back: Destination, direction and distance signs help drivers identify towns and cities and the distance remaining to them.

sec04-card-sec04-F059.front: What specific spot does an interstate exit guide sign mark for motorists?
sec04-card-sec04-F059.expected_back: An interstate exit guide identifies a place to leave the highway.

sec04-card-sec04-F060.front: What background color, symbol color, and two common shapes identify work-zone signs?
sec04-card-sec04-F060.expected_back: Work-zone signs often use orange backgrounds with black words or symbols and rectangular or diamond shapes.

sec04-card-sec04-F061.front: Which five specific conditions can orange work-zone warnings alert you to ahead?
sec04-card-sec04-F061.expected_back: Work-zone warnings may identify workers, lower speeds, detours, slow equipment or surfaces that change abruptly.

sec04-card-sec04-F062.front: What three driving adjustments protect you and crews inside a work zone?
sec04-card-sec04-F062.expected_back: Reduce speed in work zones, allow for sudden stops and avoid following too closely.

sec04-card-sec04-F063.front: Which three traffic commands from a work-zone flagger are you legally required to obey?
sec04-card-sec04-F063.expected_back: Obey a work-zone flagger’s directions about travel, slowing and stopping.

sec04-card-sec04-F064.front: What two jobs do orange drums, cones, and vertical panels perform around road work?
sec04-card-sec04-F064.expected_back: Drums, cones and panels guide vehicles around work hazards and may block closed or unsafe road areas.

sec04-card-sec04-F065.front: Where must you stop when a temporary traffic signal controls a work zone?
sec04-card-sec04-F065.expected_back: Temporary traffic signals can control a work zone; stop at the white stop line when one is present.

sec04-card-sec04-F066.front: What colors and shape form the slow-moving-vehicle emblem, and which vehicles mount it on back?
sec04-card-sec04-F066.expected_back: The slow-moving-vehicle emblem is an orange-and-red triangle displayed at the rear of vehicles such as farm equipment or animal-drawn vehicles.

sec04-card-sec04-F067.front: When and on what type of roads should you stay especially alert for slow-moving vehicles?
sec04-card-sec04-F067.expected_back: Watch for slow-moving vehicles in daylight and darkness, particularly on rural roads.

sec04-card-sec04-F068.front: What must you confirm before pulling out to overtake a slow-moving vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F068.expected_back: Before overtaking a slow-moving vehicle, confirm that passing is safe and proceed carefully.

sec04-card-sec04-F069.front: Which two movements by farm machinery should you watch for on rural state highways?
sec04-card-sec04-F069.expected_back: Watch for farm machinery both crossing roads and traveling along rural state highways.

sec04-card-sec04-F070.front: Why must you pass farm machinery with extra caution even on a straight rural stretch?
sec04-card-sec04-F070.expected_back: A farm-machine operator may not hear an approaching vehicle, so pass cautiously.

sec04-card-sec04-F071.front: How do roadway rights and traffic duties apply to horse riders and animal-drawn vehicles?
sec04-card-sec04-F071.expected_back: Animal-drawn vehicles and horse riders have the same roadway-use rights and must follow the same traffic rules as motor vehicles.

sec04-card-sec04-F072.front: Which two loud car actions must you avoid when passing horses or animal-drawn vehicles?
sec04-card-sec04-F072.expected_back: Pass horses and animal-drawn vehicles carefully, avoiding horn use or engine revving that could frighten the horse.

sec04-card-sec04-F073.front: What turning move should you anticipate before overtaking an animal-drawn vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F073.expected_back: Expect animal-drawn vehicles to turn left toward fields or driveways.

sec04-card-sec04-F074.front: How do rural highways alert drivers ahead of time where horses and buggies travel often?
sec04-card-sec04-F074.expected_back: Warning signs may identify areas where horses and animal-drawn vehicles are likely, so remain alert.

sec02-card-sec02-F001.front: Which two separate braking systems must every Mississippi motor vehicle carry?
sec02-card-sec02-F001.expected_back: A vehicle needs both a foot-operated brake and a parking brake.

sec02-card-sec02-F002.front: Within how many feet must your foot brake stop the vehicle from twenty miles per hour?
sec02-card-sec02-F002.expected_back: At twenty miles per hour, the foot brake must stop the vehicle within thirty feet.

sec02-card-sec02-F003.front: Within how many feet must the parking brake be able to stop a vehicle from twenty miles per hour?
sec02-card-sec02-F003.expected_back: The parking brake must be capable of stopping the vehicle within fifty-five feet from twenty miles per hour.

sec02-card-sec02-F004.front: From at least what distance must a vehicle's horn be audible on Mississippi roads?
sec02-card-sec02-F004.expected_back: The vehicle’s horn must be audible at a distance of two hundred feet.

sec02-card-sec02-F005.front: Which three noise-making warning devices are prohibited on regular vehicles in Mississippi?
sec02-card-sec02-F005.expected_back: A vehicle may not carry a siren, exhaust whistle or spark whistle; the handbook prohibits noise-making devices.

sec02-card-sec02-F006.front: How many headlights and how many rear lights must a passenger vehicle have?
sec02-card-sec02-F006.expected_back: A passenger vehicle must have two headlights and at least one rear light.

sec02-card-sec02-F007.front: How far ahead does the manual recommend headlights reveal a person on a clear night?
sec02-card-sec02-F007.expected_back: For clear-weather night driving, the handbook recommends headlights that let you see a person five hundred feet ahead.

sec02-card-sec02-F008.front: What color must a vehicle's rear light shine, and from what distance behind must it show?
sec02-card-sec02-F008.expected_back: A vehicle’s rear light must shine red and be visible from five hundred feet behind it.

sec02-card-sec02-F009.front: Besides standard headlights, what is the maximum number of spotlights and auxiliary lights allowed?
sec02-card-sec02-F009.expected_back: Beyond the headlights, the vehicle may carry at most one spotlight and three auxiliary lights.

sec02-card-sec02-F010.front: Which two colors are illegal on spotlights and auxiliary vehicle lights?
sec02-card-sec02-F010.expected_back: Spotlights and auxiliary lights may not be red or blue.

sec02-card-sec02-F011.front: Not counting the headlights, how many extra lights at most should shine at the same time?
sec02-card-sec02-F011.expected_back: No more than four lights other than the headlights should be illuminated together.

sec02-card-sec02-F012.front: Why must your vehicle's muffler stay in working order at all times?
sec02-card-sec02-F012.expected_back: The muffler must remain operational to limit unusual or excessive noise and bothersome smoke.

sec02-card-sec02-F013.front: What rule governs muffler cutouts, bypasses, or similar exhaust-routing switches?
sec02-card-sec02-F013.expected_back: A muffler cutout, bypass or comparable device may not be used.

sec02-card-sec02-F014.front: How does the Mississippi manual treat an interior rearview mirror between recommendation and general mandate?
sec02-card-sec02-F014.expected_back: The handbook recommends a rearview mirror while stating that Mississippi does not generally require one.

sec02-card-sec02-F015.front: When is a truck legally required to carry a side mirror in Mississippi?
sec02-card-sec02-F015.expected_back: A truck needs a side mirror when its body prevents a view of the road behind.

sec02-card-sec02-F016.front: What equipment standard applies to a vehicle's windshield wipers?

sec02-card-sec02-F017.front: What inflation and surface standards must your tires meet to stay roadworthy?
sec02-card-sec02-F017.expected_back: Tires need appropriate inflation and sound tread without cuts, breaks or deterioration.

sec02-card-sec02-F018.front: What fender-height gap from suspension, frame, or chassis modifications makes a passenger vehicle illegal on Mississippi roads?
sec02-card-sec02-F018.expected_back: Mississippi prohibits driving a passenger vehicle on public streets or highways when suspension, frame or chassis alterations leave its front fender at least four inches higher than its rear fender.

sec02-card-sec02-F019.front: How is vertical fender height measured under Mississippi's vehicle-modification law?
sec02-card-sec02-F019.expected_back: Measure fender height vertically from the ground, through the wheel’s centerline, to the fender’s bottom edge.

sec02-card-sec02-F020.front: How does the manual define a vehicle fender and its practical job?
sec02-card-sec02-F020.expected_back: A fender is the shaped covering over a road wheel that reduces splashing from mud, water and similar material.

sec02-card-sec02-F021.front: When does the Mississippi manual classify a modified vehicle as squatted?
sec02-card-sec02-F021.expected_back: The handbook calls a vehicle squatted when the front fenders are at least four inches above the rear fenders, making it appear to rest on its rear tires.

sec02-card-sec02-F022.front: What tool should you use to verify tire inflation before heading out?
sec02-card-sec02-F022.expected_back: Use a pressure gauge to check tire inflation before driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F023.front: Which two places on or in your vehicle list the recommended tire inflation pressure?
sec02-card-sec02-F023.expected_back: Use the tire-pressure recommendation in the owner’s manual or on the driver-side door jamb.

sec02-card-sec02-F024.front: How often should you inspect your tires for wear and damage?
sec02-card-sec02-F024.expected_back: Inspect tires for damage and wear monthly and before a lengthy trip.

sec02-card-sec02-F025.front: What three driving tasks depend directly on maintaining clear vision?
sec02-card-sec02-F025.expected_back: Clear vision helps a driver identify road conditions and traffic, notice developing hazards and respond promptly.

sec02-card-sec02-F026.front: When must you wear your eyeglasses or contacts if corrective lenses are required for driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F026.expected_back: If corrective lenses are required for driving, wear them every time you drive.

sec02-card-sec02-F027.front: Which kind of corrective lenses should drivers avoid wearing at night?
sec02-card-sec02-F027.expected_back: Avoid dark or tinted corrective lenses during night driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F028.front: Which four triggers does the manual link to physical or mental driver fatigue?
sec02-card-sec02-F028.expected_back: Fatigue is physical or mental tiredness associated with strain, repetitive work, illness or insufficient sleep.

sec02-card-sec02-F029.front: Which two driving abilities suffer under fatigue, and what rule follows?
sec02-card-sec02-F029.expected_back: Fatigue may interfere with vision and slow decisions, so avoid driving while tired.

sec02-card-sec02-F030.front: How many hours of sleep does the manual say most people need for daytime alertness?
sec02-card-sec02-F030.expected_back: The handbook says most people need seven to nine hours of sleep for daytime alertness.

sec02-card-sec02-F031.front: How often should you schedule rest stops by distance or time during a long drive?
sec02-card-sec02-F031.expected_back: During a long trip, plan a stop roughly every hundred miles or two hours.

sec02-card-sec02-F032.front: How can bringing a passenger along help lower fatigue risk on a long trip?
sec02-card-sec02-F032.expected_back: A travel companion is one of the handbook’s suggestions for reducing fatigue risk on a trip.

sec02-card-sec02-F033.front: What should you inspect on prescription or over-the-counter medicine before driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F033.expected_back: Check medication labels for drowsiness warnings before driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F034.front: What is the manual's rule on driving after consuming alcohol or other drugs?
sec02-card-sec02-F034.expected_back: Do not drive after using alcohol or other drugs.

sec02-card-sec02-F035.front: What credential habit must you verify before pulling out, and what if an officer asks for it?
sec02-card-sec02-F035.expected_back: Carry your driver’s license before setting out, and present it when requested as required by state law.

sec02-card-sec02-F036.front: How should you position the driver's seat before putting the vehicle in motion?
sec02-card-sec02-F036.expected_back: Before moving, position the seat so the steering wheel and pedals are easy to reach.

sec02-card-sec02-F037.front: When should you fasten your seat belt for a drive?
sec02-card-sec02-F037.expected_back: Buckle the seat belt before driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F038.front: When and why must you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
sec02-card-sec02-F038.expected_back: Adjust the rearview and side mirrors before driving so you can monitor the roadway behind.

sec02-card-sec02-F039.front: Where on the steering wheel does the Mississippi manual place your hands for control?
sec02-card-sec02-F039.expected_back: For steering control, place your hands on opposite outside edges of the wheel at three and nine o’clock.

sec02-card-sec02-F040.front: Why does the manual warn against using the older two-and-ten steering hand position?
sec02-card-sec02-F040.expected_back: The handbook discourages the older two-and-ten hand position because of the hazard in vehicles equipped with airbags.

sec02-card-sec02-F041.front: How should your fingers and thumbs rest on the steering wheel?
sec02-card-sec02-F041.expected_back: Hold the wheel firmly but gently with the fingers, keeping the thumbs along its face.

sec02-card-sec02-F042.front: Which part of the steering wheel must you never grip from the inside to turn?
sec02-card-sec02-F042.expected_back: Do not turn the steering wheel with your hands gripping its inside edge.

sec02-card-sec02-F043.front: Where does the manual call for slower speed and extra caution because children may appear suddenly?
sec02-card-sec02-F043.expected_back: Slow down and use extra caution where children may walk, cycle or play, including schools, playgrounds and residential areas.

sec02-card-sec02-F044.front: What dangerous assumption must you avoid making when sharing lanes near a bicyclist?
sec02-card-sec02-F044.expected_back: Do not presume that a bicyclist has received bicycle-safety training.

sec02-card-sec02-F045.front: What sudden hazard should you scan parked cars along your lane for?
sec02-card-sec02-F045.expected_back: Watch parked cars for doors that may open into your lane.

sec02-card-sec02-F046.front: Why should you scan side driveways and bumpers for clues that another car is entering traffic?
sec02-card-sec02-F046.expected_back: Look for signs that another vehicle may enter traffic and be ready for abrupt turns or stops.

sec02-card-sec02-F047.front: What should you do whenever possible if a reckless driver bears down near you?
sec02-card-sec02-F047.expected_back: When possible, move out of a reckless driver’s way.

sec02-card-sec02-F048.front: Every how many miles should you take a break during long-distance highway driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F048.expected_back: On long trips, take a break every hundred miles.

sec02-card-sec02-F049.front: Why should you avoid trailing the same vehicle or cluster of cars for a long stretch?
sec02-card-sec02-F049.expected_back: Avoid following one vehicle or group for an extended period, because excessive relaxation can reduce concentration.

sec02-card-sec02-F050.front: Which two in-car habits keep your mind sharp during long-distance driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F050.expected_back: Keep scanning with your eyes and keep the cabin cool when driving long distances.

sec02-card-sec02-F051.front: Which three parts of your attention or body can a driving distraction pull off the road?
sec02-card-sec02-F051.expected_back: A driving distraction can draw your eyes, hands or mind away from the driving task.

sec02-card-sec02-F052.front: Which two mobile-phone activities does the manual advise every driver to avoid behind the wheel?
sec02-card-sec02-F052.expected_back: The handbook advises drivers to avoid both phone conversations and texting while driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F053.front: If an urgent phone call cannot wait while driving, what equipment does the manual recommend?
sec02-card-sec02-F053.expected_back: If a call must be made while driving, the handbook recommends a hands-free device.

sec02-card-sec02-F054.front: Which three actions involving a text message are prohibited while driving in Mississippi?
sec02-card-sec02-F054.expected_back: Writing, sending or reading a text message while driving is prohibited.

sec02-card-sec02-F055.front: What social-networking actions are illegal on a hand-held mobile phone while driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F055.expected_back: A driver may not use a hand-held mobile phone to read or post on a social-networking site.

sec02-card-sec02-F056.front: How does Mississippi's phone law define a hand-held mobile phone, and what devices are excluded?
sec02-card-sec02-F056.expected_back: A hand-held mobile phone is a phone or portable communication device used for a call or text interaction with at least one hand, excluding voice-operated and hands-free devices.

sec02-card-sec02-F057.front: How does the distracted-driving phone law define a covered motor vehicle?
sec02-card-sec02-F057.expected_back: The phone-use provision defines a motor vehicle as mechanically driven or drawn and manufactured mainly for public-highway use.

sec02-card-sec02-F058.front: Which three user features define a social-networking service under the Mississippi phone statute?
sec02-card-sec02-F058.expected_back: A social-networking service lets users build a profile, identify connections to other users and communicate with them.

sec02-card-sec02-F059.front: Which digital messages count as texts under the phone ban, and which alerts or functions are exempt?
sec02-card-sec02-F059.expected_back: For the phone-use provision, texts include instant messages, electronic messages and email, but exclude emergency, traffic or weather alerts and messages about operating or navigating the vehicle.

sec02-card-sec02-F060.front: What minimal hand touch is still permitted on a voice-operated or hands-free device?
sec02-card-sec02-F060.expected_back: A voice-operated or hands-free device permits text interaction without either hand, apart from starting, stopping or activating a function.

sec02-card-sec02-F061.front: How do the phone-use definitions translate writing, sending, and reading a text message?
sec02-card-sec02-F061.expected_back: The phone-use definitions treat writing, sending and reading as manually entering, transmitting and retrieving a text message.

sec02-card-sec02-F062.front: What should you do when anger, grief, fear, illness, worry, or an argument wrecks your focus?
sec02-card-sec02-F062.expected_back: Let another person drive if worry, illness, anger, fear, grief or an argument leaves you unable to concentrate safely.

sec02-card-sec02-F063.front: What kind of talk with passengers should you avoid while operating a vehicle?
sec02-card-sec02-F063.expected_back: Avoid arguments and emotionally stressful conversations with passengers.

sec02-card-sec02-F064.front: What does the Mississippi manual advise regarding eating behind the wheel?
sec02-card-sec02-F064.expected_back: You should avoid eating while driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F065.front: What must a driver verify before moving whenever children ride in the vehicle?
sec02-card-sec02-F065.expected_back: Make sure children are secured correctly and safely with their restraints.

sec02-card-sec02-F066.front: How does the manual say pets should travel inside a moving vehicle?
sec02-card-sec02-F066.expected_back: Transport pets securely in a carrier or portable kennel.

sec02-card-sec02-F067.front: Why must you skip stereo headphones and keep cabin music at a reasonable volume?
sec02-card-sec02-F067.expected_back: Do not wear stereo headphones or turn music up so loudly that you cannot hear warning sounds.

sec02-card-sec02-F068.front: What items must you keep off your vehicle's windshield?
sec02-card-sec02-F068.expected_back: Keep unofficial stickers and signs off the windshield.

sec02-card-sec02-F069.front: Which four window coverings or treatments are banned on Mississippi vehicle windows?
sec02-card-sec02-F069.expected_back: Vehicle windows may not carry signs, posters, stickers or glazing material that creates a mirrored effect.

sec02-card-sec02-F070.front: What does the manual advise about hanging air fresheners, tassels, or charms from the rearview mirror?
sec02-card-sec02-F070.expected_back: Avoid suspending decorations from the rearview mirror.

sec02-card-sec02-F071.front: Why should you clear loose bags, phones, or bottles off the front seat before driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F071.expected_back: Clear loose objects from the front seat so sudden movement will not make them fall.

sec01-card-sec01-F001.question_text: What credential is generally required to drive a motor vehicle on Mississippi streets and highways, and what is excluded?
sec01-card-sec01-F001.teaching_text: Driving any non-exempt motor vehicle on public pavement without a valid license or learner's permit violates state law.

sec01-card-sec01-F002.question_text: Does sitting beside a licensed driver or parent make it legal to drive without a permit or license?
sec01-card-sec01-F002.teaching_text: Even with a licensed parent riding shotgun, the person behind the wheel must hold at least a learner's permit.

sec01-card-sec01-F003.question_text: Which armed-forces vehicles can be driven in Mississippi without holding a Mississippi driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F003.teaching_text: Driving federal military rigs for an armed-forces branch qualifies for a state credential exemption, unlike your personal car.

sec01-card-sec01-F004.question_text: At what age may a nonresident drive in Mississippi using a valid home-state or home-country license?
sec01-card-sec01-F004.teaching_text: Visitors past age sixteen stay legal only while keeping their valid home-state or home-country license on them.

sec01-card-sec01-F005.question_text: Which types of road and farm machinery may operate on Mississippi streets and highways without a driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F005.teaching_text: Mississippi carves out road machines, farm tractors, and farm implements from standard motor-vehicle licensing on public roads.

sec01-card-sec01-F006.question_text: How does an active license suspension or revocation affect getting a Mississippi driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F006.teaching_text: You cannot bypass an active suspension or revocation by applying fresh until your driving privilege is cleared.

sec01-card-sec01-F007.question_text: Which two substance-related conditions listed in the manual prevent Mississippi from issuing a driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F007.teaching_text: Chronic alcohol intoxication or narcotic addiction disqualifies an applicant because ongoing impairment threatens everyone sharing the highway.

sec01-card-sec01-F008.question_text: When does a physical or mental health condition prevent Mississippi from issuing a driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F008.teaching_text: Any physical or mental impairment that conflicts with safe vehicle control bars issuance until safely managed or cleared.

sec01-card-sec01-F009.question_text: Which court-adjudicated mental status does the Mississippi manual list as preventing license issuance?
sec01-card-sec01-F009.teaching_text: Test questions check the exact statutory bars in chapter one, including an unreversed court adjudication of insanity.

sec01-card-sec01-F010.question_text: Within how many days after moving to Mississippi must a new resident obtain a Mississippi driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F010.teaching_text: Watch the split deadlines closely because newcomers get sixty days for their driver's license after moving in.

sec01-card-sec01-F011.question_text: Within how many days after moving to Mississippi must you get a Mississippi license plate or tag?
sec01-card-sec01-F011.teaching_text: DMV distractors swap the two newcomer clocks, since your car's tag is due in thirty days while licensing allows sixty.

sec01-card-sec01-F012.question_text: What must you do with driver's licenses from other states when applying for a Mississippi license?
sec01-card-sec01-F012.teaching_text: Holding active driver's licenses from two states at once is banned, so prior cards get turned in.

sec01-card-sec01-F013.question_text: What must you submit if your out-of-state license is lost when applying for a Mississippi license?
sec01-card-sec01-F013.teaching_text: When you cannot hand over a lost plastic card, a notarized Affidavit of Inability to Surrender closes the gap.

sec01-card-sec01-F014.question_text: What record check does Mississippi run on applicants before issuing a state driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F014.teaching_text: Moving across state lines never erases unpaid tickets or suspensions because Mississippi screens out-of-state driving records first.

sec01-card-sec01-F015.question_text: Which requirement drops and which stays when you transfer a valid out-of-state driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F015.teaching_text: A current out-of-state license excuses computerized knowledge testing, yet every transferring driver still completes vision screening.

sec01-card-sec01-F016.question_text: How long past expiration does an out-of-state license lose its waiver and require computerized testing?
sec01-card-sec01-F016.teaching_text: Letting your former state's card sit expired beyond thirty days costs your waiver and puts computerized testing back.

sec01-card-sec01-F017.question_text: Which three document categories must an out-of-state applicant bring for a Mississippi license or ID?
sec01-card-sec01-F017.teaching_text: Showing up without a certified state birth record, original Social Security proof, and two residency papers stalls your visit.

sec01-card-sec01-F018.question_text: How long after discharge or returning to Mississippi may a service member renew a license that expired away?
sec01-card-sec01-F018.teaching_text: Active duty outside Mississippi pauses expiration penalties, giving returning service members ninety days after discharge or return.

sec01-card-sec01-F019.question_text: What document proves military absence and discharge or return for the ninety-day military renewal rule?
sec01-card-sec01-F019.teaching_text: Filing an affidavit that confirms military service plus your discharge or state return unlocks the ninety-day renewal protection.

sec01-card-sec01-F020.question_text: How are delinquency fees and testing handled during a qualifying post-service military renewal?
sec01-card-sec01-F020.teaching_text: Qualifying service members skip both late fees and retesting unless the department has reason to question eligibility.

sec01-card-sec01-F021.question_text: How far ahead of expiration may an eligible driver renew a Mississippi license?
sec01-card-sec01-F021.teaching_text: Renewing up to six months before your birthday deadline keeps travel plans and work schedules free from expired-card headaches.

sec01-card-sec01-F022.question_text: May nonresident service members and their dependents drive in Mississippi on valid licenses from another state?
sec01-card-sec01-F022.teaching_text: Stationed military personnel and family members keep nonresident privilege as long as their home-state credentials remain valid.

sec01-card-sec01-F023.question_text: Can out-of-state college students drive in Mississippi using their home state's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F023.teaching_text: Attending a Mississippi college from out of state lets students keep driving on valid home-state credentials.

sec01-card-sec01-F024.question_text: What vehicle item shares the same out-of-state exemption given to military families and college students?
sec01-card-sec01-F024.teaching_text: Military families and visiting college students do not have to swap their valid out-of-state vehicle tags either.

sec01-card-sec01-F025.question_text: Which two credential actions may military personnel and college students complete online?
sec01-card-sec01-F025.teaching_text: Online renewal and replacement keep stationed troops and away-from-home students legal without traveling back to an office.

sec01-card-sec01-F026.question_text: Which standard licensing requirement is waived when a noncitizen applies in Mississippi?
sec01-card-sec01-F026.teaching_text: Noncitizens meet every regular licensing requirement except presenting a Social Security card when applying.

sec01-card-sec01-F027.question_text: What two immigration pathways qualify a noncitizen to seek a regular Mississippi license?
sec01-card-sec01-F027.teaching_text: Applicants must prove either permanent-resident status or valid immigration paperwork showing their authorized United States stay.

sec01-card-sec01-F028.question_text: Which three immigration document combinations does Mississippi accept for an original noncitizen license or ID?
sec01-card-sec01-F028.teaching_text: Counter staff verify original permanent-resident cards, or else pair your foreign passport with valid immigration papers or an arrival record.

sec01-card-sec01-F029.question_text: Besides immigration papers, what birth-record format and residency count must an original noncitizen applicant bring?
sec01-card-sec01-F029.teaching_text: Foreign birth certificates require a university translation alongside two Mississippi residency documents before staff issue an original card.

sec01-card-sec01-F030.question_text: What must a noncitizen bring when renewing an existing Mississippi license or ID card?
sec01-card-sec01-F030.teaching_text: Renewing noncitizens present updated immigration status paperwork together with their existing Mississippi license or ID.

sec01-card-sec01-F031.question_text: How long does a noncitizen's regular Mississippi license or ID remain valid?
sec01-card-sec01-F031.teaching_text: Card expiration stops at four years or the end date of authorized stay, whichever arrives sooner.

sec01-card-sec01-F032.question_text: Does a noncitizen pay a reduced fee when lawful status makes the license valid for less than four years?
sec01-card-sec01-F032.teaching_text: Test writers dangle prorated discounts, yet Mississippi charges the regular license fee even on shortened validity terms.

sec01-card-sec01-F033.question_text: How does the computerized testing requirement for a regular learner's permit compare to a regular driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F033.teaching_text: Beginners take the exact same computerized multiple-choice screening for a learner's permit as for a regular license.

sec01-card-sec01-F034.question_text: How long does a passing computerized examination score remain valid in Mississippi?
sec01-card-sec01-F034.teaching_text: Knowing your computerized result holds for two years helps you time permit practice and license advancement cleanly.

sec01-card-sec01-F035.question_text: How can a permit holder advance within the two-year window without retaking computerized testing?
sec01-card-sec01-F035.teaching_text: Filing the affidavit for fifty observed driving hours and safe proficiency within two years skips repeating computerized testing.

sec01-card-sec01-F036.question_text: What happens if you wait longer than two years after passing before advancing from your permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F036.teaching_text: Once the two-year window closes on your passing result, you must sit for computerized testing all over again.

sec01-card-sec01-F037.question_text: Which school-related affidavit is required when upgrading from a learner's permit to a regular license?
sec01-card-sec01-F037.teaching_text: Forgetting your School Attendance Affidavit at upgrade time turns away otherwise ready teen drivers at the counter.

sec01-card-sec01-F038.question_text: What is the minimum age to apply for a regular learner's permit in Mississippi?
sec01-card-sec01-F038.teaching_text: Turning fifteen opens the door to a regular learner's permit so supervised driving hours can begin.

sec01-card-sec01-F039.question_text: How long must a learner normally hold a permit before licensing, and what birthday overrides that wait?
sec01-card-sec01-F039.teaching_text: Normally you hold a permit one full year, yet turning seventeen lets you apply before twelve months finish.

sec01-card-sec01-F040.question_text: After how much time does a Mississippi regular learner's permit expire?
sec01-card-sec01-F040.teaching_text: A regular learner's permit stays active for two years, matching the two-year lifespan of your computerized score.

sec01-card-sec01-F041.question_text: Who must sit in the seat right beside a Mississippi learner's permit holder while driving?
sec01-card-sec01-F041.teaching_text: Putting a twenty-one-plus licensed supervisor in the back seat or driving with an eighteen-year-old buddy breaks permit law.

sec01-card-sec01-F042.question_text: What happens to your license if you need glasses or special equipment to pass licensing checks?
sec01-card-sec01-F042.teaching_text: Qualifying with corrective lenses or adaptive gear adds a mandatory restriction requiring that aid whenever you drive.

sec01-card-sec01-F043.question_text: Besides required identity and residency documents, which two checks must a Class R license applicant pass?
sec01-card-sec01-F043.teaching_text: Every regular Class R license applicant brings required paperwork and clears both written knowledge and vision checks.

sec01-card-sec01-F044.question_text: What three age or prior-credential paths make an applicant eligible for a Class R regular license?
sec01-card-sec01-F044.teaching_text: You qualify at sixteen after a one-year permit, upon turning seventeen, or after six months licensed out of state.

sec01-card-sec01-F045.question_text: Besides age and paperwork, what two personal factors can affect Class R license eligibility?
sec01-card-sec01-F045.teaching_text: Class R applicants still have to meet physical standards, and certain traffic or legal convictions can block eligibility.

sec01-card-sec01-F046.question_text: What road-waiver affidavit must a Class R applicant younger than seventeen provide?
sec01-card-sec01-F046.teaching_text: Applicants under seventeen submit a road-waiver affidavit certifying at least fifty observed driving hours and safe skill.

sec01-card-sec01-F047.question_text: When does a teen who gets a learner's permit at fifteen and a half qualify under the one-year route?
sec01-card-sec01-F047.teaching_text: Turning sixteen alone is not enough when your permit started at fifteen and a half; twelve full months must pass.

sec01-card-sec01-F048.question_text: What credential do you get first if you start applying at age sixteen, and when can you upgrade?
sec01-card-sec01-F048.teaching_text: Beginning at sixteen still starts with a learner's permit before advancing to the regular license at age seventeen.

sec01-card-sec01-F049.question_text: What shortcut applies if you begin the licensing process at age seventeen or older?
sec01-card-sec01-F049.teaching_text: Beginners aged seventeen and up skip holding a learner's permit and sit computerized testing for a regular license same day.

sec01-card-sec01-F050.question_text: When must you have your Mississippi driver's license in your possession?
sec01-card-sec01-F050.teaching_text: Leaving your plastic credential in another jacket while driving still counts as operating without a license on hand.

sec01-card-sec01-F051.question_text: Which agency division supplies the form used to apply for a Mississippi driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F051.teaching_text: Handwritten notes or outside printouts never count because every applicant starts on the standard bureau application sheet.

sec01-card-sec01-F052.question_text: Which four personal identity items must be entered on a Mississippi license application?
sec01-card-sec01-F052.teaching_text: Incomplete legal names or missing Social Security numbers stall processing before your application ever reaches vision screening.

sec01-card-sec01-F053.question_text: Besides basic identity fields, what three background details must a license application include?
sec01-card-sec01-F053.teaching_text: Reviewers check physical traits, medical and mental background, and prior driving experience to spot safety risks before issuing credentials.

sec01-card-sec01-F054.question_text: What residency proof rule applies to an original-license applicant aged eighteen or older?
sec01-card-sec01-F054.teaching_text: Post-office boxes never prove where you sleep, so adult original applicants need two documents showing a physical street address.

sec01-card-sec01-F055.question_text: Up to what age cutoff may an applicant rely on a parent's residency documentation?
sec01-card-sec01-F055.teaching_text: Young adults under twenty-one often have no utility bills in their own name, so parent residence papers qualify.

sec01-card-sec01-F056.question_text: Which household or banking papers prove residency, and which common checkbook item is rejected?
sec01-card-sec01-F056.teaching_text: Utility bills, bank statements, leases, and mortgages verify residence, while a blank check gets rejected at the counter.

sec01-card-sec01-F057.question_text: What three requirements must an employer's residency letter meet to count for licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F057.teaching_text: An unnotarized note or missing employer phone number disqualifies a workplace residency verification letter.

sec01-card-sec01-F058.question_text: Whose Mississippi driver's license can help prove residency for an applicant younger than twenty-one?
sec01-card-sec01-F058.teaching_text: Applicants under twenty-one can present a parent's or legal guardian's Mississippi driver's license among residency proofs.

sec01-card-sec01-F059.question_text: Which two foundational identification documents are required on the license and permit application page?
sec01-card-sec01-F059.teaching_text: Unverified photocopies get turned away at the counter because standard applicants must bring certified birth proof and Social Security documentation.

sec01-card-sec01-F060.question_text: What must you do before applying if your Social Security card is lost or missing?
sec01-card-sec01-F060.teaching_text: Showing up hoping to recite your digits from memory fails because you must replace a missing card beforehand.

sec01-card-sec01-F061.question_text: Alongside identity and residency proofs, what must a current out-of-state license holder turn in?
sec01-card-sec01-F061.teaching_text: Every transferring driver produces either the physical out-of-state card or a notarized lost-license affidavit.

sec01-card-sec01-F062.question_text: Who must bring school enrollment proof, and how recent must that attendance certification be?
sec01-card-sec01-F062.teaching_text: Grabbing a school attendance form before summer break backfires once the paper passes its strict thirty-day freshness limit.

sec01-card-sec01-F063.question_text: Where does a home-schooled teen get the attendance form, and who signs it?
sec01-card-sec01-F063.teaching_text: Home-schooled applicants download the attendance certification from the Department of Public Safety website for a parent signature.

sec01-card-sec01-F064.question_text: What document may a married applicant younger than eighteen substitute for school attendance certification?
sec01-card-sec01-F064.teaching_text: Mississippi lets married applicants under eighteen present their marriage license in place of a school attendance form.

sec01-card-sec01-F065.question_text: What penalty can follow making a false statement on your signed Mississippi license application?
sec01-card-sec01-F065.teaching_text: Fudging age, residency, or prior suspensions on a signed application can trigger suspension of your driving privileges.

sec01-card-sec01-F066.question_text: When does an applicant younger than seventeen need signatures from both parents?
sec01-card-sec01-F066.teaching_text: One parent signing alone falls short for an under-seventeen applicant whenever both parents are living and share custody.

sec01-card-sec01-F067.question_text: Who signs for an under-seventeen applicant when both parents are not alive or lack joint custody?
sec01-card-sec01-F067.teaching_text: When the two-parent custody rule cannot be met, Mississippi shifts signing authority to a legal guardian or employer.

sec01-card-sec01-F068.question_text: Who may sign a minor's application if there is no custodial parent, legal guardian, or employer?
sec01-card-sec01-F068.teaching_text: Any responsible adult willing to assume the legal liability obligations may sign when no parent, guardian, or employer exists.

sec01-card-sec01-F069.question_text: What financial risk does an adult cosigner accept, and how must their signature be verified?
sec01-card-sec01-F069.teaching_text: Cosigning a minor's application carries legal liability for negligent or willful driving misconduct and requires notarization.

sec01-card-sec01-F070.question_text: How can an adult who signed a minor's application later revoke their consent and end that credential?
sec01-card-sec01-F070.teaching_text: Parents or cosigners are never locked in permanently and can file a verified written request canceling the teen's permit.

sec01-card-sec01-F071.question_text: Which three main subject areas from the Mississippi driver's manual anchor computerized testing?
sec01-card-sec01-F071.teaching_text: Studying random trivia wastes time when computerized screening focuses squarely on state traffic laws, safe driving, and licensing.

sec01-card-sec01-F072.question_text: Which four practical driving areas and attitudes are evaluated by the Mississippi examination?
sec01-card-sec01-F072.teaching_text: Beyond memorizing speeds, applicants must know signs and signals, safe vehicle condition, road-user courtesy, and personal fitness.

sec01-card-sec01-F073.question_text: What does Mississippi's vision examination verify before you receive driving privileges?
sec01-card-sec01-F073.teaching_text: Clear distance sight is non-negotiable for reading highway signs and spotting hazards early enough to brake.

sec01-card-sec01-F074.question_text: When might an applicant need a medical certificate before sitting for licensing checks?
sec01-card-sec01-F074.teaching_text: Applicants treated by a physician for a physical or mental condition may need medical clearance before testing.

sec01-card-sec01-F075.question_text: What happens if your licensing vision screening indicates that you need eyeglasses?
sec01-card-sec01-F075.teaching_text: Staff refer you to an optometrist or eye specialist to examine your eyes and complete vision form DE26.

sec01-card-sec01-F076.question_text: What two accommodations help a reading-impaired applicant prepare for and complete computerized testing?
sec01-card-sec01-F076.teaching_text: Reading-impaired applicants can prepare alongside a study helper and listen through the station headset during computerized testing.

sec01-card-sec01-F077.question_text: How does the Mississippi manual define the format of its computerized licensing examination?
sec01-card-sec01-F077.teaching_text: Knowing the computerized session uses multiple-choice items lets you practice spotting subtle rule distractors ahead of time.

sec01-card-sec01-F078.question_text: In the Mississippi driver's manual definitions, what roadways count as a highway?
sec01-card-sec01-F078.teaching_text: Many beginners picture only fast interstates, yet statutory highway rules cover neighborhood municipal streets and public roadways too.

sec01-card-sec01-F079.question_text: How does the manual define an intersection, and what pedestrian zone is included inside it?
sec01-card-sec01-F079.teaching_text: Stopping on a crosswalk already puts your bumper inside the legal intersection where roads join or cross.

sec01-card-sec01-F080.question_text: Which four types of vehicles are excluded from the manual's definition of a motor vehicle?
sec01-card-sec01-F080.teaching_text: Exam distractors test those four statutory carve-outs, separating trains, electric bikes, golf carts, and neighborhood low-speed rides from standard cars.

sec01-card-sec01-F081.question_text: How do the glossary terms nonresident and operator differ in the Mississippi manual?
sec01-card-sec01-F081.teaching_text: Nonresident describes someone living outside Mississippi, whereas operator identifies whoever is actively driving on the highway.

sec01-card-sec01-F082.question_text: How does the Mississippi manual define the phrase right of way?
sec01-card-sec01-F082.teaching_text: Right of way means legal priority to use that piece of roadway immediately, though safety still beats stubbornness.

sec01-card-sec01-F083.question_text: Under the manual's definition, must a school bus be publicly owned to count as a school bus?
sec01-card-sec01-F083.teaching_text: Privately operated buses paid to carry students to and from school carry the same school-bus status as public ones.

sec01-card-sec01-F084.question_text: What does the legal definition of a stop require of your vehicle?
sec01-card-sec01-F084.teaching_text: Slowing to a two-mile-per-hour creep fails the definition because a lawful stop requires all wheel movement to end.

sec01-card-sec01-F085.question_text: Besides motor vehicles, which other highway users are included inside the manual's definition of traffic?
sec01-card-sec01-F085.teaching_text: Pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, and streetcars all count as legal traffic sharing highway rights and duties.

sec01-card-sec01-F086.question_text: Which three personal habits form the core of defensive driving in the Mississippi manual?
sec01-card-sec01-F086.teaching_text: Practicing courtesy, self-control, and equal respect toward walkers and fellow motorists defuses road rage and prevents crashes.

sec03-card-sec03-F001.question_text: Which three types of highway pavement markings guide traffic that drivers are required to obey?
sec03-card-sec03-F001.teaching_text: Painted stripes and directional arrows carry full legal force, organizing lanes and intersection turns without words.

sec03-card-sec03-F002.question_text: What traffic directions are separated by a single broken yellow center line?
sec03-card-sec03-F002.teaching_text: Yellow paint down the center always warns that the lane beside yours carries oncoming headlights.

sec03-card-sec03-F003.question_text: Under what two conditions may you cross a broken yellow center line into the opposing lane?
sec03-card-sec03-F003.teaching_text: Drifting across dashed yellow without clear sight distance invites a head-on collision with oncoming traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F004.question_text: What kind of traffic flow runs on both sides of a broken white lane line?
sec03-card-sec03-F004.teaching_text: White lane dashes confirm neighboring lanes travel with you rather than coming head-on.

sec03-card-sec03-F005.question_text: When are you allowed to move across a broken white pavement line?
sec03-card-sec03-F005.teaching_text: Dashed white lines permit changing lanes once mirrors, signals, and blind-spot checks confirm an open gap.

sec03-card-sec03-F006.question_text: What traffic streams are divided when a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line run side by side?
sec03-card-sec03-F006.teaching_text: Whenever yellow stripes pair up down the middle, lanes on opposite sides carry two-way opposing vehicles.

sec03-card-sec03-F007.question_text: On a road with paired solid and broken yellow lines, what may drivers on the broken-line side do?
sec03-card-sec03-F007.teaching_text: Having the dashed stripe closest to your tires grants passing permission only when oncoming sight distance is clear.

sec03-card-sec03-F008.question_text: What is the passing rule when the solid stripe of paired yellow lines sits next to your lane?
sec03-card-sec03-F008.teaching_text: Hills or curves hide oncoming cars from your side, so crossing when solid yellow hugs your lane is illegal.

sec03-card-sec03-F009.question_text: What two rules do double solid yellow center lines establish?
sec03-card-sec03-F009.teaching_text: Two solid yellow stripes lock down overtaking in both directions where sightlines or traffic make passing unsafe.

sec03-card-sec03-F010.question_text: What lanes do paired solid white lines separate, and may you cross them?
sec03-card-sec03-F010.teaching_text: DMV questions contrast single and double white lines because paired solid white stripes prohibit lane changes outright.

sec03-card-sec03-F011.question_text: What does a single solid white line between lanes mean about lane flow and changing lanes?
sec03-card-sec03-F011.teaching_text: Single solid white marks turn pockets or tricky approaches where weaving across lanes is discouraged for safety.

sec03-card-sec03-F012.question_text: What do white directional arrows painted inside an approach lane tell drivers?
sec03-card-sec03-F012.teaching_text: Reading painted lane arrows early lets you line up turns or straight travel before solid stripes lock lanes.

sec03-card-sec03-F013.question_text: What should you do if you accidentally enter a turn-arrow lane you did not mean to take?
sec03-card-sec03-F013.teaching_text: Jerking out of a turn-only pocket at the last second sideswipes neighboring lanes, so complete the marked turn.

sec03-card-sec03-F014.question_text: What movement is required when your lane carries a painted left-only arrow?
sec03-card-sec03-F014.teaching_text: Driving straight out of a dedicated left-turn bay cuts right across neighboring through traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F015.question_text: What movement is required in a lane marked with a straight-only pavement arrow?
sec03-card-sec03-F015.teaching_text: Turning from a straight-only lane surprises drivers turning legally from adjacent turn bays.

sec03-card-sec03-F016.question_text: What must every driver do when positioned in a lane with a right-only pavement arrow?
sec03-card-sec03-F016.teaching_text: Continuing straight through an intersection from a right-only pocket collides with curb tapers or turning lanes.

sec03-card-sec03-F017.question_text: Which two movements are legal from a pavement arrow showing both straight and left branches?
sec03-card-sec03-F017.teaching_text: Dual-headed straight-and-left arrows let drivers continue ahead or signal a left turn from the same lane.

sec03-card-sec03-F018.question_text: Which two movements are permitted by a pavement arrow with straight and right branches?
sec03-card-sec03-F018.teaching_text: Drivers in a combined straight-and-right lane may proceed ahead or signal and turn right cleanly.

sec03-card-sec03-F019.question_text: What overtaking move is illegal inside a shared center turn-only lane?
sec03-card-sec03-F019.teaching_text: Opposing drivers enter shared center lanes to turn left, turning illegal passing maneuvers into head-on traps.

sec03-card-sec03-F020.question_text: Where besides street intersections can painted pedestrian crosswalks appear?
sec03-card-sec03-F020.teaching_text: Campuses, shopping districts, and parks paint midblock crosswalks wherever foot traffic crosses regularly.

sec03-card-sec03-F021.question_text: Where must your vehicle never come to a stop when approaching a pedestrian crosswalk?
sec03-card-sec03-F021.teaching_text: Stopping even your front bumper across crosswalk paint forces walkers out into live moving traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F022.question_text: What safety check does the manual tell pedestrians to make before stepping into a crosswalk?
sec03-card-sec03-F022.teaching_text: Right-of-way laws never bend physics, so walkers still scan left and right before leaving the curb.

sec03-card-sec03-F023.question_text: Must drivers yield to pedestrians in an intersection crosswalk when no white lines are painted?
sec03-card-sec03-F023.teaching_text: Exam questions bait beginners with unpainted corners, yet unmarked intersection crosswalks carry full pedestrian right-of-way.

sec05-card-sec05-F001.question_text: How should you approach every railroad crossing regarding its signs and road markings?
sec05-card-sec05-F001.teaching_text: Trains cannot swerve and take up to a mile to stop, so catching early crossing clues prevents deadly surprises.

sec05-card-sec05-F002.question_text: What does a large painted X flanked by two R letters on your lane mean?
sec05-card-sec05-F002.teaching_text: Spotting painted rail letters on the asphalt gives your foot an early cue to cover the brake before tracks appear.

sec05-card-sec05-F003.question_text: Near railroad tracks, what does the solid yellow line forbid, and what color marks the track approaches?
sec05-card-sec05-F003.teaching_text: Pulling out to pass near tracks blocks your view of crossbucks, gates, and oncoming locomotives.

sec05-card-sec05-F004.question_text: What shape, color, and black symbols appear on the advance railroad warning sign?
sec05-card-sec05-F004.teaching_text: Test questions pair sign shapes with meanings—a yellow circle belongs exclusively to railroad advance warning.

sec05-card-sec05-F005.question_text: On rural roads, how many feet ahead of the tracks does the railroad advance-warning sign usually sit?
sec05-card-sec05-F005.teaching_text: Country highway speeds eat pavement fast, so rural warnings start well back to give smooth braking room.

sec05-card-sec05-F006.question_text: Which three immediate actions does a railroad advance-warning sign tell you to take, and why?
sec05-card-sec05-F006.teaching_text: Quiet rural crossings often lack gates, making your own eyes, ears, and reduced speed the primary defense.

sec05-card-sec05-F007.question_text: What white sign marks most rail crossings, and how does it warn of multiple tracks?
sec05-card-sec05-F007.teaching_text: Reading a multi-track number plaque warns you that a second hidden train could follow right behind the first.

sec05-card-sec05-F008.question_text: What must you do the moment railroad crossing lights begin flashing?
sec05-card-sec05-F008.teaching_text: Trying to beat freshly triggered red flashers misjudges deceptive locomotive closing speed.

sec05-card-sec05-F009.question_text: At an ungated crossing with flashing lights, when may you start rolling across again?
sec05-card-sec05-F009.teaching_text: Rolling forward after one caboose passes while lights still flash walks straight into a second train.

sec05-card-sec05-F010.question_text: At a crossing equipped with gates, when must you bring your vehicle to a stop?
sec05-card-sec05-F010.teaching_text: Darting onto tracks while warning lights flash risks getting trapped between descending gate arms.

sec05-card-sec05-F011.question_text: At a gated railroad crossing, which two conditions must finish before you drive forward?
sec05-card-sec05-F011.teaching_text: Starting early while gates are still lifting or bells still flash risks clipping the arm or missing a second train.

sec05-card-sec05-F012.question_text: Which three categories of vehicles must stop at every railroad crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-F012.teaching_text: Trailing too closely behind a school bus or fuel tanker invites a rear-end crash when it halts at clear tracks.

sec05-card-sec05-F013.question_text: Once a required-stop vehicle halts at railroad tracks, what check comes before pulling forward?
sec05-card-sec05-F013.teaching_text: Stopping is useless unless the driver actively checks left and right down the rails before accelerating.

sec05-card-sec05-F014.question_text: What is the number-one survival rule if your vehicle stalls or gets stuck on railroad tracks?
sec05-card-sec05-F014.teaching_text: Sheet metal can be replaced by insurance, whereas staying inside to crank a dead starter turns fatal in seconds.

sec05-card-sec05-F015.question_text: If crossing lights flash while your car sits stuck on tracks, which direction and angle should you run?
sec05-card-sec05-F015.teaching_text: Running away from tracks angled toward the oncoming train keeps flying car wreckage moving past behind you.

sec05-card-sec05-F016.question_text: Right after escaping a car stuck on tracks with warning lights flashing, whom do you call?
sec05-card-sec05-F016.teaching_text: With warning lights already active, a train is seconds away—emergency dispatch coordinates immediate rescue and rail alerts.

sec05-card-sec05-F017.question_text: If your car stalls on tracks with no warning lights flashing, which two numbers do you call after exiting?
sec05-card-sec05-F017.teaching_text: Calling both nine-one-one and the blue rail Emergency Notification System plaque gives dispatchers time to halt distant trains.

sec05-card-sec05-F018.question_text: Which four facts must you give when reporting a vehicle stuck on railroad tracks?
sec05-card-sec05-F018.teaching_text: Pinpointing the exact crossing number and cross street lets railroad dispatchers stop the right train on the right line.

sec05-card-sec05-F019.question_text: Which five crossing warnings legally require every driver to stop before railroad tracks?
sec05-card-sec05-F019.teaching_text: Any single one of those five cues—even without lowered gates—makes crossing unlawful and life-threatening.

sec05-card-sec05-F020.question_text: Does the legal duty to stop at triggered rail warnings vanish if you can't see a train?
sec05-card-sec05-F020.teaching_text: Curves, trees, fog, or parked boxcars can hide a fast-moving locomotive until it hits the crossing.

sec05-card-sec05-F021.question_text: Which three conditions must all be true before pulling forward from a railroad stop?
sec05-card-sec05-F021.teaching_text: Confirming every parallel track is empty alongside raised gates and dark signals prevents hidden second-train collisions.

sec05-card-sec05-F022.question_text: Is weaving around a lowered railroad crossing gate ever legal?
sec05-card-sec05-F022.teaching_text: Zigzagging past lowered gates is both a serious traffic crime and a leading cause of fatal rail crashes.

sec05-card-sec05-F023.question_text: Why must you leave extra space behind buses and tankers approaching quiet railroad tracks?
sec05-card-sec05-F023.teaching_text: Assuming a school bus or fuel truck will roll straight across clear tracks sets up a rear-end collision.

sec05-card-sec05-F024.question_text: What manual-transmission habit must you avoid while crossing railroad tracks?
sec05-card-sec05-F024.teaching_text: Missing a shift mid-crossing can stall your engine directly in the path of oncoming rail traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F025.question_text: What hidden danger lurks behind a passing train, and what gamble must you never take at tracks?
sec05-card-sec05-F025.teaching_text: Optical illusions make huge locomotives appear slower than they travel, turning every race into a losing bet.

sec05-card-sec05-F026.question_text: How should you respond when a traffic officer waves you across a railroad crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-F026.teaching_text: Promptly clearing the rails as directed prevents traffic backups from stranding cars across the tracks.

sec05-card-sec05-F027.question_text: Where do you find the blue Emergency Notification System sign at a railroad crossing, and what does it show?
sec05-card-sec05-F027.teaching_text: Knowing whether to check the crossbuck post or nearby signal cabinet saves precious seconds during a track emergency.

sec05-card-sec05-F028.question_text: Whom does the Emergency Notification System phone number reach, and what action can they take?
sec05-card-sec05-F028.teaching_text: Calling the rail dispatcher directly connects straight to train crews far faster than routing through general channels alone.

sec05-card-sec05-F029.question_text: Which four crossing hazards should citizens report using the blue rail emergency number?
sec05-card-sec05-F029.teaching_text: Reporting stuck gates, stalled vehicles, or track trespassers early prevents derailments and crossing tragedies.
sec05-card-sec05-F029.must_match_memory_hook: Broken signals, blocked tracks, trespassers, hazards

visual_sync.text_span: Broken signals, blocked tracks, trespassers, hazards

sec05-card-sec05-F030.question_text: What does a steady red traffic signal require, and what is the lone standard exception?
sec05-card-sec05-F030.teaching_text: Rolling past the stop line on red violates right-of-way and draws immediate intersection tickets.

sec05-card-sec05-F031.question_text: What three conditions govern making a lawful right turn on a steady red light?
sec05-card-sec05-F031.teaching_text: Scanning for crosswalk pedestrians and checking for a No Turn on Red sign prevents curb-edge crashes and citations.

sec05-card-sec05-F032.question_text: Does slowing down and yielding without stopping satisfy Mississippi's right-turn-on-red law?
sec05-card-sec05-F032.teaching_text: Rolling rights are a classic road-test failure—your wheels must lock to zero before creeping to turn.

sec05-card-sec05-F033.question_text: What warning does a steady circular yellow light give, and how should you respond?
sec05-card-sec05-F033.teaching_text: Punching the gas on yellow stretches braking distance and risks T-boning cross traffic or left-turners.

sec05-card-sec05-F034.question_text: Even when your light turns steady green, whom must you let clear before entering?
sec05-card-sec05-F034.teaching_text: Green gives permission to go only when clear—never barge into walkers or cars still finishing the last phase.

sec05-card-sec05-F035.question_text: When turning left on a steady round green ball, who holds the right-of-way?
sec05-card-sec05-F035.teaching_text: Assuming a solid green circle stops opposing straight traffic is one of the deadliest rookie intersection mistakes.

sec05-card-sec05-F036.question_text: What turn status does a green arrow grant from the proper lane, and what light faces opposing traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-F036.teaching_text: Still scan for stray crosswalk walkers or red-light runners even when a green arrow holds oncoming lanes on red.

sec05-card-sec05-F037.question_text: Under what condition may you turn from the proper lane on a flashing yellow arrow?
sec05-card-sec05-F037.teaching_text: Treat a flashing yellow arrow just like an unprotected green ball—wait for a safe, unhurried gap.

sec05-card-sec05-F038.question_text: Why is a turn on a flashing yellow arrow considered unprotected?
sec05-card-sec05-F038.teaching_text: Oncoming drivers are cruising through at full speed under green, so misjudging their gap causes severe T-bone hits.

sec05-card-sec05-F039.question_text: What does a steady yellow turn arrow warn is coming next, and what must you do?
sec05-card-sec05-F039.teaching_text: Squeezing through a dying yellow arrow risks meeting freshly released oncoming traffic mid-turn.

sec05-card-sec05-F040.question_text: In a shared straight-and-left lane facing red with no green arrow, which movements are allowed?
sec05-card-sec05-F040.teaching_text: Without an active green arrow, a red signal locks down every movement from that shared lane.

sec05-card-sec05-F041.question_text: When a signal displays both a green left arrow and a steady red ball, what is allowed versus forbidden?
sec05-card-sec05-F041.teaching_text: Drivers in through lanes must stay stopped on the red ball while dedicated left-turners clear safely.

sec05-card-sec05-F042.question_text: What movements are permitted when both a green left-turn arrow and a steady green ball shine together?
sec05-card-sec05-F042.teaching_text: Staying in the proper lane lets protected left-turners and straight-through traffic move smoothly at once.

sec05-card-sec05-F043.question_text: Between which signal phases does a yellow turn arrow bridge?
sec05-card-sec05-F043.teaching_text: Recognizing that protected priority is ending stops you from turning blindly as opposing traffic gets green.

sec05-card-sec05-F044.question_text: Which two signal displays share the exact same yield-to-oncoming rule for left turns?
sec05-card-sec05-F044.teaching_text: Permit exams test whether drivers realize both signals mean oncoming traffic still owns right-of-way.

sec05-card-sec05-F045.question_text: How must you handle an intersection controlled by a flashing red light?
sec05-card-sec05-F045.teaching_text: Treat a flashing red exactly like a stop sign—halt completely first, then yield before moving.

sec05-card-sec05-F046.question_text: What two actions does a flashing circular yellow light require?
sec05-card-sec05-F046.teaching_text: Slamming to an unexpected stop under flashing yellow risks getting rear-ended, while speeding ignores cross-street hazards.

sec05-card-sec05-F047.question_text: If a malfunctioning traffic signal drops into flashing yellow mode, how should you cross?
sec05-card-sec05-F047.teaching_text: Cross-street drivers normally face flashing red during fault mode, yet scanning cautiously guards against confused motorists.

sec05-card-sec05-F048.question_text: What rule governs an intersection when a power outage leaves every signal light dark?
sec05-card-sec05-F048.teaching_text: Blowing through a dead signal without stopping causes high-speed T-bone crashes during storm blackouts.

sec05-card-sec05-F049.question_text: Regardless of signal or sign type, whom must you always yield to at any intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-F049.teaching_text: Right-of-way is never a license to hit someone—let pedestrians and clearing vehicles finish crossing first.

sec05-card-sec05-F050.question_text: On reversible or lane-controlled roads, which overhead color permits travel and which forbids entry?
sec05-card-sec05-F050.teaching_text: Entering a reversible lane marked red puts you nose-to-nose against oncoming rush-hour traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F051.question_text: If a uniformed traffic officer waves you through a steady red light or stop sign, whom do you obey?
sec05-card-sec05-F051.teaching_text: Officers managing crash scenes, parades, or broken lights see hazards fixed signals cannot detect.

sec05-card-sec05-F052.question_text: What hand position and whistle sound do traffic officers typically use to command a stop?
sec05-card-sec05-F052.teaching_text: Recognizing one long whistle blast paired with a raised palm helps you brake smoothly in noisy intersections.

sec05-card-sec05-F053.question_text: How does a traffic officer typically wave stopped lanes forward with hand and whistle?
sec05-card-sec05-F053.teaching_text: Several short whistle chirps paired with a hand wave distinguish go-ahead cues cleanly from the long stop blast.

sec05-card-sec05-F054.question_text: What tool may a traffic officer use after dark to direct motorists?
sec05-card-sec05-F054.teaching_text: Slowing down when illuminated wand or flashlight beams sweep ahead keeps night scene responders out of harm's way.

sec05-card-sec05-F055.question_text: What must a pedestrian still standing on the curb do when the pedestrian signal starts flashing?
sec05-card-sec05-F055.teaching_text: Flashing countdown phases leave only enough seconds for walkers already in the street, not late starters.

sec05-card-sec05-F056.question_text: What should a pedestrian already partway across the street do if the crossing signal begins flashing?
sec05-card-sec05-F056.teaching_text: Turning back mid-street creates confusion—clearance intervals are timed so walkers already crossing reach the far curb.

sec05-card-sec05-F057.question_text: Before stepping into any crosswalk, what traffic check should every pedestrian make?
sec05-card-sec05-F057.teaching_text: Walk signals never physically stop distracted drivers, so checking left and right protects your life.

sec06-card-sec06-F001.question_text: What maximum vehicle speed does Mississippi's handbook set inside a school zone?
sec06-card-sec06-F001.teaching_text: Dropping to fifteen gives you stopping margin when distracted students step between parked buses.

sec06-card-sec06-F002.question_text: What is the top speed for a school bus carrying students along its regular school route?
sec06-card-sec06-F002.teaching_text: Frequent neighborhood stops and standing-aisle risks cap route buses well below highway passenger limits.

sec06-card-sec06-F003.question_text: When a school bus travels on a Mississippi interstate highway, what is its maximum handbook speed?
sec06-card-sec06-F003.teaching_text: Exam questions contrast route versus interstate bus limits—forty-five on normal routes jumps to sixty-five on interstates.

sec06-card-sec06-F004.question_text: What minimum and maximum interstate speeds apply to passenger cars and unloaded half-ton pickups?
sec06-card-sec06-F004.teaching_text: Driving below forty on a fast freeway creates nearly as dangerous a closing-speed delta as speeding.

sec06-card-sec06-F005.question_text: On Mississippi state or United States four-lane highways, what minimum and maximum speeds govern passenger cars?
sec06-card-sec06-F005.teaching_text: Non-interstate four-lane highways can still have driveway entries and cross streets, capping top speed five lower than interstates.

sec06-card-sec06-F006.question_text: What is the usual maximum passenger-car speed on state and United States two-lane highways?
sec06-card-sec06-F006.teaching_text: Undivided two-lane roads carry oncoming traffic just across paint, demanding lower speeds than divided corridors.

sec06-card-sec06-F007.question_text: What maximum speed limit does the handbook list for the Natchez Trace Parkway?
sec06-card-sec06-F007.teaching_text: Scenic parkway cyclists, wildlife, and tourist overlooks make the fifty-mile-per-hour Trace limit strictly enforced.

sec06-card-sec06-F008.question_text: How do posted speed signs interact with default handbook limits, and what two things must you monitor?
sec06-card-sec06-F008.teaching_text: Default state limits only govern unposted stretches—always match local speed signs against your dashboard speedometer.

sec06-card-sec06-F009.question_text: Which four roadway or traffic situations call for slowing down below normal cruising speed?
sec06-card-sec06-F009.teaching_text: Tight bends and packed intersections shrink sightlines and escape space well below open-highway assumptions.

sec06-card-sec06-F010.question_text: How must your speed change whenever bad weather or poor visibility rolls in?
sec06-card-sec06-F010.teaching_text: Rain, fog, smoke, and dusk cut both tire traction and sight distance simultaneously.

sec06-card-sec06-F011.question_text: Does driving at the posted speed limit guarantee your speed is safe and legal in every condition?
sec06-card-sec06-F011.teaching_text: Driving the posted sixty-five in blinding rain can still earn a too-fast-for-conditions ticket—or a hydroplane crash.

sec06-card-sec06-F012.question_text: How does higher travel speed affect crash likelihood and survival odds?
sec06-card-sec06-F012.teaching_text: Kinetic impact energy climbs exponentially with speed, overwhelming crumple zones and seat belts in high-speed hits.

sec06-card-sec06-F013.question_text: Before which five maneuvers must you activate your turn signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F013.teaching_text: Drivers often forget to signal when pulling into or out of curb parallel-parking spots—examiners score both.

sec06-card-sec06-F014.question_text: When should your turn signal start blinking relative to a turn or pass?
sec06-card-sec06-F014.teaching_text: Flipping the blinker mid-swerve tells nobody anything—early flashes let trailing cars ease off the gas.

sec06-card-sec06-F015.question_text: Should you copy the turn signal of the vehicle ahead if you plan to keep going straight?
sec06-card-sec06-F015.teaching_text: Echoing a lead car's blinker tricks cross-street drivers into pulling out directly across your straight path.

sec06-card-sec06-F016.question_text: Why must you never flash your left turn signal to wave a trailing driver past you?
sec06-card-sec06-F016.teaching_text: A left blinker tells traffic you're moving left, and only the overtaking driver can judge oncoming clearance.

sec06-card-sec06-F017.question_text: Which three groups of road users may rely on hand-and-arm signals?
sec06-card-sec06-F017.teaching_text: Recognizing manual arm cues keeps you from clipping cyclists, tractors, or cars nursing a blown fuse.

sec06-card-sec06-F018.question_text: How should your arm be positioned, and for what minimum distance must you hold an arm signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F018.teaching_text: Half-hearted wrist waves out the window vanish at road speeds—extend straight and hold for one hundred feet.

sec06-card-sec06-F019.question_text: Which three leftward maneuvers does a left arm extended straight horizontally signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F019.teaching_text: Pulling away from a right-hand curb enters the left travel lane, using the same horizontal left-arm cue.

sec06-card-sec06-F020.question_text: Which three rightward moves does a left arm bent upward at the elbow indicate?
sec06-card-sec06-F020.teaching_text: Exam questions swap upward and downward elbows—forearm pointing skyward always means moving right.

sec06-card-sec06-F021.question_text: What does a left arm pointed downward with an open palm facing backward tell trailing traffic?
sec06-card-sec06-F021.teaching_text: When brake lights fail, an open palm angled toward the asphalt warns following drivers to brake early.

sec06-card-sec06-F022.question_text: What primary collision type does following another vehicle too closely invite?
sec06-card-sec06-F022.teaching_text: Riding another bumper leaves zero human reaction margin when lead brake lights suddenly flash red.

sec06-card-sec06-F023.question_text: What minimum following-space formula does Mississippi's handbook give per ten miles per hour of speed?
sec06-card-sec06-F023.teaching_text: At sixty miles per hour, holding at least six full vehicle lengths gives dry-pavement brakes room to work.

sec06-card-sec06-F024.question_text: What sudden lead-vehicle action must your forward space cushion always handle safely?
sec06-card-sec06-F024.teaching_text: Blowouts, deer, or missed turns can make the car ahead slam brakes without warning.

sec06-card-sec06-F025.question_text: Beyond braking room, what visual advantage should a proper following gap give you?
sec06-card-sec06-F025.teaching_text: Hanging back opens sightlines past the car ahead so you spot stalled lanes before brake lights even glow.

sec06-card-sec06-F026.question_text: How should you adjust your following distance behind a large truck or bus?
sec06-card-sec06-F026.teaching_text: Tall boxy trailers wall off forward vision and hide potholes until they appear right under your bumper.

sec06-card-sec06-F027.question_text: When driving inside a motorcade or funeral procession, why must you leave spacing gaps?
sec06-card-sec06-F027.teaching_text: Bumper-to-bumper convoys trap overtaking or merging cars in oncoming lanes with nowhere to tuck in.

sec06-card-sec06-F028.question_text: How should you manage speed and spacing while traveling in a procession?
sec06-card-sec06-F028.teaching_text: Accordion-style gas-and-brake surges ripple backward through tight lines and cause chain-reaction fender-benders.

sec06-card-sec06-F029.question_text: Which three ideal conditions does the handbook's stopping-distance chart assume?
sec06-card-sec06-F029.teaching_text: Treat chart numbers as absolute best-case minimums rather than real-world wet-commute guarantees.

sec06-card-sec06-F030.question_text: Which four road or driver factors can stretch real stopping distances far beyond handbook chart numbers?
sec06-card-sec06-F030.teaching_text: Slick asphalt lengthens tire slide while drowsiness or alcohol stretches reaction travel before your foot even moves.

sec06-card-sec06-F031.question_text: When do thinking and reaction distance happen during an emergency stop?
sec06-card-sec06-F031.teaching_text: At highway speed, your car covers dozens of feet just while your brain recognizes danger and moves your foot.

sec06-card-sec06-F032.question_text: From what exact moment to what endpoint is braking distance measured?
sec06-card-sec06-F032.teaching_text: Keeping reaction travel separate from braking travel is a favorite multiple-choice distinction on written exams.

sec06-card-sec06-F033.question_text: Which two travel phases combine to equal total stopping distance?
sec06-card-sec06-F033.teaching_text: Forgetting reaction distance tricks drivers into thinking they can stop in half the room physics actually demands.

sec07-card-sec07-F001.question_text: Do traffic lanes still exist on streets or rural highways that have no painted lane lines?
sec07-card-sec07-F001.teaching_text: Driving down the dead center of an unpainted residential street steals oncoming room and risks head-on scrapes.
