sec07-card-sec07-F002.question_text: What determines how many lanes a roadway has?
sec07-card-sec07-F002.teaching_text: Judging roadway width by side-by-side car rows keeps traffic orderly even where fresh asphalt lacks striping.

sec07-card-sec07-F003.question_text: Which three features may separate opposing directions of travel on a roadway?
sec07-card-sec07-F003.teaching_text: Recognizing what divides opposing flow prevents turning into the wrong side of a divided boulevard.

sec07-card-sec07-F004.question_text: On city streets, what extra lane often runs right beside an active travel lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F004.teaching_text: Mistaking a curbside parking strip for a through lane forces sudden swerves when parked bumpers appear ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-F005.question_text: When multiple lanes run in your direction, which lane should you normally use, and what two exceptions apply?
sec07-card-sec07-F005.teaching_text: Camping in left lanes blocks overtaking flow and pushes impatient drivers into risky right-side passes.

sec07-card-sec07-F006.question_text: Which lane must you turn left from when no dedicated left-turn pocket exists?
sec07-card-sec07-F006.teaching_text: Turning left from an outer right lane cuts directly across straight traffic moving beside your left flank.

sec07-card-sec07-F007.question_text: May you cross double solid yellow lines to pass a vehicle creeping slowly ahead?
sec07-card-sec07-F007.teaching_text: Double yellow paint marks blind crests, curves, or junctions where even a slow pass risks a head-on crash.

sec07-card-sec07-F008.question_text: Under what conditions does a dashed yellow center line allow crossing to pass?
sec07-card-sec07-F008.teaching_text: Dashed yellow paint marks sightline permission, never a guarantee—you still own verifying oncoming clearance.

sec07-card-sec07-F009.question_text: Where solid and broken yellow center lines sit side by side, which side may pass?
sec07-card-sec07-F009.teaching_text: Highway engineers place the dashed stripe exclusively on the lane with enough forward sightline to overtake safely.

sec07-card-sec07-F010.question_text: How should you position your vehicle inside traffic lanes, and when may you shift lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-F010.teaching_text: Straddling lane stripes or drifting sideways without mirror and shoulder checks invites sideswipe collisions.

sec07-card-sec07-F011.question_text: What special roadway lane should you pull into when preparing for a left turn where provided?
sec07-card-sec07-F011.teaching_text: Tucking into the center turn pocket clears high-speed through traffic off your rear bumper while waiting.

sec07-card-sec07-F012.question_text: On a two-lane highway, which directions of traffic are barred from passing by double solid yellow lines?
sec07-card-sec07-F012.teaching_text: Twin solid yellow stripes lock down overtaking from both ways where hills, curves, or driveways limit sight.

sec07-card-sec07-F013.question_text: Alongside a paired solid-and-broken yellow center stripe, what rule binds the driver next to the solid line?
sec07-card-sec07-F013.teaching_text: A solid yellow stripe right off your left fender means your forward sightline is blind—wait until dashes return.

sec07-card-sec07-F014.question_text: On an undivided four-lane highway, may you ever cross the center line to overtake?
sec07-card-sec07-F014.teaching_text: With two same-direction lanes already on your side, crossing center puts you head-on into fast oncoming lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F015.question_text: Where broken white lines divide same-direction lanes on interstates or four-lane highways, which lanes allow passing?
sec07-card-sec07-F015.teaching_text: Broken white dashes separate traffic moving the same way, allowing cautious lane changes and overtaking when clear.

sec07-card-sec07-F016.question_text: Before pulling left to overtake, which three clearance zones must you verify?
sec07-card-sec07-F016.teaching_text: Checking behind catches a faster car already overtaking you, while checking ahead ensures room to merge back.

sec07-card-sec07-F017.question_text: Why must you hang back rather than tailgate a vehicle you plan to pass?
sec07-card-sec07-F017.teaching_text: Hugging a truck's bumper blinds you until half your hood is already poking into oncoming traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F018.question_text: How should you combine signaling, checking, and pace when pulling left to pass?
sec07-card-sec07-F018.teaching_text: Crisp, decisive passing after signaling minimizes seconds spent exposed inside an opposing or passing lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F019.question_text: After overtaking a vehicle, what mirror landmark confirms enough space to return to the right lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F019.teaching_text: Cutting back right before the overtaken bumper fills your inside mirror risks clipping its front fender.

sec07-card-sec07-F020.question_text: When does a single vehicle ahead justify overtaking on the right?
sec07-card-sec07-F020.teaching_text: Still verify paved lane room—never bounce onto gravel shoulders to squeeze past a left-turning car.

sec07-card-sec07-F021.question_text: How do multilane interstates treat overtaking on the right?
sec07-card-sec07-F021.teaching_text: Even where legal on interstates, watch right-side blind spots carefully because drivers expect passes on the left.

sec07-card-sec07-F022.question_text: Which two other unobstructed roadway types permit passing on the right?
sec07-card-sec07-F022.teaching_text: Unobstructed four-lane highways free of parked cars and wide one-way streets give full paved lanes on the right.

sec07-card-sec07-F023.question_text: Even on roads where right-side passing is legal, what overarching rule still governs?
sec07-card-sec07-F023.teaching_text: Legal permission never overrides poor visibility, slick pavement, or unpredictable blind-spot drift.

sec07-card-sec07-F024.question_text: May you ever drive off the paved lane or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F024.teaching_text: Soft gravel edges, drainage drop-offs, and stalled roadside cars turn shoulder passes into rollovers.

sec07-card-sec07-F025.question_text: What rule governs passing on hills, around curves, or anywhere forward sight is blocked?
sec07-card-sec07-F025.teaching_text: An oncoming vehicle hidden behind a crest closes at combined double highway speed—zero time to escape.

sec07-card-sec07-F026.question_text: Within how many feet of bridges, viaducts, overpasses, rail crossings, crosswalks, or intersections is passing banned?
sec07-card-sec07-F026.teaching_text: Memorize all six landmarks—bridges, viaducts, overpasses, tracks, crosswalks, and intersections carry a hundred-foot buffer.

sec07-card-sec07-F027.question_text: Where must you position your car when another driver overtakes you on a two- or three-lane highway?
sec07-card-sec07-F027.teaching_text: Hugging the right side widens lateral clearance so the passing car clears cleanly without clipping mirrors.

sec07-card-sec07-F028.question_text: What throttle rule binds you from the moment another car starts passing until it clears ahead?
sec07-card-sec07-F028.teaching_text: Accelerating traps the passing driver inside the oncoming lane and turns pride into a head-on wreck.

sec07-card-sec07-F029.question_text: According to Mississippi's passing rules, when may a car next to a broken center line overtake?
sec07-card-sec07-F029.teaching_text: Even beside broken dashes, pulling out against oncoming headlights puts full legal fault on the passer.

sec07-card-sec07-F030.question_text: In a paired solid-and-broken center marking, which side do the handbook's passing rules forbid from overtaking?
sec07-card-sec07-F030.teaching_text: Treat the stripe closest to your left tire as your personal command—solid means stay tucked in.

sec08-card-sec08-F001.question_text: Where do you position your vehicle, and what warning do you give before starting a confined-space turnaround?
sec08-card-sec08-F001.teaching_text: Starting tight against the right edge maximizes turning radius across narrow two-lane pavement.

sec08-card-sec08-F002.question_text: How do you combine speed and steering at the start of a confined-space turnaround?
sec08-card-sec08-F002.teaching_text: Turning the wheel sharply while creeping slowly pivots the car tightly without lurching over the opposite curb.

sec08-card-sec08-F003.question_text: During the first forward swing of a turnaround, how close to the left curb or edge do you stop?
sec08-card-sec08-F003.teaching_text: Bumping or mounting the curb during a turnaround deducts points—or fails—your road test.

sec08-card-sec08-F004.question_text: After stopping inches from the left edge, how do you steer and move on the reverse leg?
sec08-card-sec08-F004.teaching_text: Checking over your shoulder while reversing slowly with full right lock swings your nose cleanly down-road.

sec08-card-sec08-F005.question_text: How do you wrap up the turnaround once your reverse leg reaches near the rear curb?
sec08-card-sec08-F005.teaching_text: Extra-narrow streets occasionally need one additional short pass rather than forcing tires over a curb.

sec08-card-sec08-F006.question_text: Where must you wait if backed-up traffic blocks the street past an intersection?
sec08-card-sec08-F006.teaching_text: Pulling forward without exit space strands your car across crosswalks and cross traffic when lights change.

sec08-card-sec08-F007.question_text: How should you plan an upcoming turn if unsure of street names, and what mistake must you avoid?
sec08-card-sec08-F007.teaching_text: Whipping across lanes at the last second causes sideswipes—passing your turn safely and circling back beats crashing.

sec08-card-sec08-F008.question_text: Whom does early turn signaling warn around an intersection?
sec08-card-sec08-F008.teaching_text: Crosswalk walkers rely on your blinking corner light just as much as trailing and oncoming drivers do.

sec08-card-sec08-F009.question_text: When should you move into the proper lane for an upcoming turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F009.teaching_text: Lining up early avoids cutting across adjacent lanes right at solid intersection channel lines.

sec08-card-sec08-F010.question_text: Why must you look in every direction before turning or changing lanes even with your blinker on?
sec08-card-sec08-F010.teaching_text: A blinking bulb never clears blind spots or forces distracted drivers to yield space.

sec08-card-sec08-F011.question_text: Where should you finish slowing down for a turn, and how must your front wheels stay aimed until turning?
sec08-card-sec08-F011.teaching_text: Pre-cocked front wheels launch your car straight into oncoming lanes or pedestrians if rear-ended while waiting.

sec08-card-sec08-F012.question_text: How should you manage speed, brake, and clutch once inside a turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F012.teaching_text: Braking hard or coasting on the clutch mid-corner upsets tire grip and invites skids on slick asphalt.

sec08-card-sec08-F013.question_text: What transmission habit should you avoid as you enter an intersection?
sec08-card-sec08-F013.teaching_text: Select your gear beforehand so both hands stay on the wheel and the engine never stalls mid-crossing.

sec08-card-sec08-F014.question_text: Which lane path must you trace through and out of every turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F014.teaching_text: Drifting wide mid-turn sideswipes parallel turners or oncoming drivers turning right onto the same street.

sec08-card-sec08-F015.question_text: Which three steps get you positioned in the left lane well ahead of a left turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F015.teaching_text: Checking mirrors and signaling before sliding left prevents cutting off faster cars already in the inside lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F016.question_text: At least how far before the intersection must you start signaling left and slowing down?
sec08-card-sec08-F016.teaching_text: One hundred feet is Mississippi's classic exam benchmark for both left-turn and right-turn intersection signals.

sec08-card-sec08-F017.question_text: Where inside your lane do you wait for a left turn, and which way do your wheels point?
sec08-card-sec08-F017.teaching_text: Hugging the center line keeps right-side room tidy while straight wheels prevent getting shoved into oncoming cars.

sec08-card-sec08-F018.question_text: When cleared to turn left, where relative to the intersection's center point should you enter?
sec08-card-sec08-F018.teaching_text: Entering just right of center keeps your arc clean instead of slicing diagonally into cross-street nose lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F019.question_text: Which two sloppy path mistakes must you avoid during a left turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F019.teaching_text: Cutting inside clips waiting cross-street bumpers, while swinging into the right lane hits oncoming right-turners.

sec08-card-sec08-F020.question_text: Once you finish a left turn into the inside lane of a multilane road, what follows when clear?
sec08-card-sec08-F020.teaching_text: Completing the turn into the left lane first, then signaling right separately, keeps lane changes predictable.

sec08-card-sec08-F021.question_text: What three steps position your car properly well ahead of a right turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F021.teaching_text: Moving into the right lane early keeps cyclists and curb-hugging cars from sneaking inside your turn radius.

sec08-card-sec08-F022.question_text: At least how many feet before an intersection must you signal right and start slowing?
sec08-card-sec08-F022.teaching_text: Giving trailing drivers at least one hundred feet of warning prevents panic braking behind your tighter right turn.

sec08-card-sec08-F023.question_text: Where in your lane do you wait before turning right, and how are your wheels aimed?
sec08-card-sec08-F023.teaching_text: Keeping wheels straight until rolling prevents getting pushed onto the sidewalk into waiting pedestrians if bumped.

sec08-card-sec08-F024.question_text: When permitted to turn right, how do you scan and position as you enter the intersection?
sec08-card-sec08-F024.teaching_text: Entering as far right as practical prevents wide arcs that drift across center lines or adjacent lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F025.question_text: Which lane must you finish a right turn inside, and what error must you avoid?
sec08-card-sec08-F025.teaching_text: Swinging wide into the left lane collides with opposing left-turners legally claiming that inside lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F026.question_text: How do you navigate intersections where two or more side-by-side lanes turn together?
sec08-card-sec08-F026.teaching_text: Following painted guide dashes and lane arrows stops side-by-side turners from drifting into each other's fenders.

sec08-card-sec08-F027.question_text: If you choose to turn from a shared straight-and-turn lane, what lane rule binds your turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F027.teaching_text: Changing lanes mid-turn from an optional turn lane cuts directly across the inner turner's path.

sec08-card-sec08-F028.question_text: When two oncoming drivers both turn left at once, how should they pass each other and align lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-F028.teaching_text: Passing in front of each other—left door past left door—keeps sightlines open instead of locking horns.

sec08-card-sec08-F029.question_text: From which lane do you turn off a one-way street when no multi-turn signs are posted?
sec08-card-sec08-F029.teaching_text: Turning left from the far-left curb on a one-way street eliminates oncoming traffic cutting across your left flank.

sec08-card-sec08-F030.question_text: What critical traffic check must you make before turning onto a one-way street?
sec08-card-sec08-F030.teaching_text: Checking One Way arrows and parked-car noses prevents turning straight into head-on downtown lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F031.question_text: What specific mistake do turn-restriction signs at one-way intersections prevent?
sec08-card-sec08-F031.teaching_text: No Left Turn or No Right Turn signs pair directly with Do Not Enter boards to block head-on wrong-way turns.

sec09-card-sec09-F001.question_text: How should you approach every cross street or intersecting road?
sec09-card-sec09-F001.teaching_text: Side streets hide late-braking drivers, cyclists, and darting pedestrians right up to the corner line.

sec09-card-sec09-F002.question_text: What three steps apply whenever buildings, hedges, or parked cars block your full view of an intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F002.teaching_text: Entering a blind corner at full cruising speed leaves zero braking margin if cross traffic appears.

sec09-card-sec09-F003.question_text: Where must you wait when backed-up traffic blocks the lane beyond an intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F003.teaching_text: Rolling past the crosswalk without exit room strands your vehicle sideways across cross-street lanes when signals flip.

sec09-card-sec09-F004.question_text: How should you manage speed entering an intersection versus once you clear the far side?
sec09-card-sec09-F004.teaching_text: Covering the brake into crossings buys reaction time, while gradual throttle afterward keeps traction steady.

sec09-card-sec09-F005.question_text: Why must you drive defensively through intersections instead of assuming others read your plan?
sec09-card-sec09-F005.teaching_text: Distracted drivers and pedestrians miss turn signals every day—keep eyes scanning and an escape cushion ready.

sec09-card-sec09-F006.question_text: What does holding right-of-way grant one road user, and what duty falls on the other?
sec09-card-sec09-F006.teaching_text: Traffic order works only when one traveler moves cleanly and the yielding traveler waits without crowding.

sec09-card-sec09-F007.question_text: After checking who holds intersection priority, why must you never force your right-of-way?
sec09-card-sec09-F007.teaching_text: Being legally right in traffic court never repairs wrecked fenders or prevents hospital trips.

sec09-card-sec09-F008.question_text: What should you do if another driver barges ahead and refuses to yield?
sec09-card-sec09-F008.teaching_text: Swallowing pride for three seconds lets a reckless driver clear harmlessly instead of trading paint.

sec09-card-sec09-F009.question_text: At which crosswalk types must drivers yield to crossing pedestrians?
sec09-card-sec09-F009.teaching_text: Every sidewalk-to-sidewalk corner extension counts as a legal crosswalk even without painted white stripes.

sec09-card-sec09-F010.question_text: Who holds priority between a vehicle already inside an intersection and one just arriving to enter?
sec09-card-sec09-F010.teaching_text: Letting vehicles already mid-crossing finish clears the box cleanly before fresh traffic enters.

sec09-card-sec09-F011.question_text: How much right-of-way priority does a bicycle carry compared with a motor vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F011.teaching_text: Cutting across an oncoming cyclist on a left turn carries the exact same legal fault as hitting a sedan.

sec09-card-sec09-F012.question_text: When vehicles arrive at different moments at an all-way stop, who goes first?
sec09-card-sec09-F012.teaching_text: Watching arrival order as you roll up eliminates awkward hesitation waves at four-way stops.

sec09-card-sec09-F013.question_text: When two vehicles reach an all-way stop at the exact same instant, who yields to whom?
sec09-card-sec09-F013.teaching_text: Checking your right-hand cross street breaks simultaneous four-way-stop ties cleanly every time.

sec09-card-sec09-F014.question_text: Why must you never slam your brakes approaching an all-way stop just to claim first arrival?
sec09-card-sec09-F014.teaching_text: Dive-braking to win a stop-sign tie invites getting rear-ended by the driver trailing behind you.

sec09-card-sec09-F015.question_text: When stop signs control only two opposing streets at a four-way crossing, who holds priority?
sec09-card-sec09-F015.teaching_text: Never assume cross traffic also has a stop sign—peek at the backs of corner posts to confirm.

sec09-card-sec09-F016.question_text: How long must a driver halted at a stop sign wait before pulling across?
sec09-card-sec09-F016.teaching_text: Stopping legally is only step one—pulling into a tight cross-traffic gap still causes T-bone collisions.

sec09-card-sec09-F017.question_text: Once cross traffic clears at a two-way stop, which waiting stop-sign driver goes first?
sec09-card-sec09-F017.teaching_text: Arrival order still settles priority between opposing stop-sign lanes once the through street empties.

sec09-card-sec09-F018.question_text: If two opposing cars stop simultaneously at a two-way stop, who wins between straight travel and a left turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F018.teaching_text: Turning across an oncoming car's path always yields to the driver continuing straight through.

sec09-card-sec09-F019.question_text: Where must your vehicle stop at an intersection stop sign or red signal, and whom do you yield to?
sec09-card-sec09-F019.teaching_text: Stopping before the crosswalk keeps pedestrian lanes open while you yield to walkers and clearing vehicles.

sec09-card-sec09-F020.question_text: What must you do before pulling onto a street from a private driveway or unmarked entrance without a stop sign?
sec09-card-sec09-F020.teaching_text: Missing stop signs never make driveways through-streets—halt completely before crossing sidewalks or entering traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F021.question_text: How do you handle an uncontrolled highway intersection with no signs or lights?
sec09-card-sec09-F021.teaching_text: Rural junctions without signs demand slowing down, yielding to approaching vehicles, and entering only when safe.

sec09-card-sec09-F022.question_text: In which direction does traffic circulate around a roundabout's raised center island?
sec09-card-sec09-F022.teaching_text: Keeping the raised island off your left shoulder guides every entry smoothly rightward into counterclockwise flow.

sec09-card-sec09-F023.question_text: What speed and yield rule governs entering a roundabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F023.teaching_text: Vehicles already inside the circle own right-of-way—wait for a clean gap from your left before merging.

sec09-card-sec09-F024.question_text: Once circulating counterclockwise inside a roundabout, what must you do before taking your exit?
sec09-card-sec09-F024.teaching_text: Signaling your exit tells waiting drivers at the next entry leg whether you're leaving or looping past.

sec09-card-sec09-F025.question_text: At least how far away must you stop when a school bus flashes red lights or extends its stop arm?
sec09-card-sec09-F025.teaching_text: Holding a ten-foot buffer keeps your front bumper clear of blind spots where small children cross.

sec09-card-sec09-F026.question_text: Which four events tell you it is legal to resume moving after stopping for a school bus?
sec09-card-sec09-F026.teaching_text: Never creep forward just because doors shut—stragglers can dart back until the arm folds and the bus rolls.
sec09-card-sec09-F026.must_match_memory_hook: Kids clear, bus rolls, lights-arm off

visual_sync.text_span: Kids clear, bus rolls, lights-arm off

sec09-card-sec09-F027.question_text: On standard undivided roads, which directions of traffic must stop for a flashing red school bus?
sec09-card-sec09-F027.teaching_text: Students routinely cross oncoming lanes to reach driveways opposite the bus door.

sec09-card-sec09-F028.question_text: On a divided highway of four or more lanes with two-plus lanes each way, what must drivers behind a school bus do?
sec09-card-sec09-F028.teaching_text: Even on wide divided corridors, overtaking a stopped school bus from behind in any adjacent lane is unlawful.

sec09-card-sec09-F029.question_text: On a divided highway with at least four lanes and two-plus lanes each way, what applies to oncoming traffic opposite a school bus?
sec09-card-sec09-F029.teaching_text: Students aren't permitted to cross multi-lane divided medians, freeing opposite-side lanes to continue attentively.

sec09-card-sec09-F030.question_text: When is stopping unnecessary for a bus halted inside a highway or adjacent loading zone?
sec09-card-sec09-F030.teaching_text: Controlled turnout bays that forbid pedestrians from crossing active lanes separate riders from highway flow.

sec09-card-sec09-F031.question_text: Which two sudden pedestrian movements must you scan for along rows of parked cars?
sec09-card-sec09-F031.teaching_text: Scanning through parked car windows and beneath bumpers spots feet or swinging doors a split-second earlier.

sec09-card-sec09-F032.question_text: While setting up for an intersection turn, where must your eyes check beyond vehicle gaps?
sec09-card-sec09-F032.teaching_text: Drivers fixated on oncoming car gaps often miss walkers stepping off the curb right into their target turn.

sec09-card-sec09-F033.question_text: What does a white cane—sometimes tipped in red—tell drivers about a pedestrian?
sec09-card-sec09-F033.teaching_text: Spotting a white or red-tipped cane early tells you eye contact and visual hand waves won't register.

sec09-card-sec09-F034.question_text: How must you drive near visually impaired pedestrians at intersections and crosswalks?
sec09-card-sec09-F034.teaching_text: Never honk or rev your engine at a blind pedestrian—halt completely and give unhurried crossing room.

sec09-card-sec09-F035.question_text: How does Mississippi's handbook treat yielding to a passing funeral procession?
sec09-card-sec09-F035.teaching_text: Exam writers love testing courtesy versus statute—yielding respects grieving families even without a statutory mandate.

sec09-card-sec09-F036.question_text: What vehicle-control posture must you maintain around pedestrians near any crosswalk?
sec09-card-sec09-F036.teaching_text: Controlled speed near corners ensures you can yield smoothly whether a crosswalk is painted or unmarked.

sec10-card-sec10-F001.question_text: What legal consequences can follow parking on a blind curve or another hazardous spot?
sec10-card-sec10-F001.teaching_text: Leaving a car around a blind bend turns your rear bumper into a sudden wall for highway traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F002.question_text: How does Mississippi law treat a genuinely broken-down car stopped in a hazardous spot, and what must follow?
sec10-card-sec10-F002.teaching_text: Mechanical failure excuses you from dangerous-parking arrest, yet safety demands towing it clear promptly.

sec10-card-sec10-F003.question_text: Which three steps secure an automatic or manual vehicle every time you park?
sec10-card-sec10-F003.teaching_text: Relying on gear teeth alone without the parking brake risks rollaways if a pawl slips on a grade.

sec10-card-sec10-F004.question_text: May you leave a parked vehicle unattended across a private or public driveway?
sec10-card-sec10-F004.teaching_text: Blocking driveways traps residents or delivery trucks inside and risks an immediate tow.

sec10-card-sec10-F005.question_text: How far must unattended parked cars stay from a fire-station driveway—and when posted opposite?
sec10-card-sec10-F005.teaching_text: Wide-swinging hook-and-ladder rigs need extra curb clearance to turn out rapidly on emergency calls.

sec10-card-sec10-F006.question_text: Within how many feet of a fire hydrant does Mississippi prohibit unattended parking?
sec10-card-sec10-F006.teaching_text: Memorize ten feet for Mississippi hydrants—firefighters cannot spare seconds snaking heavy supply hoses around bumpers.

sec10-card-sec10-F007.question_text: Is leaving an unattended vehicle parked on a sidewalk or crosswalk ever legal?
sec10-card-sec10-F007.teaching_text: Parking across walkways forces wheelchair users, strollers, and kids out into active traffic lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-F008.question_text: How many feet back from an intersection crosswalk is unattended parking prohibited?
sec10-card-sec10-F008.teaching_text: Keeping twenty feet open at corners lets drivers and crossing pedestrians spot each other clearly.

sec10-card-sec10-F009.question_text: May a vehicle ever be parked unattended inside an intersection?
sec10-card-sec10-F009.teaching_text: Even wide rural or residential junctions forbid unattended parking anywhere inside intersecting roadways.

sec10-card-sec10-F010.question_text: Within how many feet approaching a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal is unattended parking banned?
sec10-card-sec10-F010.teaching_text: Tall pickups or vans parked inside thirty feet hide stop signs and red lights from approaching drivers.

sec10-card-sec10-F011.question_text: Which three elevated or tunnel-like highway structures prohibit unattended parking?
sec10-card-sec10-F011.teaching_text: Bridges and underpasses lack escape shoulders, turning any parked car into a bottleneck trap.

sec10-card-sec10-F012.question_text: Is parking alongside another vehicle already stopped or parked at the curb allowed?
sec10-card-sec10-F012.teaching_text: Double-parking blocks an active travel lane while trapping the curb-parked motorist inside.

sec10-card-sec10-F013.question_text: When must you avoid parking near a street work crew or roadway obstruction?
sec10-card-sec10-F013.teaching_text: Parking opposite utility cones or roadwork chokes remaining squeeze width and gridlocks the street.

sec10-card-sec10-F014.question_text: May you leave your vehicle parked along a curb posted with signs prohibiting stopping?
sec10-card-sec10-F014.teaching_text: No-Stopping zones protect rush-hour flow, fire lanes, and sight triangles where even brief halts snarl traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F015.question_text: Outside business and residential districts, where must you position your vehicle to park?
sec10-card-sec10-F015.teaching_text: High-speed country traffic doesn't expect stationary bumpers sitting inside paved travel lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-F016.question_text: When parking beside a highway, how many feet of clear roadway width should remain for passing traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-F016.teaching_text: Twenty clear feet lets opposing lanes pass each other safely without squeezing onto soft shoulders.

sec10-card-sec10-F017.question_text: From at least what distance in both directions should a highway-parked vehicle be clearly visible?
sec10-card-sec10-F017.teaching_text: Two hundred feet of unobstructed sightline gives approaching drivers time to spot your parked silhouette and steer clear.

sec10-card-sec10-F018.question_text: Which lights must stay on if your vehicle is parked beside a highway after dark?
sec10-card-sec10-F018.teaching_text: An unlit dark car on a rural shoulder stays invisible until headlights are dangerously close.

sec10-card-sec10-F019.question_text: How close to the curb must your right-side tires finish when parallel parked?
sec10-card-sec10-F019.teaching_text: Finishing wider than one foot pokes your street-side mirror into passing traffic—and loses road-test points.

sec10-card-sec10-F020.question_text: How should you handle opening street-side doors versus unloading passengers or cargo?
sec10-card-sec10-F020.teaching_text: Swinging a driver door blindly into traffic clips cyclists, while unloading onto the sidewalk keeps riders safe.

sec10-card-sec10-F021.question_text: What three setup actions begin a clean parallel-parking maneuver?
sec10-card-sec10-F021.teaching_text: Signaling early holds trailing cars back so they don't nose right into the pocket you're backing toward.

sec10-card-sec10-F022.question_text: Once traffic clears, how do you steer while backing in—and what alignment landmark cues your wheel flip?
sec10-card-sec10-F022.teaching_text: Matching your front tire with the forward car's rear bumper sets the exact angle to swing your nose clear.

sec10-card-sec10-F023.question_text: After your front tire aligns with the forward car's rear bumper, how do you steer while backing?
sec10-card-sec10-F023.teaching_text: Cranking sharply left tucks your front end cleanly inside the lane without tapping the parked car behind.

sec10-card-sec10-F024.question_text: How do you straighten and position your vehicle to finish parallel parking?
sec10-card-sec10-F024.teaching_text: Centering with cushion fore and aft ensures neither neighbor gets boxed in when pulling out later.

sec10-card-sec10-F025.question_text: Who holds right-of-way when a parked driver pulls out into traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-F025.teaching_text: Moving lanes and sidewalk walkers always outrank a parked car—wait until the path is completely open.

sec10-card-sec10-F026.question_text: Which two safety steps come right before pulling out of a parallel-parking space?
sec10-card-sec10-F026.teaching_text: Side mirrors miss cars and bikes tucked in your left rear quarter—always turn your head and signal.

sec10-card-sec10-F027.question_text: How should you reverse out of an angled or perpendicular parking stall?
sec10-card-sec10-F027.teaching_text: Parking-lot aisles mix rolling carts, backing minivans, and small kids—keep looking backward the entire way out.

sec10-card-sec10-F028.question_text: Why must you look over your shoulder while reversing instead of relying on mirrors alone?
sec10-card-sec10-F028.teaching_text: Rearview mirrors frame a narrow tunnel, missing pedestrians or cross-aisle cars approaching from either rear corner.

sec10-card-sec10-F029.question_text: Which way do you turn your front wheels when parking downhill—with or without a curb?
sec10-card-sec10-F029.teaching_text: Pointing wheels right lets gravity roll a slipping car into the curb or off-road shoulder rather than traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F030.question_text: Which direction do you turn your front wheels when parking uphill with no curb?
sec10-card-sec10-F030.teaching_text: With no curb to catch a backward roll, turning right aims the rear away from active center lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-F031.question_text: Which hill-parking scenario is the lone case where you turn your front wheels sharply left?
sec10-card-sec10-F031.teaching_text: Memorize the lone left—uphill beside a curb hooks the back of your right front tire against the stone.

sec10-card-sec10-F032.question_text: How must your driving adjust once darkness cuts forward visibility?
sec10-card-sec10-F032.teaching_text: Depth perception, color contrast, and peripheral sight all shrink sharply the moment daylight fades.

sec10-card-sec10-F033.question_text: What rule links your nighttime speed directly to your headlight beam reach?
sec10-card-sec10-F033.teaching_text: Driving faster than your beams illuminate means you won't spot a stalled car or deer until braking is impossible.

sec10-card-sec10-F034.question_text: What two actions protect your eyes and lane position when dazzling headlights approach?
sec10-card-sec10-F034.teaching_text: Flashing high beams back blinds both drivers—tracking the right pavement edge keeps you centered until they pass.

sec10-card-sec10-F035.question_text: Where in your lane should you position when an oncoming vehicle shows only one working headlight?
sec10-card-sec10-F035.teaching_text: That lone bulb could be a motorcycle—or a wide pickup missing its driver-side headlight right near center.

sec10-card-sec10-F036.question_text: Why should you never wear sunglasses or dark lenses against glare at night or on gloomy days?
sec10-card-sec10-F036.teaching_text: Tinted lenses dim unlit pedestrians, animals, and lane edges far more than they soften headlight glare.

sec10-card-sec10-F037.question_text: Within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle must you switch from high beams to low beams?
sec10-card-sec10-F037.teaching_text: Mississippi uses five hundred feet for both oncoming and following beam drops—easy to lock in as one pair.

sec10-card-sec10-F038.question_text: Within how many feet behind a lead vehicle must you switch to low beams?
sec10-card-sec10-F038.teaching_text: High beams inside five hundred feet bounce off rearview and side mirrors, blinding the driver right ahead of you.

sec10-card-sec10-F039.question_text: During what clock period and visibility threshold must your headlights be on?
sec10-card-sec10-F039.teaching_text: Heavy rain, smoke, or fog in midday triggers the exact same five-hundred-foot headlight law as nighttime.

sec10-card-sec10-F040.question_text: May you drive using parking lights instead of full headlights at dusk or in poor visibility?
sec10-card-sec10-F040.teaching_text: Parking lights mark stationary cars only and cast almost zero illumination onto dark asphalt.

sec10-card-sec10-F041.question_text: Where do high beams belong, and how should your night speed still compare to daytime?
sec10-card-sec10-F041.teaching_text: Even bright high beams cover less sight distance than sunshine, so ease below daytime highway speeds.

sec10-card-sec10-F042.question_text: Which three driving environments call for low beams rather than high beams?
sec10-card-sec10-F042.teaching_text: Daytime and nighttime fog alike need low beams angled down onto pavement rather than scattering upward.

sec10-card-sec10-F043.question_text: What happens to your forward visibility if you flick on high beams in fog?
sec10-card-sec10-F043.teaching_text: Upward high-beam rays bounce straight back off tiny water droplets into a blinding white wall.

sec11-card-sec11-F001.question_text: Which seating rows must wear properly fastened safety belts under Mississippi's handbook?
sec11-card-sec11-F001.teaching_text: Unbelted back-seat passengers become deadly forward projectiles against front-seat riders in a crash.

sec11-card-sec11-F002.question_text: When and where does Mississippi's passenger-vehicle seat-belt requirement apply?
sec11-card-sec11-F002.teaching_text: The moment your passenger vehicle rolls forward on any public street, road, or highway, everyone must be buckled.

sec11-card-sec11-F003.question_text: How must a child younger than age four ride in a vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F003.teaching_text: Adult lap-and-shoulder belts cannot hold small toddler frames—approved child seats cradle fragile necks and chests.

sec11-card-sec11-F004.question_text: When does a child age four through six legally require an approved belt-positioning booster seat?
sec11-card-sec11-F004.teaching_text: Boosters lift smaller kids so adult belts cross strong hip and collarbone points instead of soft stomachs and necks.

sec11-card-sec11-F005.question_text: What legal penalty can hit violations of Mississippi's seat-belt or child-restraint laws?
sec11-card-sec11-F005.teaching_text: Skipping buckles or booster seats exposes you to roadside fines long before any crash happens.

sec11-card-sec11-F006.question_text: Below what age does Mississippi's handbook recommend keeping children in a rear seat?
sec11-card-sec11-F006.teaching_text: Front airbags inflate fast enough to injure children twelve and younger sitting up front.

sec11-card-sec11-F007.question_text: How long does the American Academy of Pediatrics guidance in the handbook keep a child rear-facing?
sec11-card-sec11-F007.teaching_text: Extended rear-facing supports developing spines far better than turning forward at the earliest birthday.

sec11-card-sec11-F008.question_text: Apart from the legal age rule, across what weight range does the handbook recommend using a booster seat?
sec11-card-sec11-F008.teaching_text: Matching booster fit to forty-through-sixty-five-pound body size prevents loose lap belts from riding up.

sec11-card-sec11-F009.question_text: Why must you drop speed right when rain starts falling?
sec11-card-sec11-F009.teaching_text: The first ten minutes of rain float oil and road grime into a slicker glaze than steady downpours.

sec11-card-sec11-F010.question_text: Why must you slow down whenever standing water covers the road?
sec11-card-sec11-F010.teaching_text: Once tire grooves can't pump water fast enough, speed lifts rubber completely off the asphalt.

sec11-card-sec11-F011.question_text: What actually happens beneath your steering tires during hydroplaning?
sec11-card-sec11-F011.teaching_text: With zero rubber touching pavement, turning the wheel or stomping brakes has almost no steering effect.

sec11-card-sec11-F012.question_text: How do you prevent hydroplaning during rainstorms and near puddles?
sec11-card-sec11-F012.teaching_text: Slower rotation lets tire tread channels squeeze water aside and keep solid grip on pavement.

sec11-card-sec11-F013.question_text: What must you do when facing a flooded roadway or deep pool of standing water?
sec11-card-sec11-F013.teaching_text: Shallow-looking floodwater hides washed-out pavement, stalls engines, and sweeps heavy cars downstream.

sec11-card-sec11-F014.question_text: Why avoid sudden braking in a skid, and what manual-transmission pedal must you leave alone?
sec11-card-sec11-F014.teaching_text: Slamming brakes locks sliding wheels worse, and pressing the clutch disconnects steady engine drag.

sec11-card-sec11-F015.question_text: What are your first two pedal rules the instant a tire goes flat or blows out?
sec11-card-sec11-F015.teaching_text: Jabbing the brake during a blowout yanks the vehicle violently toward the shredded tire's side.

sec11-card-sec11-F016.question_text: Once steady after a blowout, how should you brake—or stop when plenty of clear road lies ahead?
sec11-card-sec11-F016.teaching_text: Letting rolling resistance slow the car naturally keeps steering predictable until you pull safely off-road.

sec11-card-sec11-F017.question_text: How should you use your brakes if your wheels drop off the paved roadway edge?
sec11-card-sec11-F017.teaching_text: Jerking back onto higher asphalt at highway speed whips the car sideways across oncoming lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-F018.question_text: Where should you move a disabled vehicle whenever possible?
sec11-card-sec11-F018.teaching_text: Getting completely onto the far-right shoulder clears high-speed lanes and gives tow trucks safe access.

sec11-card-sec11-F019.question_text: If forced to walk for help, which side of a regular highway do you use, and what interstate rule applies?
sec11-card-sec11-F019.teaching_text: Facing oncoming cars lets you see drifting bumpers early, while high-speed interstates are deadly to cross on foot.

sec11-card-sec11-F020.question_text: What three immediate steps follow involvement in a crash with injuries?
sec11-card-sec11-F020.teaching_text: Fleeing an injury crash turns an accident into a serious crime while delaying life-saving care.

sec11-card-sec11-F021.question_text: What human harm in a traffic crash triggers a prompt report to law enforcement?
sec11-card-sec11-F021.teaching_text: Any bodily injury or fatality requires an official police investigation and report without delay.

sec11-card-sec11-F022.question_text: Above what apparent dollar amount of property damage does Mississippi's handbook require reporting a crash?
sec11-card-sec11-F022.teaching_text: Modern bumper sensors easily pass five hundred dollars even on minor parking-lot or fender taps.

sec11-card-sec11-F023.question_text: Which four pieces of information must crash participants exchange with one another?
sec11-card-sec11-F023.teaching_text: Trading all four items both ways before leaving protects everyone's claim and satisfies legal duties.

sec11-card-sec11-F024.question_text: What coverage details must you show the investigating officer at a crash scene?
sec11-card-sec11-F024.teaching_text: Keeping current paper or digital insurance cards handy lets officers log active coverage on the spot.

sec11-card-sec11-F025.question_text: Can an uninsured driver still get ticketed after a crash caused entirely by someone else?
sec11-card-sec11-F025.teaching_text: Being rear-ended at a red light won't shield you from a no-insurance citation if you lack coverage proof.

sec11-card-sec11-F026.question_text: Who may file the immediate crash report if injuries keep the driver from doing so?
sec11-card-sec11-F026.teaching_text: Allowing an uninjured passenger to report ensures timely notice while the driver receives medical care.

sec11-card-sec11-F027.question_text: How does Mississippi's handbook classify the privacy status of crash reports?
sec11-card-sec11-F027.teaching_text: State confidentiality rules protect personal crash filings from casual public browsing after you report properly.

sec11-card-sec11-F028.question_text: What toll-free mobile keypad code connects directly to Mississippi Highway Patrol dispatch in a real highway emergency?
sec11-card-sec11-F028.teaching_text: Memorizing star four seven links rural highway emergencies straight to state troopers without airtime charges.

sec11-card-sec11-F029.question_text: What location info do you give Highway Patrol dispatch, and when is that hotkey allowed?
sec11-card-sec11-F029.teaching_text: Watching green mileposts lets troopers find you fast, while keeping non-emergencies off emergency dispatch lines.

sec11-card-sec11-F030.question_text: Which emergency vehicles and active warning signals claim immediate right-of-way?
sec11-card-sec11-F030.teaching_text: Scanning mirrors and keeping cabin music reasonable helps you spot red or blue strobes before sirens peak.

sec11-card-sec11-F031.question_text: Where should you move and wait when an active emergency vehicle approaches?
sec11-card-sec11-F031.teaching_text: Moving uniformly right opens a predictable center corridor instead of scattering cars onto both sides.

sec11-card-sec11-F032.question_text: What should you do if you are already inside an intersection when an emergency siren approaches?
sec11-card-sec11-F032.teaching_text: Stopping dead inside the intersection box blocks the exact turn path the fire engine or ambulance needs.

sec11-card-sec11-F033.question_text: On a four-lane highway, how must you respond to a roadside emergency vehicle flashing lights or sounding a siren?
sec11-card-sec11-F033.teaching_text: Putting an empty lane between highway speed and roadside responders prevents deadly shoulder sideswipes.

sec11-card-sec11-F034.question_text: What is your backup duty if heavy traffic makes merging away from a roadside emergency vehicle unsafe?
sec11-card-sec11-F034.teaching_text: Never swerve into occupied lanes—shed speed sharply and cover the brake past the scene.

sec11-card-sec11-F035.question_text: How should you pull over when a law-enforcement officer signals a traffic stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F035.teaching_text: Using your turn signal acknowledges the officer immediately while you reach a safe shoulder spot.

sec11-card-sec11-F036.question_text: Once stopped for an officer, what should you turn off—and should you step out?
sec11-card-sec11-F036.teaching_text: Jumping out of your car unasked startles officers and exposes you to passing roadside traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F037.question_text: What interior switch should you turn on during a nighttime traffic stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F037.teaching_text: Lighting up the cabin puts the approaching officer at ease by making everyone's hands clearly visible.

sec11-card-sec11-F038.question_text: Where should your hands rest while speaking with an officer during a traffic stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F038.teaching_text: Resting open hands on top of the wheel prevents misunderstandings while listening to instructions.

sec11-card-sec11-F039.question_text: Why might you lower the passenger window instead of the driver window at a traffic stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F039.teaching_text: Officers often walk up the curb-side passenger door on busy highways to avoid speeding lane mirrors.

sec11-card-sec11-F040.question_text: What must you tell the officer right away if a weapon is inside the vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F040.teaching_text: Calmly stating a weapon's presence up front—while keeping hands on the wheel—keeps the stop safe.

sec11-card-sec11-F041.question_text: When should you reach into a pocket, console, or glovebox for your license and papers?
sec11-card-sec11-F041.teaching_text: Ducking toward a dark glovebox as an officer walks up looks suspicious—wait until asked.

sec11-card-sec11-F042.question_text: Which three documents do officers typically ask to inspect at a traffic stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F042.teaching_text: Knowing exact spots for all three items avoids stressed fumbling when pulled over.

sec11-card-sec11-F043.question_text: What should you do if requested papers sit out of reach in a backpack or trunk?
sec11-card-sec11-F043.teaching_text: Telling the officer where the folder sits and waiting for acknowledgment keeps every movement transparent.

sec11-card-sec11-F044.question_text: What identification should an officer out of uniform display, and what if they don't?
sec11-card-sec11-F044.teaching_text: Plainclothes officers carry official law-enforcement credentials, and motorists have every right to ask to see them.

sec11-card-sec11-F045.question_text: If an officer instructs you to step out of your vehicle, how should you exit and stand?
sec11-card-sec11-F045.teaching_text: Following exact standing-spot instructions keeps both you and the officer clear of passing highway mirrors.

sec11-card-sec11-F046.question_text: Which three enforcement outcomes can end a traffic stop, and what question may you ask?
sec11-card-sec11-F046.teaching_text: Asking respectfully for an explanation clarifies next steps, court dates, or equipment fixes needed.

sec11-card-sec11-F047.question_text: Where should you contest a ticket instead of arguing on the roadside?
sec11-card-sec11-F047.teaching_text: Roadside shoulders are dangerous places for legal debates—established court procedures exist to hear disputes fairly.

sec11-card-sec11-F048.question_text: Does signing and accepting a traffic citation mean you are pleading guilty?
sec11-card-sec11-F048.teaching_text: Your signature simply confirms receipt of the notice and your promise to respond or appear.

sec11-card-sec11-F049.question_text: How should you follow up if you have concerns about an officer's conduct during a stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F049.teaching_text: Reaching out to a department supervisor promptly after the stop uses proper accountability channels safely.

sec12-card-sec12-F001.question_text: What speed rule governs your approach along an interstate entrance ramp?
sec12-card-sec12-F001.teaching_text: Curved cloverleaf ramps tilt sharply—exceeding ramp advisory speeds risks sliding off before reaching the freeway.

sec12-card-sec12-F002.question_text: What is the exact purpose of an interstate acceleration lane before merging?
sec12-card-sec12-F002.teaching_text: Building right up to freeway pace inside the merge strip lets you slip into gaps seamlessly.

sec12-card-sec12-F003.question_text: Why avoid merging onto an interstate far faster or slower than surrounding traffic?
sec12-card-sec12-F003.teaching_text: Crawling onto a seventy-mile-per-hour freeway forces panic braking or abrupt swerves across multiple lanes.

sec12-card-sec12-F004.question_text: Who holds right-of-way at an interstate on-ramp, and how should you blend into traffic?
sec12-card-sec12-F004.teaching_text: Through freeway traffic owns the lane—never swerve abruptly across solid gore lines expecting trucks to brake.

sec12-card-sec12-F005.question_text: What small step finishes every interstate merge?
sec12-card-sec12-F005.teaching_text: Gentle lane angles rarely auto-cancel turn stalks, and a lingering left blinker misleads faster passing lanes.

sec12-card-sec12-F006.question_text: At least how far ahead of your interstate exit should you already sit in the exit lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F006.teaching_text: Lining up a quarter-mile early eliminates frantic three-lane dives across big-rig bows.

sec12-card-sec12-F007.question_text: Why must you read overhead exit signs carefully even though most ramps leave on the right?
sec12-card-sec12-F007.teaching_text: Urban interchanges occasionally peel off from the far-left lane, catching autopilot right-lane drivers off guard.

sec12-card-sec12-F008.question_text: Which three steps take you cleanly off the main freeway into the deceleration lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F008.teaching_text: Scanning mirrors and your blind spot catches vehicles already riding an extended exit-only auxiliary lane.

sec12-card-sec12-F009.question_text: When should you begin slowing down for an interstate exit, and what follows inside the ramp lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F009.teaching_text: Braking early on the main freeway invites seventy-mile-per-hour rear-enders—wait until clear inside the exit lane.

sec12-card-sec12-F010.question_text: What must you do if you accidentally peel onto the wrong interstate exit ramp?
sec12-card-sec12-F010.teaching_text: Continuing down the ramp costs two minutes to turn around safely, whereas backing up risks fatal ramp hits.

sec12-card-sec12-F011.question_text: What is the only safe and legal response if you drive past your intended interstate exit?
sec12-card-sec12-F011.teaching_text: Backing along a freeway shoulder puts reverse gear straight against seventy-mile-per-hour exiting traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F012.question_text: Which three maneuvers are strictly forbidden on any interstate exit ramp?
sec12-card-sec12-F012.teaching_text: One-way exit ramps carry fast decelerating traffic around blind curves—any stopped or reversed car causes pileups.

sec12-card-sec12-F013.question_text: How do the right lane and left lane divide duties on a standard interstate?
sec12-card-sec12-F013.teaching_text: Keeping through cruisers right and faster passers left maintains smooth, predictable freeway flow.

sec12-card-sec12-F014.question_text: On a multilane interstate, on which sides is overtaking permitted?
sec12-card-sec12-F014.teaching_text: Although left is standard for overtaking, divided same-direction freeway lanes legally allow safe passes either side.

sec12-card-sec12-F015.question_text: Which lane belongs to drivers traveling slower than surrounding interstate traffic?
sec12-card-sec12-F015.teaching_text: Holding the right lane when cruising slower prevents bottlenecks and aggressive tailgating behind you.

sec12-card-sec12-F016.question_text: How must you manage speed while another interstate driver is overtaking you?
sec12-card-sec12-F016.teaching_text: Matching a passer's acceleration pins both vehicles side-by-side inside mutual blind spots.

sec12-card-sec12-F017.question_text: Why avoid lingering side-by-side next to a vehicle you are overtaking on the interstate?
sec12-card-sec12-F017.teaching_text: Pacing beside another car traps your escape path if tire debris or a swerving animal appears.

sec12-card-sec12-F018.question_text: How does the handbook rate cruising inside another vehicle's blind spot?
sec12-card-sec12-F018.teaching_text: If a neighbor checks mirrors quickly without turning their head, your car disappears right before they merge.

sec12-card-sec12-F019.question_text: When cruising in the right interstate lane near an on-ramp, how can you help entering traffic?
sec12-card-sec12-F019.teaching_text: Sliding left one lane when clear eliminates merge friction for accelerating ramp cars and heavy trucks.

sec12-card-sec12-F020.question_text: Which two checks must precede every interstate lane change?
sec12-card-sec12-F020.teaching_text: Even wide-set mirrors miss motorcycles or fast sedans closing rapidly along the next lane.

sec12-card-sec12-F021.question_text: Once mirrors and blind spots check clear, what three steps complete a lane change?
sec12-card-sec12-F021.teaching_text: Forgetting to click off your blinker on flat freeways leaves trailing drivers guessing your next move.

sec12-card-sec12-F022.question_text: What checking and signaling routine applies when moving back into your original lane after passing?
sec12-card-sec12-F022.teaching_text: Never assume the right lane stayed empty—another car may have merged in while you passed.

sec12-card-sec12-F023.question_text: What interstate maximum speed does the handbook give for both daylight and darkness—and what qualifies it?
sec12-card-sec12-F023.teaching_text: Mississippi doesn't lower the statutory interstate number at sunset, yet urban zones and storms still override seventy.

sec12-card-sec12-F024.question_text: What two speed boundaries govern interstate driving alongside the maximum limit?
sec12-card-sec12-F024.teaching_text: Slowing appropriately in storms stays safe, whereas crawling below the forty-mile minimum on dry pavement creates hazards.

sec12-card-sec12-F025.question_text: At least how many car lengths of following space does the handbook specify at seventy versus fifty miles per hour?
sec12-card-sec12-F025.teaching_text: Both freeway benchmarks follow Mississippi's clean formula of one vehicle length per ten miles per hour.

sec12-card-sec12-F026.question_text: Where must you move your vehicle after an interstate crash or mechanical breakdown?
sec12-card-sec12-F026.teaching_text: Clearing every inch of tire off seventy-mile-per-hour travel asphalt cuts secondary rear-end crash odds dramatically.

sec12-card-sec12-F027.question_text: Which lights must stay illuminated after a nighttime crash or breakdown on an interstate?
sec12-card-sec12-F027.teaching_text: Flashing hazard lights warn high-speed drivers from afar that your shoulder silhouette is stationary, not moving.

sec12-card-sec12-F028.question_text: How do you signal passing patrols and motorists that your broken-down interstate car needs help?
sec12-card-sec12-F028.teaching_text: Blinking hazard flashers communicate mechanical distress cleanly without anyone stepping outside into freeway windblast.

sec12-card-sec12-F029.question_text: Which four outside-the-car actions must a stranded interstate driver never take?
sec12-card-sec12-F029.teaching_text: Freeway shoulders see drifted mirrors and fatigued drivers—stepping into traffic, walking, crossing, or hitchhiking turns deadly.

sec12-card-sec12-F030.question_text: Where and how does Mississippi's handbook advise a stranded interstate driver to wait for help?
sec12-card-sec12-F030.teaching_text: Steel cabin pillars plus locked doors shield you from both highway traffic and strangers until troopers arrive.

sec12-card-sec12-F031.question_text: What visibility gap sits directly behind a large tractor-trailer?
sec12-card-sec12-F031.teaching_text: Semis have no inside rearview mirror—hugging a trailer's rear doors hides your entire car.

sec12-card-sec12-F032.question_text: How can you tell instantly whether a large truck's driver can see your car?
sec12-card-sec12-F032.teaching_text: Spotting the trucker's face or side mirror glass confirms line-of-sight—otherwise drop back immediately.

sec12-card-sec12-F033.question_text: What should you do if you aren't sure which interchange ramp enters the interstate properly?
sec12-card-sec12-F033.teaching_text: Guessing at a divided cloverleaf risks turning up an off-ramp straight into wrong-way freeway traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F034.question_text: When is it safe to drive onto a complex interstate interchange ramp?
sec12-card-sec12-F034.teaching_text: Reading green guide signs and Do Not Enter shields beforehand beats freezing mid-ramp in fast traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F001.question_text: Why is lingering closely around a semi-truck or bus risky for smaller cars?
sec13-card-sec13-F001.teaching_text: Tall cabs and long trailers create blind zones where commercial drivers cannot spot or react to nearby cars.

sec13-card-sec13-F002.question_text: How should you position your car when trailing behind a large truck?
sec13-card-sec13-F002.teaching_text: Hanging back far enough to stay visible in the rig's side mirrors keeps you out of rear blind spots.

sec13-card-sec13-F003.question_text: What does it mean if you cannot see a large truck's front-mounted side mirrors from your driver's seat?
sec13-card-sec13-F003.teaching_text: Losing sight of the rig's side mirrors guarantees your car is tucked invisibly inside a blind zone.

sec13-card-sec13-F004.question_text: Why must you switch to low beams when following a large truck at night?
sec13-card-sec13-F004.teaching_text: Oversized commercial side mirrors bounce high-beam glare straight into the trucker's eyes at night.

sec13-card-sec13-F005.question_text: Why should you leave extra room when stopped behind a heavy truck facing uphill?
sec13-card-sec13-F005.teaching_text: Loaded trucks can drift backward slightly as clutches engage on an incline, crunching bumpers parked too close.

sec13-card-sec13-F006.question_text: Where inside your own lane should you stop behind a large truck on an uphill grade?
sec13-card-sec13-F006.teaching_text: Positioning toward the left edge of your lane puts your hood inside the driver's left mirror.

sec13-card-sec13-F007.question_text: How does a large truck's stopping distance compare with a passenger car's, and how should you follow?
sec13-card-sec13-F007.teaching_text: Tens of thousands of pounds stretch truck braking distances, while tailgating also blocks your view of hazards ahead.

sec13-card-sec13-F008.question_text: What checks and conditions are required before pulling into the passing lane around a large vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-F008.teaching_text: Commit to passing a long trailer only inside a legal passing zone after verifying clear lanes ahead and behind.

sec13-card-sec13-F009.question_text: On a flat road, how much longer does overtaking a large vehicle take compared to passing a car?
sec13-card-sec13-F009.teaching_text: Passing a seventy-foot trailer on flat pavement demands noticeably more open sightline than overtaking a compact sedan.

sec13-card-sec13-F010.question_text: How does an uphill grade typically affect passing a heavy truck?
sec13-card-sec13-F010.teaching_text: Steep climbs sap momentum from heavy freight, shortening the distance needed to clear a legal pass.

sec13-card-sec13-F011.question_text: What happens to a heavy truck's speed on a downhill grade, and what smart choice remains?
sec13-card-sec13-F011.teaching_text: Gravity accelerates loaded trailers on downgrades, making patience for a flatter passing stretch the smarter play.

sec13-card-sec13-F012.question_text: After overtaking a large truck, what must appear in your rearview mirror before you merge back?
sec13-card-sec13-F012.teaching_text: Cutting back before spotting the rig's front tires on the asphalt steals the trucker's braking cushion.

sec13-card-sec13-F013.question_text: What should you do with your speed right after pulling back in front of a large vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-F013.teaching_text: Lifting off the gas right in front of forty tons forces the trucker onto air brakes.

sec13-card-sec13-F014.question_text: How should you steer and manage speed when a large truck is overtaking your car?
sec13-card-sec13-F014.teaching_text: Keeping over away from the rig while holding constant speed clears the windy pass window fast.

sec13-card-sec13-F015.question_text: Where should you position your car when meeting an oncoming semi-truck, and why?
sec13-card-sec13-F015.teaching_text: Edging right inside your lane cuts wind blast turbulence and adds buffer against wide mirrors.

sec13-card-sec13-F016.question_text: Why might a large truck swing toward the left just before making a right turn?
sec13-card-sec13-F016.teaching_text: Long trailers track tighter than cab wheels, forcing drivers to swing left first to clear the right curb.

sec13-card-sec13-F017.question_text: What pass must you never attempt when a truck ahead could be setting up a right turn?
sec13-card-sec13-F017.teaching_text: Sneaking into the right-side gap as a semi swings wide pins your car between trailer wheels and curb.

sec13-card-sec13-F018.question_text: How does Mississippi law classify a bicycle riding on a public road?
sec13-card-sec13-F018.teaching_text: Bicycles on public pavement count as vehicles whose riders hold the same rights and traffic duties as motorists.

sec13-card-sec13-F019.question_text: How should you treat an approaching cyclist when yielding right-of-way at an intersection?
sec13-card-sec13-F019.teaching_text: Turning left across an oncoming bike because it looks narrow causes severe intersection crashes.

sec13-card-sec13-F020.question_text: What is the minimum side clearance Mississippi requires when overtaking a bicycle?
sec13-card-sec13-F020.teaching_text: Giving cyclists at least three feet of lateral space absorbs wobble around potholes or road grit.

sec13-card-sec13-F021.question_text: When does Mississippi's bicycle-sharing guidance allow overtaking a same-direction cyclist inside a no-passing zone?
sec13-card-sec13-F021.teaching_text: You may ease past a slow bicycle in a no-passing stretch only when sightlines and opposing traffic make it safe.

sec13-card-sec13-F022.question_text: After overtaking a cyclist traveling your direction, when may you turn right?
sec13-card-sec13-F022.teaching_text: Misjudging bike speed right after passing hooks the rider into your passenger fender as you turn.

sec13-card-sec13-F023.question_text: What turning shortcut in front of a bicyclist is strictly off-limits?
sec13-card-sec13-F023.teaching_text: Whipping across a bike rider's nose to catch a side street leaves thin bicycle tires zero room to stop.

sec13-card-sec13-F024.question_text: How should you use lanes when overtaking a bicycle instead of squeezing beside the rider?
sec13-card-sec13-F024.teaching_text: Slowing down and moving cleanly into the next lane beats threading mirrors inches from handlebars.

sec13-card-sec13-F025.question_text: What must you do if oncoming cars prevent passing a bicyclist with safe clearance?
sec13-card-sec13-F025.teaching_text: Ten seconds of patience behind the cyclist prevents pinching a vulnerable human between two bumpers.

sec13-card-sec13-F026.question_text: Even without physical contact, how can passing too closely destabilize a bicyclist?
sec13-card-sec13-F026.teaching_text: High-speed air push and suction off an SUV or truck can knock a lightweight bike off balance.

sec13-card-sec13-F027.question_text: What intersection controls and turn-signaling duties apply to bicyclists on Mississippi roads?
sec13-card-sec13-F027.teaching_text: Predictable road sharing depends on cyclists obeying stoplights and stop signs while signaling turns by hand or arm.

sec13-card-sec13-F028.question_text: Where in the roadway should a cyclist normally ride, and how far from the pavement edge?
sec13-card-sec13-F028.teaching_text: Riding two to four feet inside the right edge keeps tires off broken pavement while leaving room to steer.

sec13-card-sec13-F029.question_text: Which two situations allow a cyclist to move away from the right edge toward the left?
sec13-card-sec13-F029.teaching_text: Broken glass, storm grates, parked cars, or slower riders justify a cyclist taking space farther left.

sec13-card-sec13-F030.question_text: For which two intersection paths may a cyclist move farther into the travel lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F030.teaching_text: Moving inward avoids right-turn-only pockets when continuing straight and sets up safe left turns.

sec13-card-sec13-F031.question_text: How fast can an experienced cyclist travel, and what misjudgment does that create for drivers?
sec13-card-sec13-F031.teaching_text: Seasoned riders cruising at twenty to twenty-five miles per hour reach intersections far sooner than motorists expect.

sec13-card-sec13-F032.question_text: Why should cyclists wear a bicycle helmet, and where might wearing one be mandatory?
sec13-card-sec13-F032.teaching_text: Certified bike helmets slash serious head-trauma risk, and city or county ordinances may require them legally.

sec13-card-sec13-F033.question_text: Should a bicyclist ride with the flow of traffic or facing oncoming cars?
sec13-card-sec13-F033.teaching_text: Riding against traffic puts bikes where driveway and intersection drivers never look and compounds crash speed.

sec13-card-sec13-F034.question_text: What riding pattern helps motorists anticipate a cyclist's path safely?
sec13-card-sec13-F034.teaching_text: Holding a straight, predictable line instead of darting between bumpers lets drivers leave consistent passing space.

sec13-card-sec13-F035.question_text: What must a cyclist do before rolling into a street from a driveway, alley, or behind parked cars?
sec13-card-sec13-F035.teaching_text: Darting out from behind parked SUVs gives street traffic zero warning unless the rider stops and yields first.

sec13-card-sec13-F036.question_text: What gear helps motorists spot a cyclist during the day and after dark?
sec13-card-sec13-F036.teaching_text: High-contrast daytime clothes plus bright front and rear lamps with reflective gear at night prevent dark-road strikes.

sec13-card-sec13-F037.question_text: Which three carriers should cyclists use to haul packages or gear safely?
sec13-card-sec13-F037.teaching_text: Dangling bags off one handlebar upsets steering and braking, while baskets, racks, and panniers keep both hands free.

sec13-card-sec13-F038.question_text: When is carrying a passenger on a bicycle prohibited?
sec13-card-sec13-F038.teaching_text: Perching a friend on handlebars or pegs overwhelms brakes and destabilizes a frame built for one rider.

sec13-card-sec13-F039.question_text: What rule governs holding onto or attaching a bicycle to another moving vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-F039.teaching_text: One bump or brake tap while being towed throws a cyclist straight under moving vehicle tires.

sec13-card-sec13-F040.question_text: What should a cyclist do on a narrow stretch when trailing cars cannot pass and a line builds?
sec13-card-sec13-F040.teaching_text: Stepping aside briefly at a safe turnout clears frustrated queues before someone tries a blind pass.

sec13-card-sec13-F041.question_text: Does Mississippi law allow cyclists to ride two abreast, and what limit applies?
sec13-card-sec13-F041.teaching_text: Side-by-side riding is legal under state law only while it does not block normal, reasonable traffic flow.

sec13-card-sec13-F042.question_text: How should cyclists position themselves on a roadway with multiple lanes?
sec13-card-sec13-F042.teaching_text: Straddling lane stripes on a multi-lane road blocks two streams of traffic at once.

sec14-card-sec14-F001.question_text: Which three items must every Mississippi resident's vehicle carry or maintain legally?
sec14-card-sec14-F001.teaching_text: Operating a resident vehicle without a Mississippi tag, certificate of title, and adequate liability coverage invites penalties.

sec14-card-sec14-F002.question_text: When must a motorist carry a valid driver's license?
sec14-card-sec14-F002.teaching_text: Even if your car's tag and insurance are spotless, you must carry your valid driver's license whenever driving.

sec14-card-sec14-F003.question_text: In which county must you buy your vehicle tag, and which local official handles tag information?
sec14-card-sec14-F003.teaching_text: Tags must be purchased in your county of residence through the local County Tax Collector.

sec14-card-sec14-F004.question_text: How many days do you have to get a Mississippi license plate after moving a vehicle into the state?
sec14-card-sec14-F004.teaching_text: Waiting past thirty days after bringing your car into Mississippi triggers late tag penalties.

sec14-card-sec14-F005.question_text: Where on the vehicle must a Mississippi license plate be mounted?
sec14-card-sec14-F005.teaching_text: Tossing your tag onto the dashboard instead of bolting it to the rear violates display law.

sec14-card-sec14-F006.question_text: What rule applies to trailer hitches, frames, emblems, or decorations around your license plate?
sec14-card-sec14-F006.teaching_text: Novelty frames or tow balls blocking even one character on your rear plate can draw a traffic stop.

sec14-card-sec14-F007.question_text: From how far away must your license-plate light make tag characters readable at night?
sec14-card-sec14-F007.teaching_text: A burned-out rear tag bulb fails the sixty-foot nighttime readability rule and gives officers probable cause.

sec14-card-sec14-F008.question_text: Which ownership document is required for every vehicle in Mississippi?
sec14-card-sec14-F008.teaching_text: A certificate of title establishes legal vehicle ownership before plates or transfers can go forward.

sec14-card-sec14-F009.question_text: Who supplies the title application when you buy from a new-car or used-car dealership?
sec14-card-sec14-F009.teaching_text: Licensed new and used dealerships prepare the title application directly for vehicles sold off their lots.

sec14-card-sec14-F010.question_text: Which two supporting records does the manual list when backing a title application?
sec14-card-sec14-F010.teaching_text: Bringing a bill of sale plus two years of prior tag receipts satisfies that handbook title-application rule.

sec14-card-sec14-F011.question_text: What document is needed to apply for a Mississippi title on a car brought from another state?
sec14-card-sec14-F011.teaching_text: Transferring ownership registration into Mississippi requires presenting the vehicle's existing out-of-state title.

sec14-card-sec14-F012.question_text: Which two groups must qualify in order to accept Mississippi title applications?
sec14-card-sec14-F012.teaching_text: Licensed auto dealers and county tax collectors serve as qualified intake agents for vehicle title paperwork.

sec14-card-sec14-F013.question_text: Which lending organizations can also qualify as designated title-application agents?
sec14-card-sec14-F013.teaching_text: Auto lenders and banks can qualify as designated agents to file title applications when financing vehicles.

sec14-card-sec14-F014.question_text: What check is required if your Mississippi-registered car has aftermarket window tint film installed?
sec14-card-sec14-F014.teaching_text: Aftermarket window film must pass light-transmission testing at an authorized Mississippi tint inspection station.

sec14-card-sec14-F015.question_text: Which two compliance items are required once aftermarket-tinted windows pass inspection?
sec14-card-sec14-F015.teaching_text: Passing tint inspection gives you both a paper compliance certificate and a windshield decal.

sec14-card-sec14-F016.question_text: What fee does the Mississippi manual list for the window-tint compliance certificate and decal?
sec14-card-sec14-F016.teaching_text: Test writers check exact inspection fees, and tint stations collect five dollars to issue your compliance sticker and certificate.

sec14-card-sec14-F017.question_text: On which corner of the windshield must the window-tint compliance decal be placed?
sec14-card-sec14-F017.teaching_text: Sticking the tint decal at the lower-left windshield corner lets officers verify compliance without obstructing center view.

sec14-card-sec14-F018.question_text: Where inside the cabin must you keep your paper window-tint compliance certificate?
sec14-card-sec14-F018.teaching_text: Keeping the tint certificate on the dash or inside the glove compartment makes roadside verification quick.

sec14-card-sec14-F019.question_text: Which vehicles operated in Mississippi are required to carry liability insurance?
sec14-card-sec14-F019.teaching_text: Mandatory liability coverage applies across every motor vehicle operated on Mississippi roads.

sec14-card-sec14-F020.question_text: What are Mississippi's minimum liability coverage amounts for injury to one person and for two or more people?
sec14-card-sec14-F020.teaching_text: Policies must cover at least twenty-five thousand dollars for one injured person and fifty thousand for multiple people.

sec14-card-sec14-F021.question_text: What is Mississippi's minimum liability coverage for damaging another person's property in one crash?
sec14-card-sec14-F021.teaching_text: Pairing twenty-five thousand in property coverage with the injury floors forms Mississippi's twenty-five, fifty, twenty-five baseline.

sec14-card-sec14-F022.question_text: What insurance proof must insured owners keep inside each covered vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F022.teaching_text: Leaving an expired card in the console while the new one sits at home risks an avoidable ticket.

sec14-card-sec14-F023.question_text: What immediate consequences can follow failing to show insurance proof at a traffic stop or crash?
sec14-card-sec14-F023.teaching_text: Being unable to produce proof of liability coverage during a stop or collision exposes you to citations and fines.

sec14-card-sec14-F024.question_text: Must your Mississippi insurance card be printed on paper, or is digital display allowed?
sec14-card-sec14-F024.teaching_text: Mississippi allows motorists to show valid insurance proof electronically on a smartphone or mobile device.

sec14-card-sec14-F025.question_text: What license penalty can strike a driver who cannot show insurance after a crash?
sec14-card-sec14-F025.teaching_text: Beyond citations, lacking proof of coverage after an accident puts your driver's license at risk of suspension.

sec14-card-sec14-F026.question_text: What straightforward proof avoids a post-crash insurance suspension if you merely lacked the card on scene?
sec14-card-sec14-F026.teaching_text: Showing that adequate liability insurance was already active at the exact moment of the crash stops suspension.

sec14-card-sec14-F027.question_text: What dollar value in a deposit certificate or securities does the manual list as post-crash financial responsibility?
sec14-card-sec14-F027.teaching_text: Watch the number carefully because the listed post-crash deposit certificate or securities figure is fifteen thousand dollars.

sec14-card-sec14-F028.question_text: What payment commitment must a Mississippi self-insurance certificate include?
sec14-card-sec14-F028.teaching_text: Self-insured fleet owners must formally agree to pay legal judgments equal to a standard owner's policy.

sec14-card-sec14-F029.question_text: How many vehicles must an owner have to qualify as a self-insurer in Mississippi?
sec14-card-sec14-F029.teaching_text: Notice it says more than twenty-five vehicles, meaning twenty-six or more rather than a tiny household fleet.

sec14-card-sec14-F030.question_text: Which three financial guarantees sufficient to cover crash damages may the department accept after a collision?
sec14-card-sec14-F030.teaching_text: Depositing enough cash, marketable securities, or a corporate bond to cover collision damages satisfies financial responsibility rules.

sec14-card-sec14-F031.question_text: Which three fault or payment outcomes can also prevent a post-crash license suspension?
sec14-card-sec14-F031.teaching_text: A signed liability release, a final non-liability ruling, or proof the other party paid damages avoids suspension.

sec14-card-sec14-F032.question_text: What insurance purchase and filing must an uninsured driver make after causing an injury or damage crash?
sec14-card-sec14-F032.teaching_text: Causing an injury or property-damage wreck while uninsured triggers a mandate to buy liability coverage and file proof.

sec14-card-sec14-F033.question_text: What two standards must that mandatory post-crash liability policy satisfy?
sec14-card-sec14-F033.teaching_text: Your filed policy must carry at least Mississippi's minimum limits and come from an insurer licensed in Mississippi.

sec14-card-sec14-F034.question_text: For how long from the crash date must filed liability coverage stay active after an uninsured at-fault wreck?
sec14-card-sec14-F034.teaching_text: Dropping your filed policy early triggers trouble because post-crash coverage must remain continuous for three years.

sec15-card-sec15-F001.question_text: What is Mississippi's legal rule on driving while impaired by alcohol or drugs?
sec15-card-sec15-F001.teaching_text: Getting behind the wheel impaired by alcohol or any drug violates Mississippi criminal traffic law.
