sec15-card-sec15-F002.question_text: Which three mental traits can alcohol alter, and what physical response does it slow?
sec15-card-sec15-F002.teaching_text: Even one or two drinks shift temperament, cloud risk judgment, and stretch brake reaction times dangerously.

sec15-card-sec15-F003.question_text: Besides staying out of the driver's seat yourself after drinking, what else must you refuse to allow?
sec15-card-sec15-F003.teaching_text: Handing your keys to a buddy who also drank puts two lives and everyone ahead in danger.

sec15-card-sec15-F004.question_text: How can marijuana, street drugs, or even prescription medicines affect your driving skills?
sec15-card-sec15-F004.teaching_text: Pharmacy bottles and cannabis distort split-second braking reflexes and risk assessment just like alcohol.

sec15-card-sec15-F005.question_text: What legal consequence can follow smoking medical cannabis inside a vehicle or controlling a vehicle impaired?
sec15-card-sec15-F005.teaching_text: Lighting medical cannabis in a cabin or controlling a car while impaired breaks state law and brings arrest.

sec15-card-sec15-F006.question_text: Does holding a valid doctor's prescription or medical-cannabis card make impaired driving legal?
sec15-card-sec15-F006.teaching_text: Officers judge whether you can operate safely, so neither pharmacy labels nor medical-cannabis cards excuse impairment.

sec15-card-sec15-F007.question_text: What testing agreement do you automatically accept simply by driving on Mississippi roads?
sec15-card-sec15-F007.teaching_text: Turning the key on public pavement triggers automatic legal consent to chemical screening for intoxicating substances.

sec15-card-sec15-F008.question_text: When may a Mississippi officer ask a driver to take a breath or chemical screening?
sec15-card-sec15-F008.teaching_text: Weaving lanes, slurred speech, or odor gives an officer good reason to request breath or chemical screening.

sec15-card-sec15-F009.question_text: What three-letter abbreviation stands for blood alcohol content in the manual?
sec15-card-sec15-F009.teaching_text: Every DUI chart in the Mississippi manual uses BAC to measure alcohol concentration in your bloodstream.

sec15-card-sec15-F010.question_text: What BAC threshold triggers regular DUI classification for drivers aged twenty-one or older?
sec15-card-sec15-F010.teaching_text: Hitting that eight-hundredths adult threshold or above triggers per-se regular DUI charges regardless of how sober you feel.

sec15-card-sec15-F011.question_text: What much lower BAC threshold applies to Mississippi drivers younger than twenty-one?
sec15-card-sec15-F011.teaching_text: Even half a drink can push an under-twenty-one driver up to that strict two-hundredths underage mark.

sec15-card-sec15-F012.question_text: What happens to your physical driver's license on the spot if you refuse a breath or chemical check?
sec15-card-sec15-F012.teaching_text: Saying no to chemical screening forces you to hand your plastic license directly to the officer immediately.

sec15-card-sec15-F013.question_text: How many days does the temporary driving receipt last after a breath or chemical refusal?
sec15-card-sec15-F013.teaching_text: Watch the receipt split closely because refusal gives forty-five days while failing BAC gives thirty days.

sec15-card-sec15-F014.question_text: Where does the officer forward your seized license and sworn report after a chemical refusal?
sec15-card-sec15-F014.teaching_text: Forwarding your card and sworn refusal report to the Public Safety Commissioner starts administrative suspension review.

sec15-card-sec15-F015.question_text: How long is the baseline administrative license suspension described for refusing a breath or chemical check?
sec15-card-sec15-F015.teaching_text: Refusing chemical screening triggers an automatic ninety-day administrative suspension even before court DUI penalties.

sec15-card-sec15-F016.question_text: How are suspensions affected if you refuse chemical screening again after a prior conviction or non-adjudication?
sec15-card-sec15-F016.teaching_text: Prior DUI convictions or non-adjudications stretch suspension length beyond ninety days on a later refusal.

sec15-card-sec15-F017.question_text: For how many days is the officer's temporary driving receipt valid when your BAC hits the legal limit?
sec15-card-sec15-F017.teaching_text: Testing at or above your legal BAC cap yields a thirty-day paper receipt after the officer takes your card.

sec15-card-sec15-F018.question_text: Which age group and minimum BAC reading anchor the manual's regular DUI penalty schedule?
sec15-card-sec15-F018.teaching_text: Drivers twenty-one and up at zero point zero eight percent or above face the standard adult DUI schedule.

sec15-card-sec15-F019.question_text: How is a first regular DUI classified, and what fine range does the manual list?
sec15-card-sec15-F019.teaching_text: Even a first conviction goes on your record as a misdemeanor carrying fines starting at two hundred fifty dollars.

sec15-card-sec15-F020.question_text: What maximum jail stay and license suspension length apply to a first-offense regular DUI?
sec15-card-sec15-F020.teaching_text: First-offense regular DUI carries up to forty-eight hours behind bars plus a one-hundred-twenty-day license suspension.

sec15-card-sec15-F021.question_text: Within what lookback window is a second DUI counted, how is it classed, and what is the fine range?
sec15-card-sec15-F021.teaching_text: A second DUI within five years stays a misdemeanor while jumping fines to six hundred through fifteen hundred dollars.

sec15-card-sec15-F022.question_text: What jail range and license suspension apply to a second regular DUI within five years?
sec15-card-sec15-F022.teaching_text: Second offenders face five days to six months in jail alongside a full one-year license suspension.
sec15-card-sec15-F022.must_match_memory_hook: Five days to six months, year

visual_sync.text_span: Five days to six months, year

sec15-card-sec15-F023.question_text: How does charge severity shift on a third DUI within five years, and what fine range applies?
sec15-card-sec15-F023.teaching_text: Picking up a third DUI inside five years escalates the charge to a felony fined up to five thousand dollars.

sec15-card-sec15-F024.question_text: What prison term and license loss follow a third-offense regular DUI within five years?
sec15-card-sec15-F024.teaching_text: Conviction brings one to five years in Corrections custody with driving privileges revoked for the entire sentence.

sec15-card-sec15-F025.question_text: After finishing prison on a third-offense DUI, what driving restriction applies and for how long?
sec15-card-sec15-F025.teaching_text: Release from custody allows driving only on an ignition-interlock restricted license for three full years.

sec15-card-sec15-F026.question_text: Does the five-year lookback still limit a fourth DUI, and what fine range applies?
sec15-card-sec15-F026.teaching_text: Fourth and later DUIs count across your entire lifetime regardless of elapsed years, carrying three-to-ten-thousand-dollar fines.

sec15-card-sec15-F027.question_text: What custody term and license penalty apply to a fourth or subsequent DUI?
sec15-card-sec15-F027.teaching_text: Fourth-time offenders serve two to ten years in custody and lose driving privileges throughout the sentence.

sec15-card-sec15-F028.question_text: After serving custody for a fourth or later DUI, what license limit applies and for how long?
sec15-card-sec15-F028.teaching_text: Returning from a fourth-offense sentence restricts you solely to an interlock-equipped license for ten years.

sec15-card-sec15-F029.question_text: Which age group and exact BAC band fall under Mississippi's Zero Tolerance penalty table?
sec15-card-sec15-F029.teaching_text: Zero Tolerance covers drivers under twenty-one from zero point zero two percent up to just below point zero eight.
sec15-card-sec15-F029.must_match_memory_hook: Under twenty-one, point two to eight

visual_sync.text_span: Under twenty-one, point two to eight

sec15-card-sec15-F030.question_text: How is a driver younger than twenty-one charged if their BAC reaches zero point zero eight percent or higher?
sec15-card-sec15-F030.teaching_text: Youth never shields high BAC readings because hitting point zero eight bumps minors straight into regular DUI penalties.

sec15-card-sec15-F031.question_text: What fine and suspension length apply to a first Zero Tolerance DUI offense?
sec15-card-sec15-F031.teaching_text: First-time underage offenders lose their license for four months alongside paying a two-hundred-fifty-dollar court fine.

sec15-card-sec15-F032.question_text: What maximum fine and license suspension apply to a second Zero Tolerance DUI within five years?
sec15-card-sec15-F032.teaching_text: Picking up a second Zero Tolerance offense within five years caps fines at five hundred dollars with a one-year suspension.

sec15-card-sec15-F033.question_text: What is the maximum fine for a third Zero Tolerance DUI within five years?
sec15-card-sec15-F033.teaching_text: A third Zero Tolerance violation inside five years doubles the fine cap to one thousand dollars.

sec15-card-sec15-F034.question_text: How long does the license suspension last on a third Zero Tolerance DUI?
sec15-card-sec15-F034.teaching_text: Notice it says whichever is longer, so a sixteen-year-old waits five years until turning twenty-one.

sec15-card-sec15-F035.question_text: How much extra suspension time gets added when a first DUI or Zero Tolerance conviction includes chemical refusal?
sec15-card-sec15-F035.teaching_text: Refusing the breath check stacks an extra ninety-day suspension right on top of your first-offense DUI penalty.

sec15-card-sec15-F036.question_text: Which two aggravating circumstances make DUI penalties harsher than the baseline tables?
sec15-card-sec15-F036.teaching_text: Driving while already suspended for DUI or causing an injury wreck while impaired triggers stiffer criminal penalties.

sec15-card-sec15-F037.question_text: Which state official holds authority to remove driving privileges for unlawful or unsafe driving?
sec15-card-sec15-F037.teaching_text: Your license remains a conditional privilege that the Public Safety Commissioner can pull for unsafe or illegal driving.

sec15-card-sec15-F038.question_text: When can your license be suspended immediately without holding a preliminary hearing first?
sec15-card-sec15-F038.teaching_text: When court records or solid evidence establish a listed ground, suspension starts first without a pre-suspension hearing.

sec15-card-sec15-F039.question_text: How does an offense that carries mandatory revocation also relate to suspension authority?
sec15-card-sec15-F039.teaching_text: Any conviction severe enough to demand mandatory revocation also empowers immediate administrative suspension action.

sec15-card-sec15-F040.question_text: Which three severe crash outcomes can trigger license suspension for an involved driver?
sec15-card-sec15-F040.teaching_text: Being involved as a driver in a fatal, personal-injury, or major property-damage collision is a listed suspension ground.

sec15-card-sec15-F041.question_text: Which two patterns of dangerous behind-the-wheel behavior are grounds for suspending your license?
sec15-card-sec15-F041.teaching_text: Stacking serious moving violations or driving with habitual recklessness and negligence strips away your license.

sec15-card-sec15-F042.question_text: How do driving unfitness and letting someone misuse your license affect your driving privilege?
sec15-card-sec15-F042.teaching_text: Lending your card to a friend or losing physical or mental fitness to drive both trigger suspension.

sec15-card-sec15-F043.question_text: How can a DUI or serious violation convicted in another state affect your Mississippi license?
sec15-card-sec15-F043.teaching_text: Interstate compacts share convictions, so an out-of-state DUI hits your Mississippi license like a local offense.

sec15-card-sec15-F044.question_text: What happens if someone gets a Mississippi license while suspended in another state?
sec15-card-sec15-F044.teaching_text: Slipping past an active out-of-state suspension to get a card is itself grounds for suspension.

sec15-card-sec15-F045.question_text: Which family-court financial obligation can get your Mississippi driver's license suspended if unpaid?
sec15-card-sec15-F045.teaching_text: Even with zero speeding tickets, falling behind on court-ordered child support can suspend your license.

sec15-card-sec15-F046.question_text: What license penalty follows a driving-related manslaughter or negligent-homicide conviction?
sec15-card-sec15-F046.teaching_text: Manslaughter or negligent homicide with a vehicle triggers mandatory one-year revocation rather than a brief suspension.

sec15-card-sec15-F047.question_text: What license penalty applies when a motor vehicle is used in committing any felony?
sec15-card-sec15-F047.teaching_text: Using a car or truck during a felony offense mandates a full one-year revocation of driving privileges.

sec15-card-sec15-F048.question_text: What license consequence hits a driver convicted of failing to stop and render required aid at a crash?
sec15-card-sec15-F048.teaching_text: Fleeing a crash scene without rendering required assistance costs your license through a one-year revocation.

sec15-card-sec15-F049.question_text: What happens to your license for perjury or lying to the department about vehicle ownership or operation?
sec15-card-sec15-F049.teaching_text: Swearing false statements to licensing officials about owning or operating a vehicle triggers a one-year revocation.

sec15-card-sec15-F050.question_text: How many reckless-driving convictions within twelve months trigger a mandatory one-year revocation?
sec15-card-sec15-F050.teaching_text: Racking up three reckless-driving convictions inside a single twelve-month span triggers mandatory one-year revocation.

sec15-card-sec15-F051.question_text: Does your license turn back on automatically when a suspension or revocation period ends?
sec15-card-sec15-F051.teaching_text: Driving the morning your calendar wait ends is still illegal until reinstatement fees and steps are completed.

sec15-card-sec15-F052.question_text: What reinstatement fee applies after an Implied Consent, DUI, or controlled-substance conviction?
sec15-card-sec15-F052.teaching_text: Implied Consent, DUI, and drug-law suspensions share the highest tier at one hundred seventy-five dollars.

sec15-card-sec15-F053.question_text: What reinstatement fee does the manual list after a suspension for unpaid child support?
sec15-card-sec15-F053.teaching_text: Clearing an unpaid child-support suspension carries a dedicated twenty-five-dollar reinstatement charge rather than higher DUI tiers.

sec15-card-sec15-F054.question_text: What reinstatement fee applies to standard suspensions outside the DUI, drug, or child-support tiers?
sec15-card-sec15-F054.teaching_text: Keep the three numbers straight with one seventy-five for DUI, twenty-five for support, and one hundred otherwise.

sec15-card-sec15-F055.question_text: Which single payment instrument is accepted for mailed reinstatement fees, and which three are rejected?
sec15-card-sec15-F055.teaching_text: Never mail cash, personal checks, or money orders because only a cashier's check to DPS is accepted.

sec15-card-sec15-F056.question_text: What court document is required before reinstating after failing to appear or leaving your license for bond?
sec15-card-sec15-F056.teaching_text: Resolving a missed court date or bond-deposit license requires obtaining a judge's corrected court abstract.

sec15-card-sec15-F057.question_text: To which bureau and Mississippi city are mailed DUI or unpaid-ticket reinstatement payments sent?
sec15-card-sec15-F057.teaching_text: Sending mailed DUI or unpaid-ticket cashier's checks to the wrong office delays clearing your driving record.

sec15-card-sec15-F058.question_text: Where is discarding solid waste legal on public roads, rights-of-way, or public lands?
sec15-card-sec15-F058.teaching_text: Tossing wrappers or bottles onto shoulders or public land is illegal outside authorized receptacles or disposal areas.

sec15-card-sec15-F059.question_text: Who can be cited under Mississippi's littering law when trash is thrown from a motor vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F059.teaching_text: Even if a passenger flicked the cup out, law enforcement can hold the owner, operator, or both responsible.

sec15-card-sec15-F060.question_text: What is Mississippi's rule on dumping solid waste into rivers, lakes, or state waters?
sec15-card-sec15-F060.teaching_text: Throwing trash off bridges, boat ramps, or shorelines into Mississippi waters is flatly prohibited.

sec15-card-sec15-F061.question_text: What three conditions must be met before disposing of waste on private property?
sec15-card-sec15-F061.teaching_text: Even on private land you need prior written owner permission and cannot create a public nuisance or break laws.

sec15-card-sec15-F062.question_text: What rule governs discharging raw human waste from a vehicle, camper, boat, train, or plane?
sec15-card-sec15-F062.teaching_text: Dumping raw sewage onto public or private Mississippi land or waterways is illegal from every transport mode.

sec15-card-sec15-F063.question_text: Are you off the hook if you direct or cause someone else to dump or spill prohibited waste?
sec15-card-sec15-F063.teaching_text: Directing or paying someone else to dump illegal trash puts you on the hook under state littering law.

sec16-card-sec16-F001.question_text: Which federal service and cabinet department administer the Natchez Trace Parkway?
sec16-card-sec16-F001.teaching_text: Unlike state highways, the Natchez Trace Parkway runs under the National Park Service inside the Interior Department.

sec16-card-sec16-F002.question_text: What historic route does the Natchez Trace Parkway commemorate?
sec16-card-sec16-F002.teaching_text: Scenic parkway miles preserve and honor an early frontier travel corridor vital to Old Southwest history.

sec16-card-sec16-F003.question_text: Which vehicles are barred from the Natchez Trace Parkway, and how is road entry designed?
sec16-card-sec16-F003.teaching_text: Keeping commercial freight trucks off the Trace and limiting access ramps preserves calm scenic driving.

sec16-card-sec16-F004.question_text: Who patrols the Natchez Trace Parkway to protect resources and help motorists?
sec16-card-sec16-F004.teaching_text: Federal Park Rangers patrol the Trace corridor to enforce parkway safety and assist stranded travelers.

sec16-card-sec16-F005.question_text: To whom should you report a crash, wildfire, or emergency along the Natchez Trace Parkway?
sec16-card-sec16-F005.teaching_text: Alerting the closest Park Ranger dispatches federal emergency response directly along the limited-access parkway.

sec16-card-sec16-F006.question_text: Which two key details should you give when calling for Park Ranger help on the Trace?
sec16-card-sec16-F006.teaching_text: Sharing what happened plus your approximate milepost or landmark gets Rangers to the right stretch fast.

sec16-card-sec16-F007.question_text: How do federal regulations and state traffic laws interact on the Natchez Trace Parkway?
sec16-card-sec16-F007.teaching_text: Federal parkway regulations govern facilities and road use while Mississippi state traffic laws apply right alongside.

sec16-card-sec16-F008.question_text: What is the maximum speed limit on the Natchez Trace Parkway unless posted lower?
sec16-card-sec16-F008.teaching_text: Cruising at interstate speeds draws federal citations because the Parkway tops out at fifty miles per hour.

sec16-card-sec16-F009.question_text: What duty applies to posted traffic and park signs along the Natchez Trace Parkway?
sec16-card-sec16-F009.teaching_text: Scenic overlooks, wildlife zones, and historic stops post custom Parkway controls that every driver must follow.

sec16-card-sec16-F010.question_text: What rule governs hunting or discharging firearms on Natchez Trace Parkway lands?
sec16-card-sec16-F010.teaching_text: National Park corridor lands protect visitors and wildlife by outlawing hunting and firearm use along the Trace.

sec16-card-sec16-F011.question_text: How must you handle cigarettes, matches, and trash while driving the Parkway?
sec16-card-sec16-F011.teaching_text: Flicking a glowing cigarette or match from a car window ignites dry roadside grass and violates parkway law.

sec16-card-sec16-F012.question_text: Who should you ask whenever you are unsure about a Natchez Trace Parkway regulation?
sec16-card-sec16-F012.teaching_text: Checking with a Park Ranger beforehand beats guessing wrong on camping, parking, or parkway use rules.

sec16-card-sec16-F013.question_text: In which court system are traffic or facility violations on the Natchez Trace Parkway tried?
sec16-card-sec16-F013.teaching_text: Because the Parkway is federal National Park property, citations land in federal court rather than municipal court.

sec16-card-sec16-F014.question_text: Which national industry organization operates the Share the Road highway-safety program?
sec16-card-sec16-F014.teaching_text: The American Trucking Associations runs Share the Road to reduce car-and-semi collisions nationwide.

sec16-card-sec16-F015.question_text: Who leads instruction in the Share the Road program to help drivers avoid crashes?
sec16-card-sec16-F015.teaching_text: Million-mile professional truckers show everyday motorists real blind-spot and braking realities from the cab seat.

sec16-card-sec16-F016.question_text: How do Share the Road demonstrations physically illustrate common highway crash traps?
sec16-card-sec16-F016.teaching_text: Staging passenger cars beside full-size rigs in simulated highway lanes lets people sit in the cab and see blind zones.

sec16-card-sec16-F017.question_text: Which two outreach channels does Share the Road use to promote safer highway habits?
sec16-card-sec16-F017.teaching_text: Combining news media segments with hands-on community safety events spreads no-zone awareness to new drivers.

sec16-card-sec16-F018.question_text: Which three partner groups team up with the Share the Road safety campaign?
sec16-card-sec16-F018.teaching_text: State trucking associations, highway-safety groups, and the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration back the outreach.

sec04-card-sec04-F001.question_text: What two obligations does every driver have toward roadway traffic signs and signals?
sec04-card-sec04-F001.teaching_text: Safe traffic flow collapses unless every motorist both recognizes roadway controls early and obeys their directions.

sec04-card-sec04-F002.question_text: How are U.S. road signs shifting away from text-only panels, and how are unfamiliar symbols introduced?
sec04-card-sec04-F002.teaching_text: Gradually replacing text-heavy panels with international pictures speeds comprehension, while companion plaques explain newer symbols.

sec04-card-sec04-F003.question_text: What core driver requirement does red communicate on a traffic-control device in the Mississippi manual?
sec04-card-sec04-F003.teaching_text: Seeing red on an intersection control tells your right foot to prepare for a required stop.

sec04-card-sec04-F004.question_text: Which two meanings does the color green convey on roadway controls and highway signs?
sec04-card-sec04-F004.teaching_text: Green both points highway travelers along routes and signals permitted lane or intersection movements.

sec04-card-sec04-F005.question_text: Which standard roadway message category uses the color yellow?
sec04-card-sec04-F005.teaching_text: Yellow catches peripheral vision ahead of curves, merges, or intersections requiring slower, more attentive driving.

sec04-card-sec04-F006.question_text: What do blue highway signs guide motorists toward?
sec04-card-sec04-F006.teaching_text: Scanning blue panels along interstates helps travelers locate fuel, food, rest stops, and medical care safely.

sec04-card-sec04-F007.question_text: Which sign category uses black lettering or symbols on a white background?
sec04-card-sec04-F007.teaching_text: High-contrast black on white announces enforceable speed, lane, and turn laws rather than optional tips.

sec04-card-sec04-F008.question_text: What roadside activity is announced by orange warning signs?
sec04-card-sec04-F008.teaching_text: Bright orange stands out against trees and asphalt so road crews and equipment never catch drivers fast.

sec04-card-sec04-F009.question_text: Which two kinds of public destinations are marked by brown guide signs?
sec04-card-sec04-F009.teaching_text: Brown separates state parks, campgrounds, and scenic overlooks from everyday green route or blue service signs.

sec04-card-sec04-F010.question_text: Which single traffic sign is reserved for the eight-sided octagon shape?
sec04-card-sec04-F010.teaching_text: No other roadway panel uses eight sides, letting drivers recognize a stop control even from behind.

sec04-card-sec04-F011.question_text: What type of highway sign commonly uses a wide horizontal rectangle?
sec04-card-sec04-F011.teaching_text: Wide horizontal panels fit town names, exit numbers, and directional arrows cleanly overhead or beside highways.

sec04-card-sec04-F012.question_text: Which specific right-of-way sign owns the equilateral triangle shape?
sec04-card-sec04-F012.teaching_text: Pointing downward with three equal sides makes a yield control unmistakable even in heavy rain or glare.

sec04-card-sec04-F013.question_text: What zone ahead is announced by a pennant-shaped warning sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F013.teaching_text: Spotting the tapered pennant outline stops impatient drivers from pulling out to pass right before sightlines vanish.

sec04-card-sec04-F014.question_text: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign alert drivers about?
sec04-card-sec04-F014.teaching_text: Tilted four-sided diamonds flag curves, intersections, slick pavement, or crossings on or near the roadway.

sec04-card-sec04-F015.question_text: What kind of rules appear on vertical rectangular signs, and what is a classic example?
sec04-card-sec04-F015.teaching_text: Notice the orientation split on tests because horizontal rectangles guide routes while vertical rectangles post enforceable regulations.

sec04-card-sec04-F016.question_text: Which two child-safety areas are marked by a five-sided pentagon sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F016.teaching_text: Five sides shaped like a classic schoolhouse roof alert drivers to slow down where students walk.

sec04-card-sec04-F017.question_text: What specific crossing ahead is announced by a round warning sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F017.teaching_text: Circular advance warnings give you distance to silence cabin noise and scan tracks before reaching the rails.

sec04-card-sec04-F018.question_text: What two obligations apply at every stop sign before you pull into an intersection?
sec04-card-sec04-F018.teaching_text: Coming to a dead stop is only half the rule because any cross vehicle close enough for danger goes first.

sec04-card-sec04-F019.question_text: How can a Do Not Enter sign display its ban, and what does it forbid?
sec04-card-sec04-F019.teaching_text: Whether printed in letters or shown as a horizontal white bar across a red circle, entering is illegal.

sec04-card-sec04-F020.question_text: What urgent danger does a Wrong Way sign warn you is happening right now?
sec04-card-sec04-F020.teaching_text: Seeing Wrong Way means your tires are already rolling against oncoming traffic with immediate head-on crash danger.

sec04-card-sec04-F021.question_text: What must you do right away after spotting a Wrong Way sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F021.teaching_text: Getting off live lanes onto the shoulder immediately and turning around safely prevents a high-speed collision.

sec04-card-sec04-F022.question_text: What intersection maneuver is outlawed by a No Left Turn sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F022.teaching_text: Turning left past a prohibition symbol cuts across protected pedestrian phases or one-way cross streets.

sec04-card-sec04-F023.question_text: What intersection maneuver is outlawed by a No Right Turn sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F023.teaching_text: Right-turn bans often guard wrong-way one-way streets, bus lanes, or tight pedestrian corners.

sec04-card-sec04-F024.question_text: Which three roadway spots are covered by a no-turnaround or No U-Turn prohibition?
sec04-card-sec04-F024.teaching_text: Flipping around across an intersection, mid-street centerline, or divided median where banned surprises fast oncoming traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F025.question_text: What vehicle restriction does a No Trucks regulatory sign enforce?
sec04-card-sec04-F025.teaching_text: Low bridges, weak pavement, or residential noise rules exclude commercial trucks where No Trucks panels stand.

sec04-card-sec04-F026.question_text: Under what three conditions is turning right on a red light allowed in Mississippi?
sec04-card-sec04-F026.teaching_text: Rolling a red right turn earns tickets because you must stop completely, verify clear lanes, and check signs.

sec04-card-sec04-F027.question_text: When must you hold behind the line for a green light instead of turning right on red?
sec04-card-sec04-F027.teaching_text: Blind corners and heavy crosswalks post No Turn on Red panels requiring patience until green appears.

sec04-card-sec04-F028.question_text: Who holds priority when you approach a yield sign at a merge or intersection?
sec04-card-sec04-F028.teaching_text: Entering traffic adjusts pace or halts so motorists already established on the main road never have to brake.

sec04-card-sec04-F029.question_text: What do Keep Left and Keep Right regulatory signs tell a driver approaching an obstacle or island?
sec04-card-sec04-F029.teaching_text: Passing on the wrong side of a median nose drops your car straight into opposing turn pockets.

sec04-card-sec04-F030.question_text: What choice does a driver have in a lane governed by a mandatory left-turn sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F030.teaching_text: Mandatory turn signs lock your lane into turning left and forbid continuing straight or switching late.

sec04-card-sec04-F031.question_text: What movement is required when a mandatory right-turn sign controls your lane?
sec04-card-sec04-F031.teaching_text: Going straight out of a mandatory right-turn lane sideswipes adjacent through lanes expecting you to turn.

sec04-card-sec04-F032.question_text: What travel rule does a one-direction arrow sign establish?
sec04-card-sec04-F032.teaching_text: Every lane on a one-way street flows with the arrow, making reverse-direction turns an instant head-on hazard.

sec04-card-sec04-F033.question_text: Which vehicles are legally allowed to park in reserved accessible parking spaces?
sec04-card-sec04-F033.teaching_text: Parking in an accessible stall without displaying an authorized license plate or temporary hangtag blocks mobility access.

sec04-card-sec04-F034.question_text: Which local Mississippi office provides information on getting an accessible-parking tag?
sec04-card-sec04-F034.teaching_text: Exam questions check local civic offices, and Mississippi handles accessible-parking tags through the County Tax Collector's Office.

sec04-card-sec04-F035.question_text: Under what road conditions does a posted speed-limit sign represent the top legal speed?
sec04-card-sec04-F035.teaching_text: Rain, fog, or heavy traffic lowers safe speed well below the ideal-weather number printed on the post.

sec04-card-sec04-F036.question_text: What is permitted inside a center turn-only lane, and which two uses are banned?
sec04-card-sec04-F036.teaching_text: Using a center left-turn strip as a travel or passing lane sets up head-on wrecks with opposing turners.

sec04-card-sec04-F037.question_text: What driver maneuver does a regulatory no-passing sign forbid?
sec04-card-sec04-F037.teaching_text: Blind hills, curves, or bridges hide oncoming traffic, so stepping out of lane to overtake is prohibited.

sec04-card-sec04-F038.question_text: Which three upcoming intersection controls can yellow advance warning signs announce?
sec04-card-sec04-F038.teaching_text: Hills and curves can hide red lights or stop signs until advance yellow diamonds warn you to slow.

sec04-card-sec04-F039.question_text: How does a crossroad warning diamond differ from a T-intersection warning diamond?
sec04-card-sec04-F039.teaching_text: A four-way cross symbol warns of intersecting traffic, whereas a T symbol warns that a joining road terminates.

sec04-card-sec04-F040.question_text: Which way should you prepare to merge when a warning announces that the right lane ends?
sec04-card-sec04-F040.teaching_text: Signaling and checking your left mirror early beats getting pinched against the right shoulder taper.

sec04-card-sec04-F041.question_text: Which way should you prepare to merge when a warning announces that the left lane ends?
sec04-card-sec04-F041.teaching_text: Watch the mirror direction on tests because a disappearing left lane requires blending smoothly to the right.

sec04-card-sec04-F042.question_text: What roadway feature do side-road warning signs identify ahead?
sec04-card-sec04-F042.teaching_text: Vehicles pulling out from ninety-degree or angled side roads can enter your lane with tight sightlines.

sec04-card-sec04-F043.question_text: What traffic movement does a merging-ramp warning sign alert mainline drivers to expect?
sec04-card-sec04-F043.teaching_text: Creating a courteous gap or shifting over helps ramp vehicles match highway pace without braking duels.

sec04-card-sec04-F044.question_text: How does a new-lane or added-lane warning sign differ from a standard merge sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F044.teaching_text: Instead of squeezing two streams into one lane, the entering ramp continues forward as its own fresh lane.

sec04-card-sec04-F045.question_text: What hazard ahead does a railroad-crossing warning alert a driver to?
sec04-card-sec04-F045.teaching_text: Spotting the advance rail warning gives you room to ease off the gas and listen for horns.

sec04-card-sec04-F046.question_text: What traffic pattern does a two-way-traffic warning sign tell you is operating?
sec04-card-sec04-F046.teaching_text: Leaving a one-way street or divided highway puts oncoming headlights right across the center stripe again.

sec04-card-sec04-F047.question_text: What road change ahead is announced by a divided-highway warning sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F047.teaching_text: A median island or barrier splits opposing directions ahead, requiring you to steer right of the divider.

sec04-card-sec04-F048.question_text: What change ahead does a divided-highway-ends warning sign announce?
sec04-card-sec04-F048.teaching_text: Once the center median stops, only painted stripes separate your lane from oncoming highway vehicles.

sec04-card-sec04-F049.question_text: What intersection layout ahead is announced by a traffic-circle warning sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F049.teaching_text: Slowing early before a roundabout lets you spot circulating vehicles and yield cleanly at entry.

sec04-card-sec04-F050.question_text: Which three horizontal alignment changes can curve-family warning signs announce ahead?
sec04-card-sec04-F050.teaching_text: Reading whether the arrow bends ninety degrees, sweeps once, or snakes repeatedly sets your entry speed before turning.

sec04-card-sec04-F051.question_text: What pavement risk does a Slippery When Wet warning sign highlight?
sec04-card-sec04-F051.teaching_text: Rainwater lifts tires on smooth asphalt or bridges, requiring slower speed and gentle steering inputs.

sec04-card-sec04-F052.question_text: Why can a school-crossing warning sign appear several blocks away from the school building itself?
sec04-card-sec04-F052.teaching_text: Students funnel across busy collector streets blocks from campus, so never assume school crossings sit only beside buildings.

sec04-card-sec04-F053.question_text: What speed limit does the Mississippi manual set when passing a school during recess or arrival and dismissal?
sec04-card-sec04-F053.teaching_text: Dropping to fifteen miles per hour when students arrive, leave, or play at recess gives life-saving stopping margin.

sec04-card-sec04-F054.question_text: How do painted stripes affect pedestrian right-of-way at Mississippi intersections?
sec04-card-sec04-F054.teaching_text: Lack of white paint never erases intersection crosswalk rights, so drivers yield at marked and unmarked corners alike.
sec04-card-sec04-F054.must_match_memory_hook: Pedestrians hold priority painted or not

visual_sync.text_span: Pedestrians hold priority painted or not

sec04-card-sec04-F055.question_text: What must drivers do if they remain in a lane marked by a mandatory-exit sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F055.teaching_text: Staying in an exit-only lane commits your car to leaving the highway unless you merge out safely beforehand.

sec04-card-sec04-F056.question_text: What dangerous intersection setup is flagged by a plaque warning that cross traffic does not stop?
sec04-card-sec04-F056.teaching_text: Assuming every corner has a stop sign causes T-bone crashes when cross lanes keep full nonstop priority.

sec04-card-sec04-F057.question_text: Which three highway networks are distinguished by numbered route marker shapes?
sec04-card-sec04-F057.teaching_text: Distinctive shield outlines let you tell interstate freeways, United States routes, and Mississippi state highways apart instantly.

sec04-card-sec04-F058.question_text: What two navigation facts do destination, direction, and distance signs give highway drivers?
sec04-card-sec04-F058.teaching_text: Knowing both which city lies ahead and how many miles remain helps you plan fuel and rest stops.

sec04-card-sec04-F059.question_text: What specific spot does an interstate exit guide sign mark for motorists?
sec04-card-sec04-F059.teaching_text: Exit guide panels pinpoint the ramp departure point so exiting traffic clears high-speed through lanes cleanly.

sec04-card-sec04-F060.question_text: What background color, symbol color, and two common shapes identify work-zone signs?
sec04-card-sec04-F060.teaching_text: Black text or icons on orange diamonds and rectangles signal temporary road-work zones from blocks away.

sec04-card-sec04-F061.question_text: Which five specific conditions can orange work-zone warnings alert you to ahead?
sec04-card-sec04-F061.teaching_text: Work-zone panels flag exposed workers, reduced limits, detours, slow construction rigs, and abrupt pavement drop-offs.

sec04-card-sec04-F062.question_text: What three driving adjustments protect you and crews inside a work zone?
sec04-card-sec04-F062.teaching_text: Rear-end collisions lead work-zone crashes, so slow down, expect sudden braking, and stretch your following cushion.

sec04-card-sec04-F063.question_text: Which three traffic commands from a work-zone flagger are you legally required to obey?
sec04-card-sec04-F063.teaching_text: Flaggers coordinate single-lane alternating chutes and heavy dump trucks, making their go, slow, and stop signals mandatory.

sec04-card-sec04-F064.question_text: What two jobs do orange drums, cones, and vertical panels perform around road work?
sec04-card-sec04-F064.teaching_text: Channelizing barrels and cones both guide tires past hazards and seal off closed or torn-up pavement.

sec04-card-sec04-F065.question_text: Where must you stop when a temporary traffic signal controls a work zone?
sec04-card-sec04-F065.teaching_text: Stopping well behind the white line gives oversized construction trucks turning room through narrow one-lane zones.

sec04-card-sec04-F066.question_text: What colors and shape form the slow-moving-vehicle emblem, and which vehicles mount it on back?
sec04-card-sec04-F066.teaching_text: Spotting the bright orange-and-red rear triangle warns you immediately of farm equipment or animal-drawn wagons ahead.

sec04-card-sec04-F067.question_text: When and on what type of roads should you stay especially alert for slow-moving vehicles?
sec04-card-sec04-F067.teaching_text: Tractors and wagons use country highways after sunset as well as daytime, closing highway gaps shockingly fast.

sec04-card-sec04-F068.question_text: What must you confirm before pulling out to overtake a slow-moving vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F068.teaching_text: Wide implements, hills, and hidden driveways demand verifying legal, clear sight distance before easing around.

sec04-card-sec04-F069.question_text: Which two movements by farm machinery should you watch for on rural state highways?
sec04-card-sec04-F069.teaching_text: Combines and tractors may roll slowly down your lane or cross straight from one field gate to another.

sec04-card-sec04-F070.question_text: Why must you pass farm machinery with extra caution even on a straight rural stretch?
sec04-card-sec04-F070.teaching_text: Diesel tractor roar and enclosed cabs drown out approaching cars, so never assume the farmer knows you are passing.

sec04-card-sec04-F071.question_text: How do roadway rights and traffic duties apply to horse riders and animal-drawn vehicles?
sec04-card-sec04-F071.teaching_text: Horseback riders and buggies share full roadway-use rights and follow the exact same traffic laws as motorists.

sec04-card-sec04-F072.question_text: Which two loud car actions must you avoid when passing horses or animal-drawn vehicles?
sec04-card-sec04-F072.teaching_text: Blasting a horn or revving an exhaust can panic a horse into bolting across your hood.

sec04-card-sec04-F073.question_text: What turning move should you anticipate before overtaking an animal-drawn vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F073.teaching_text: Wagons lack electric turn blinkers and may swing left toward farm lanes right as an impatient driver passes.

sec04-card-sec04-F074.question_text: How do rural highways alert drivers ahead of time where horses and buggies travel often?
sec04-card-sec04-F074.teaching_text: Yellow horse-and-buggy diamonds cue you to lift off the throttle before cresting blind rural hills.

sec02-card-sec02-F001.question_text: Which two separate braking systems must every Mississippi motor vehicle carry?
sec02-card-sec02-F001.teaching_text: Having an independent parking brake backs up your hydraulic foot pedal and holds parked wheels on hills.

sec02-card-sec02-F002.question_text: Within how many feet must your foot brake stop the vehicle from twenty miles per hour?
sec02-card-sec02-F002.teaching_text: Taking longer than thirty feet from twenty miles per hour signals worn pads or weak hydraulic pressure.

sec02-card-sec02-F003.question_text: Within how many feet must the parking brake be able to stop a vehicle from twenty miles per hour?
sec02-card-sec02-F003.teaching_text: DMV distractors mix up thirty and fifty-five feet, so pair foot brakes with thirty and parking brakes with fifty-five.

sec02-card-sec02-F004.question_text: From at least what distance must a vehicle's horn be audible on Mississippi roads?
sec02-card-sec02-F004.teaching_text: A working horn heard two hundred feet out warns distracted drivers or walkers before lanes collide.

sec02-card-sec02-F005.question_text: Which three noise-making warning devices are prohibited on regular vehicles in Mississippi?
sec02-card-sec02-F005.teaching_text: Sirens, exhaust whistles, and spark whistles impersonate emergency responders and startle nearby traffic illegally.

sec02-card-sec02-F006.question_text: How many headlights and how many rear lights must a passenger vehicle have?
sec02-card-sec02-F006.teaching_text: Driving with one dead headlight makes an approaching car look like a motorcycle in the dark.

sec02-card-sec02-F007.question_text: How far ahead does the manual recommend headlights reveal a person on a clear night?
sec02-card-sec02-F007.teaching_text: Cloudy lenses or weak bulbs cut visibility short of the five-hundred-foot cushion needed at highway speeds.

sec02-card-sec02-F008.question_text: What color must a vehicle's rear light shine, and from what distance behind must it show?
sec02-card-sec02-F008.teaching_text: Bright red rear lamps visible five hundred feet back prevent high-speed rear-end crashes on unlit highways.

sec02-card-sec02-F009.question_text: Besides standard headlights, what is the maximum number of spotlights and auxiliary lights allowed?
sec02-card-sec02-F009.teaching_text: Capping extra lamps at one spotlight and three auxiliary units prevents blinding oncoming drivers with light bars.

sec02-card-sec02-F010.question_text: Which two colors are illegal on spotlights and auxiliary vehicle lights?
sec02-card-sec02-F010.teaching_text: Red and blue forward-facing lights belong to police and emergency crews, never civilian spotlights or fog lamps.

sec02-card-sec02-F011.question_text: Not counting the headlights, how many extra lights at most should shine at the same time?
sec02-card-sec02-F011.teaching_text: Switching on more than four non-headlight lamps at once overwhelms oncoming drivers' night-adapted eyes.

sec02-card-sec02-F012.question_text: Why must your vehicle's muffler stay in working order at all times?
sec02-card-sec02-F012.teaching_text: Rusted-out or gutted mufflers blast illegal exhaust noise and foul visibility with bothersome tailpipe smoke.

sec02-card-sec02-F013.question_text: What rule governs muffler cutouts, bypasses, or similar exhaust-routing switches?
sec02-card-sec02-F013.teaching_text: Installing a valve or pipe that routes exhaust around the muffler violates Mississippi equipment law.

sec02-card-sec02-F014.question_text: How does the Mississippi manual treat an interior rearview mirror between recommendation and general mandate?
sec02-card-sec02-F014.teaching_text: Watch that classic exam nuance because the manual recommends a rearview mirror while noting no general mandate.

sec02-card-sec02-F015.question_text: When is a truck legally required to carry a side mirror in Mississippi?
sec02-card-sec02-F015.teaching_text: Box beds, campers, and tall cargo walls blind the cab window, making a side mirror mandatory.

sec02-card-sec02-F016.question_text: What equipment standard applies to a vehicle's windshield wipers?
sec02-card-sec02-F016.teaching_text: Sudden Gulf Coast downpours turn smeared, torn wiper blades into instant highway blindness.

sec02-card-sec02-F017.question_text: What inflation and surface standards must your tires meet to stay roadworthy?
sec02-card-sec02-F017.teaching_text: Underinflated rubber or tread with cuts, breaks, and dry rot risks high-speed blowouts and hydroplaning.

sec02-card-sec02-F018.question_text: What fender-height gap from suspension, frame, or chassis modifications makes a passenger vehicle illegal on Mississippi roads?
sec02-card-sec02-F018.teaching_text: Tilting the nose four inches or more above the tail aims headlights skyward and hides pedestrians ahead.

sec02-card-sec02-F019.question_text: How is vertical fender height measured under Mississippi's vehicle-modification law?
sec02-card-sec02-F019.teaching_text: Officers measure straight up from the pavement through the wheel's centerline to the bottom fender lip.

sec02-card-sec02-F020.question_text: How does the manual define a vehicle fender and its practical job?
sec02-card-sec02-F020.teaching_text: Curved body panels over each tire keep mud, gravel, and rainwater from spraying windshields around you.

sec02-card-sec02-F021.question_text: When does the Mississippi manual classify a modified vehicle as squatted?
sec02-card-sec02-F021.teaching_text: Raising front fenders at least four inches past rear fenders makes the rig look sagged onto back tires.

sec02-card-sec02-F022.question_text: What tool should you use to verify tire inflation before heading out?
sec02-card-sec02-F022.teaching_text: Eyeballing radial sidewalls misses dangerous ten-pound air drops that a simple pocket pressure gauge catches fast.

sec02-card-sec02-F023.question_text: Which two places on or in your vehicle list the recommended tire inflation pressure?
sec02-card-sec02-F023.teaching_text: Sidewall numbers list maximum burst rating, whereas the driver door jamb and owner's manual give target pressure.

sec02-card-sec02-F024.question_text: How often should you inspect your tires for wear and damage?
sec02-card-sec02-F024.teaching_text: Checking tread wear once a month and before highway road trips catches nails and bald spots early.

sec02-card-sec02-F025.question_text: What three driving tasks depend directly on maintaining clear vision?
sec02-card-sec02-F025.teaching_text: Sharp sight lets you read traffic conditions, catch developing trouble early, and brake or steer promptly.

sec02-card-sec02-F026.question_text: When must you wear your eyeglasses or contacts if corrective lenses are required for driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F026.teaching_text: Skipping required glasses even on familiar neighborhood blocks blurs hazards and violates your license restriction.

sec02-card-sec02-F027.question_text: Which kind of corrective lenses should drivers avoid wearing at night?
sec02-card-sec02-F027.teaching_text: Dark or tinted prescription glasses cut scarce nighttime contrast and hide unlit pedestrians along dark shoulders.

sec02-card-sec02-F028.question_text: Which four triggers does the manual link to physical or mental driver fatigue?
sec02-card-sec02-F028.teaching_text: Mental or physical exhaustion sneaks up not just from late nights, but from illness, strain, and monotonous work.

sec02-card-sec02-F029.question_text: Which two driving abilities suffer under fatigue, and what rule follows?
sec02-card-sec02-F029.teaching_text: Drowsiness dulls your eyesight and stretches reaction times like impairment, so stay off the road when tired.

sec02-card-sec02-F030.question_text: How many hours of sleep does the manual say most people need for daytime alertness?
sec02-card-sec02-F030.teaching_text: Running on four hours of sleep leaves microsleeps waiting to ambush you on quiet afternoon stretches.

sec02-card-sec02-F031.question_text: How often should you schedule rest stops by distance or time during a long drive?
sec02-card-sec02-F031.teaching_text: Stepping out around every hundred miles or two hours resets blood flow and breaks highway hypnosis.

sec02-card-sec02-F032.question_text: How can bringing a passenger along help lower fatigue risk on a long trip?
sec02-card-sec02-F032.teaching_text: An awake travel companion spots early yawning or lane drift and can share turns behind the wheel.

sec02-card-sec02-F033.question_text: What should you inspect on prescription or over-the-counter medicine before driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F033.teaching_text: Cold, allergy, and pain tablets routinely pack sedating ingredients that slow steering reflexes without feeling illegal.

sec02-card-sec02-F034.question_text: What is the manual's rule on driving after consuming alcohol or other drugs?
sec02-card-sec02-F034.teaching_text: Alcohol and mind-altering drugs wreck judgment, vision, and braking timing long before a driver feels drunk.

sec02-card-sec02-F035.question_text: What credential habit must you verify before pulling out, and what if an officer asks for it?
sec02-card-sec02-F035.teaching_text: Mississippi law requires both carrying your license before setting out and handing it over when requested.

sec02-card-sec02-F036.question_text: How should you position the driver's seat before putting the vehicle in motion?
sec02-card-sec02-F036.teaching_text: Adjusting seat distance while parked prevents lunging for the brake pedal or sliding mid-turn in traffic.

sec02-card-sec02-F037.question_text: When should you fasten your seat belt for a drive?
sec02-card-sec02-F037.teaching_text: Fumbling with a shoulder strap while rolling out of a driveway splits eyes and hands off traffic.

sec02-card-sec02-F038.question_text: When and why must you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
sec02-card-sec02-F038.teaching_text: Aiming interior and side glass while parked lets you monitor lanes behind without twisting away from traffic.

sec02-card-sec02-F039.question_text: Where on the steering wheel does the Mississippi manual place your hands for control?
sec02-card-sec02-F039.teaching_text: Holding opposite outside edges at three and nine o'clock maximizes balanced steering leverage and airbag clearance.

sec02-card-sec02-F040.question_text: Why does the manual warn against using the older two-and-ten steering hand position?
sec02-card-sec02-F040.teaching_text: High hands at ten and two sit across an inflating steering-hub airbag, risking arm and facial injuries.

sec02-card-sec02-F041.question_text: How should your fingers and thumbs rest on the steering wheel?
sec02-card-sec02-F041.teaching_text: Resting thumbs along the wheel face instead of hooking tight prevents sprains if a pothole jerks steering.

sec02-card-sec02-F042.question_text: Which part of the steering wheel must you never grip from the inside to turn?
sec02-card-sec02-F042.teaching_text: Reaching inside the wheel spokes traps wrists against airbags or spinning spokes during an emergency swerve.

sec02-card-sec02-F043.question_text: Where does the manual call for slower speed and extra caution because children may appear suddenly?
sec02-card-sec02-F043.teaching_text: Kids chasing balls or riding bikes dart between bumpers without looking near schools, parks, and home streets.

sec02-card-sec02-F044.question_text: What dangerous assumption must you avoid making when sharing lanes near a bicyclist?
sec02-card-sec02-F044.teaching_text: Expecting every bike rider to signal smoothly or hold a straight line ignores untrained or wobbly riders.

sec02-card-sec02-F045.question_text: What sudden hazard should you scan parked cars along your lane for?
sec02-card-sec02-F045.teaching_text: Spotting brake lights or heads inside parked cars warns you before a door swings into your fender.

sec02-card-sec02-F046.question_text: Why should you scan side driveways and bumpers for clues that another car is entering traffic?
sec02-card-sec02-F046.teaching_text: Turned front wheels or exhaust puffs give early notice before someone pulls out or brakes right ahead.

sec02-card-sec02-F047.question_text: What should you do whenever possible if a reckless driver bears down near you?
sec02-card-sec02-F047.teaching_text: Blocking or racing an erratic driver escalates danger, whereas yielding space lets the hazard pass harmlessly.

sec02-card-sec02-F048.question_text: Every how many miles should you take a break during long-distance highway driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F048.teaching_text: Stretching your legs every hundred miles refreshes concentration before highway monotony dulls your lane awareness.

sec02-card-sec02-F049.question_text: Why should you avoid trailing the same vehicle or cluster of cars for a long stretch?
sec02-card-sec02-F049.teaching_text: Locking onto one bumper ahead lulls your brain into autopilot, slowing your brake response when trouble hits.

sec02-card-sec02-F050.question_text: Which two in-car habits keep your mind sharp during long-distance driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F050.teaching_text: Warm air and a fixed stare invite highway drowsiness, while cool air and active eye movement sustain alertness.

sec02-card-sec02-F051.question_text: Which three parts of your attention or body can a driving distraction pull off the road?
sec02-card-sec02-F051.teaching_text: Visual, manual, and cognitive distractions steal critical reaction distance at highway speeds, especially when combined.

sec02-card-sec02-F052.question_text: Which two mobile-phone activities does the manual advise every driver to avoid behind the wheel?
sec02-card-sec02-F052.teaching_text: Even quick calls split mental focus, while texting stacks visual, manual, and cognitive distraction together.

sec02-card-sec02-F053.question_text: If an urgent phone call cannot wait while driving, what equipment does the manual recommend?
sec02-card-sec02-F053.teaching_text: Hands-free audio keeps both hands on the wheel at three and nine instead of cradling a phone.

sec02-card-sec02-F054.question_text: Which three actions involving a text message are prohibited while driving in Mississippi?
sec02-card-sec02-F054.teaching_text: Glancing down just to read an incoming text is every bit as illegal as typing or hitting send.

sec02-card-sec02-F055.question_text: What social-networking actions are illegal on a hand-held mobile phone while driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F055.teaching_text: Scrolling timelines or posting updates on a hand-held phone behind the wheel violates Mississippi distracted-driving law.

sec02-card-sec02-F056.question_text: How does Mississippi's phone law define a hand-held mobile phone, and what devices are excluded?
sec02-card-sec02-F056.teaching_text: Any portable communicator operated with at least one hand for calls or texts counts, excluding voice-operated gear.

sec02-card-sec02-F057.question_text: How does the distracted-driving phone law define a covered motor vehicle?
sec02-card-sec02-F057.teaching_text: The texting statute covers mechanically driven or drawn vehicles built mainly for travel on public highways.

sec02-card-sec02-F058.question_text: Which three user features define a social-networking service under the Mississippi phone statute?
sec02-card-sec02-F058.teaching_text: Any service where users build profiles, list connections, and message contacts falls under the hand-held ban.

sec02-card-sec02-F059.question_text: Which digital messages count as texts under the phone ban, and which alerts or functions are exempt?
sec02-card-sec02-F059.teaching_text: Instant messages and emails are banned texts, whereas weather, traffic, emergency alerts, and vehicle navigation stay exempt.

sec02-card-sec02-F060.question_text: What minimal hand touch is still permitted on a voice-operated or hands-free device?
sec02-card-sec02-F060.teaching_text: Hands-free interaction bars typing with either hand apart from a quick tap to start, stop, or activate voice.

sec02-card-sec02-F061.question_text: How do the phone-use definitions translate writing, sending, and reading a text message?
sec02-card-sec02-F061.teaching_text: Defining those three verbs around manual entry, transmission, and retrieval separates banned thumb typing from voice tools.

sec02-card-sec02-F062.question_text: What should you do when anger, grief, fear, illness, worry, or an argument wrecks your focus?
sec02-card-sec02-F062.teaching_text: Intense emotions tunnel your vision and trigger aggressive mistakes, so hand the keys to a calm driver.

sec02-card-sec02-F063.question_text: What kind of talk with passengers should you avoid while operating a vehicle?
sec02-card-sec02-F063.teaching_text: Heated passenger arguments hijack mental bandwidth away from brake lights, lane merges, and intersection timing.

sec02-card-sec02-F064.question_text: What does the Mississippi manual advise regarding eating behind the wheel?
sec02-card-sec02-F064.teaching_text: Unwrapping burgers or catching spilled drinks pulls a hand off steering right when traffic stops short.

sec02-card-sec02-F065.question_text: What must a driver verify before moving whenever children ride in the vehicle?
sec02-card-sec02-F065.teaching_text: Properly buckled child seats protect young passengers in crashes and stop kids from climbing around the cabin.

sec02-card-sec02-F066.question_text: How does the manual say pets should travel inside a moving vehicle?
sec02-card-sec02-F066.teaching_text: Unrestrained dogs or cats can crawl under brake pedals or become dangerous projectiles during hard stops.

sec02-card-sec02-F067.question_text: Why must you skip stereo headphones and keep cabin music at a reasonable volume?
sec02-card-sec02-F067.teaching_text: Earbuds or booming speakers drown out ambulance sirens, train horns, and screeching tires around your car.

sec02-card-sec02-F068.question_text: What items must you keep off your vehicle's windshield?
sec02-card-sec02-F068.teaching_text: Decals and parking placards plastered across windshield glass create blind spots big enough to hide pedestrians.

sec02-card-sec02-F069.question_text: Which four window coverings or treatments are banned on Mississippi vehicle windows?
sec02-card-sec02-F069.teaching_text: Signs, posters, decals, and reflective mirror-finish window film block sightlines and blind surrounding motorists.

sec02-card-sec02-F070.question_text: What does the manual advise about hanging air fresheners, tassels, or charms from the rearview mirror?
sec02-card-sec02-F070.teaching_text: Swinging mirror ornaments catch your eye constantly and block the center sightline toward crosswalks and cars.

sec02-card-sec02-F071.question_text: Why should you clear loose bags, phones, or bottles off the front seat before driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F071.teaching_text: Grabbing for a falling laptop or coffee cup during hard braking yanks your eyes and hand off steering.
